title: Responsibility Boundaries for EC2 and RDS
prompt: A company is migrating a database on EC2 to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. An auditor is reviewing responsibility for patching the underlying infrastructure and managing database user permissions. Which pair of responsibilities applies after the migration?

choices.text: AWS manages the underlying operating system and database user permissions.
choices.explanation: Even with a managed service, data access management is not transferred to AWS.

choices.text: The customer manages both.
choices.explanation: This confuses self-management on EC2 with the responsibilities under RDS.

choices.text: The customer maintains the underlying operating system, and AWS assigns database user permissions.
choices.explanation: The responsibilities are reversed.

choices.text: AWS maintains the underlying operating system, and the customer assigns database user permissions.
choices.explanation: RDS manages the underlying operating system; the customer decides which permissions to grant to users they create.

learning.reason: RDS manages the underlying operating system, while the customer decides which permissions to grant to users they create.
learning.concept: Operational responsibilities vary by service. Delegating management of the underlying platform does not transfer responsibility for controlling access to data.

title: Team-Specific Budget Alerts
prompt: Two development teams share one AWS account, and cost allocation tags are enabled. You want to email only the team responsible when its monthly budget reaches 80%, without stopping any resources. What should you configure?

choices.text: Save a monthly Cost Explorer report grouped by tag.
choices.explanation: You can inspect the breakdown, but a saved report does not send conditional email notifications.

choices.text: Configure dynamic anomaly detection with Cost Anomaly Detection.
choices.explanation: A deviation from historical usage patterns does not correspond to 80% of a monthly budget.

choices.text: Create a separate AWS Budget for each team, filtered by its cost allocation tag, and configure an actual-spend threshold and notification recipient.
choices.explanation: You can specify the tag scope, budget percentage, and recipient separately for each team.

choices.text: Create an organization-wide AWS Budget and register both teams as notification recipients.
choices.explanation: This does not separate thresholds and recipients by team.

learning.reason: The tag scope, budget percentage, and recipients can be specified separately.
learning.concept: Budget notifications, anomaly detection, and cost analysis serve different purposes. A budget alert alone does not forcibly stop spending.

title: Continuing to Serve Traffic During an AZ Failure
prompt: A stateless web application runs in one AWS Region. You want it to keep processing requests if one group of data centers goes down, without requiring an operator to change DNS. Which architecture should you choose?

choices.text: Register EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones with an Application Load Balancer that spans multiple Availability Zones.
choices.explanation: The instances are placed across separate failure-isolation boundaries, and health checks can exclude unhealthy targets.

choices.text: Run EC2 instances in two subnets in the same Availability Zone and register them with an ALB.
choices.explanation: Separating subnets does not protect against a failure affecting their shared Availability Zone.

choices.text: Run an instance in one Availability Zone and back it up so it can be restored in another Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: The application cannot continue processing while it is being restored.

choices.text: Increase the maximum capacity of an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances in one Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: Adding capacity does not replace distribution across Availability Zones.

learning.reason: Instances in different failure-isolation boundaries can be served through the load balancer, which can exclude unhealthy targets using health checks.
learning.concept: Load balancing, distributing across Availability Zones, and recovery from backups address different availability requirements.

title: Distributing Change Events
prompt: A final-approval event must be delivered at the same time to verified email addresses in multiple departments and to one SQS queue. The sending application must not manage the recipient list and must publish the event with a single API call.

choices.text: Subscribe email and SQS endpoints to an Amazon SNS FIFO topic.
choices.explanation: FIFO topics do not support direct email subscriptions.

choices.text: Set email addresses directly as targets of an Amazon EventBridge rule.
choices.explanation: Email delivery requires a supported target such as SNS.

choices.text: Share one standard SQS queue as the email subscription destination.
choices.explanation: SQS does not support email subscriptions, and consumers of the same queue do not each receive every event.

choices.text: Subscribe email and SQS endpoints to an Amazon SNS standard topic.
choices.explanation: One publication can be distributed to subscribers that use different protocols.

learning.reason: One publication can be distributed to subscribers that use different protocols.
learning.concept: Use SNS to deliver to destinations and SQS as a durable buffer from which processing can be picked up later.

choices.text: IAM credential report

choices.text: AWS Config resource configuration history

choices.text: AWS CloudTrail DeleteRole management event
choices.explanation: It can show the API operation name, time, and caller, including the session.

choices.text: AWS Health event history
choices.explanation: It covers service events and notifications, not an audit record of a user deleting an IAM role.

prompt: Images arrive in S3 in batches a few times a month. For each file, start a few seconds of metadata extraction while avoiding long-running processes and the operations of a compute platform. Which approach is the most direct?

choices.text: Use a long-running Fargate service to poll S3 periodically
choices.explanation: It reduces OS management, but still requires maintaining long-running tasks and polling.

choices.text: Process S3 Inventory output with Lambda once a day
choices.explanation: This can support a batch inventory, but it does not trigger processing as each object arrives.

choices.text: Keep an EC2 Spot Instance running to monitor S3
choices.explanation: It may reduce instance costs, but you still operate the compute platform and handle interruptions.

choices.text: Use S3 object creation notifications to invoke a Lambda function
choices.explanation: Code can run for each object creation event without a server waiting for work.

learning.reason: Code can run for each object creation event without a server waiting for work.

choices.text: A one-year Compute Savings Plan

choices.text: AWS Support manages the public-access settings, and the customer manages the physical media.

choices.text: AWS protects the physical media, and the customer manages the bucket’s public-access settings and permissions.

choices.text: AWS handles both media protection and public-access settings.

choices.text: Obtain a pricing table from AWS Artifact.

choices.text: Analyze recent AWS bills with Cost Explorer.
choices.explanation: There is no usage history to analyze, and the goal is to estimate specified new configurations.

choices.text: Enter the planned usage in AWS Pricing Calculator to create an estimate.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Find AWS Services Whose Costs Increased Over the Past Three Months
prompt: The finance team wants to understand why the overall monthly AWS bill has increased. Billing history is available. The team wants to aggregate costs by month for the past three months and compare on screen which AWS services contributed to the increase. It does not need notifications or configuration estimates. Which tool should it use?

choices.text: AWS Pricing Calculator
choices.explanation: It estimates costs from the planned usage of a proposed configuration. It does not import an account’s historical usage and chart it.

choices.text: AWS Cost Explorer
choices.explanation: It can aggregate costs or usage for a time period and compare them by dimensions such as service.

choices.text: AWS Budgets
choices.explanation: It monitors a budget amount or usage. Its primary purpose is not comparing service-level changes over the past three months.

choices.text: AWS Billing payment methods
choices.explanation: It manages payment methods; it does not analyze costs by service.

source.label: AWS Cost Management — Cost Explorerによる利用実績の分析

learning.reason: In Cost Explorer, set the time range to the past three months and view costs by month and service. This lets the team examine changes in actual usage and the cost breakdown.
learning.concept: The tools differ depending on whether the goal is to analyze existing usage or estimate an environment that is not yet running.

sourceLabel: AWS Cost Management — Analyzing Usage with Cost Explorer

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Keep a Usage Commitment Discount After Migrating a Workload
prompt: A team runs a predictable amount of compute on EC2 and plans to move some of it to Fargate and Lambda. It can commit to a fixed amount of usage for one year and wants the same discount model to apply to eligible compute usage after the migration. Which option should it choose?

choices.text: EC2 Instance Savings Plans
choices.explanation: These apply to eligible EC2 families and do not extend the same plan’s coverage to Fargate and Lambda usage.

choices.text: EC2 Capacity Reservations
choices.explanation: These reserve EC2 launch capacity under specific conditions; they are not a pricing discount covering Fargate or Lambda.

choices.text: Compute Savings Plans
choices.explanation: These use a spend commitment and can discount usage across multiple eligible compute services.

choices.text: Database Savings Plans
choices.explanation: These cover eligible database service usage, not compute plans spanning the specified EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage.

source.label: AWS Savings Plans — 適用対象とプランの種類

learning.reason: Compute Savings Plans can apply to eligible EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage. The team can change which compute services it uses under the same commitment.
learning.concept: Savings Plans are usage-based pricing discounts that require a commitment; they do not reserve the physical capacity needed to launch instances.

sourceLabel: AWS Savings Plans — Coverage and Plan Types

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Find resources to review with AWS recommendations
prompt: The management team wants to use AWS recommendation checks available under its support plan. The cost breakdown is already understood; this time, the team wants to find resources AWS checks, such as unused resources, for review. Which feature should they open?

choices.text: Cost Explorer daily billing chart
choices.explanation: This is useful for understanding cost trends, but it does not perform the usage recommendation checks requested here.

choices.text: AWS Budgets notification list
choices.explanation: This shows budget notifications, but it does not check for candidate resources that may be unnecessary.

choices.text: AWS Pricing Calculator estimate
choices.explanation: This estimates the cost of a planned configuration; it does not inspect the use of existing resources.

choices.text: AWS Trusted Advisor cost optimization checks
choices.explanation: Depending on the resources covered, these checks identify unused resources and other opportunities to review.

source.label: AWS Support — Trusted Advisorの推奨チェック

learning.reason: AWS Trusted Advisor cost optimization checks provide recommendations for covered resources. They can reveal actions to consider that are not apparent from the cost amounts in a report alone.
learning.concept: The services covered and checks available vary by support plan and other factors. A recommendation and making an actual change are separate actions.

sourceLabel: AWS Support — Trusted Advisor recommendation checks

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Use existing department tags to categorize billing reports
prompt: Multiple departments use tag-compatible EC2 resources in the same account. Each resource already has a Department tag, but the tag is not available in the cost aggregation view. Which action is required to aggregate future usage by department?

choices.text: Enable Department as a user-defined cost allocation tag in Billing and Cost Management.
choices.explanation: This makes the department tag already applied to resources available for cost aggregation.

choices.text: Set access restrictions based on Department in an IAM permissions policy.
choices.explanation: Department can be used as an authorization condition, but that does not make the tag available in billing reports.

choices.text: Change all EC2 names to department names and filter by department name in the payment method.
choices.explanation: Changing names or payment settings does not enable existing tags as an aggregation dimension.

choices.text: Change only the account's monthly budget threshold.
choices.explanation: This changes the budget threshold, but does not enable the tag for categorizing billing data.

source.label: AWS Billing — ユーザー定義のコスト配分タグ

learning.reason: Enable the Department tag as a cost allocation tag in Billing and Cost Management so its values can be used to aggregate costs.
learning.concept: Applying a tag to a resource and enabling that tag for billing data categorization are separate steps. It can take time for an enabled tag to appear in the view.

sourceLabel: AWS Billing — User-defined cost allocation tags

category: クラウドの概念
title: A cloud characteristic that adjusts capacity to demand
prompt: An ordering site sees heavy usage during the day and very little usage at night. The team increases capacity to handle requests during busy periods, then removes the excess capacity when usage declines. Which cloud characteristic does this design use?

choices.text: High availability
choices.explanation: This is the ability to remain available during failures; it does not mean increasing and decreasing capacity to match day and night usage.

choices.text: Elasticity
choices.explanation: This allows capacity to increase when needed and decrease when it is no longer needed in response to changing usage.

choices.text: Data residency
choices.explanation: This is a requirement to restrict data storage or processing to a specific geographic area.

choices.text: Capacity reservation in advance
choices.explanation: This is used to secure capacity needed at startup. It is not the concept of automatically reducing capacity in use when demand declines.

source.label: AWS概要 — クラウドコンピューティングの利点

learning.reason: The design uses elasticity to increase or decrease allocated capacity in response to demand.
learning.concept: Scalability is the ability to handle increased demand. Elasticity focuses on increasing or decreasing allocated capacity as actual demand changes.

sourceLabel: AWS Overview — Benefits of cloud computing

category: クラウドの概念
title: Avoiding upfront purchases when service usage is uncertain
prompt: The number of users for a new business is not yet predictable. With on-premises infrastructure, servers had to be purchased in advance to handle peak demand. In the cloud, the business can avoid a long-term contract and pay for the compute resources it uses. Which financial benefit does this change provide?

choices.text: The monthly bill stays constant regardless of usage.
choices.explanation: With usage-based payment, monthly charges can vary with the amount used.

choices.text: The business gains more assets that it can own long term and depreciate.
choices.explanation: The business does not own the cloud infrastructure it uses; it pays for its usage.

choices.text: The business can avoid a large upfront infrastructure investment and pay variable costs based on usage.
choices.explanation: The business does not need to buy enough capacity for maximum demand before it knows how the service will grow.

choices.text: The business must sign a fixed contract for capacity equal to its maximum demand.
choices.explanation: Pay-as-you-go usage does not itself require a fixed contract based on maximum demand.

source.label: AWS概要 — 固定費から変動費への転換

learning.reason: The business can shift from fixed upfront costs for purchasing equipment to variable costs based on the capacity or time it uses.
learning.concept: With variable costs, spending is tied to usage. Monitoring limits and stopping unneeded resources still require operational management.

sourceLabel: AWS Overview — Moving from fixed costs to variable costs

category: クラウドの概念
title: Right-size an overprovisioned resource for a steady workload
prompt: A business server continuously performs the same workload. Measurements over several weeks show substantial CPU and memory headroom even during peak periods, and a smaller configuration still meets the response-time target. Before entering into a long-term commitment, the team reviews its resource selection. Which practice does this describe?

choices.text: Rightsizing
choices.explanation: Adjust the resource size based on current utilization and response-time targets to reduce waste.

choices.text: Purchasing a reservation discount
choices.explanation: This can lower the cost of eligible usage, but it does not reduce the CPU or memory capacity of the current configuration.

choices.text: Deploying redundantly
choices.explanation: This prepares the system to continue operating during a failure; it addresses a different goal from sizing an oversized standalone server.

choices.text: Bringing a license
choices.explanation: This changes the software licensing arrangement. It is not a way to size resources based on measured hardware requirements.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected — リソースのライトサイジング

learning.reason: This is rightsizing: adjusting overallocated compute resources to an appropriate size based on measurements and requirements.
learning.concept: Buying a discount is different from changing the amount of resources needed. Reassess capacity using representative peaks as well.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Move the database for the same application to a managed service
prompt: A company is moving its self-managed MySQL database to AWS. It plans to retain the existing application and database engine largely as they are, and to migrate to Amazon RDS for MySQL to reduce the work involved in patching and backups. The overall business application will not be redesigned. Which migration strategy does this describe?

choices.text: Retain
choices.explanation: This means leaving the application in its current environment; it does not describe moving the database to AWS.

choices.text: Rehost
choices.explanation: This is closer to moving the self-managed database to a similar environment, such as EC2, and continuing to operate it.

choices.text: Refactor
choices.explanation: This involves making more substantial changes to the application's design or architecture, which the scenario does not require.

choices.text: Replatform
choices.explanation: This moves the database to a managed service and improves some operational aspects without rebuilding the application as a whole.

source.label: AWS Prescriptive Guidance — クラウド移行戦略

learning.reason: The database is being moved to a managed platform with limited changes to gain operational benefits in the cloud, so this is replatforming.
learning.concept: Rehosting generally means moving an application largely as is. Replatforming changes the platform as needed during migration.

sourceLabel: AWS Prescriptive Guidance — Cloud migration strategies

category: クラウドの概念
title: Plan migration waves for interdependent systems
prompt: An order-processing application has a strong dependency on a legacy database it reads from, and the business cannot stop operating during the migration. Different departments prefer different dates, so the migration will take place in several waves. What is the most effective preparation before deciding which systems to move in each wave?

choices.text: Migrate servers in name order and investigate dependencies afterward.
choices.explanation: Name order does not reflect runtime relationships between applications, so a dependency might become temporarily unreachable.

choices.text: Map application and database dependencies, then assess which systems to move together and how to maintain connectivity during migration.
choices.explanation: This provides information for designing the migration sequence and planning how to preserve required connections across wave boundaries.

choices.text: Select all servers with low utilization to migrate first, without checking the network traffic of their applications.
choices.explanation: Grouping by instance count or size alone does not prevent a dependency from being moved before the applications that rely on it.

choices.text: Treat all systems as independent and finalize the dates requested by each department as is.
choices.explanation: Meeting the preferred business dates does not ensure that required application-to-application communication will be maintained during migration.

source.label: AWS Prescriptive Guidance — 移行ウェーブの計画

learning.reason: Understand application dependencies and communication requirements, then plan which systems to move together and any temporary connections needed to avoid disrupting connectivity during migration.
learning.concept: Migration waves are not simply groupings by server count. Their boundaries should account for dependencies, business criticality, and readiness.

sourceLabel: AWS Prescriptive Guidance — Planning migration waves

category: クラウドの概念
title: Use existing software licenses that can be brought to AWS
prompt: A team already holds licenses for business software. Its agreement permits bringing them to AWS, and the team can meet the required hardware and licensing conditions. It wants to continue using these paid-up entitlements after migrating to AWS. Which option should it choose?

choices.text: BYOL
choices.explanation: Existing licenses can be used when they meet the conditions for bringing them to AWS.

choices.text: Use a new license-included instance
choices.explanation: AWS provides the license under this model, so it does not meet the requirement to use the team's existing entitlements.

choices.text: Configure consolidated billing with AWS Organizations
choices.explanation: This consolidates account billing but does not change software licensing terms.

choices.text: Purchase a capacity reservation
choices.explanation: Reserving capacity to launch servers is separate from obtaining software usage rights.

source.label: AWS License Manager — ライセンス込みとBYOL

learning.reason: Choose Bring Your Own License (BYOL) to bring eligible existing licenses for use on AWS.
learning.concept: For BYOL, verify the existing rights and licensing conditions. With a license-included option, the cost of an AWS-provided license is included in the usage charges.

sourceLabel: AWS License Manager — License-included and BYOL

category: クラウドの概念
title: Choose a Region based on both data location and required services
prompt: A company policy requires the data in scope to be stored in an approved AWS Region in Japan, and the application requires a specified AWS service. The company also wants to improve the experience for users overseas. When initially choosing a Region, which two items should be checked to narrow down the candidates?

choices.text: Compare the maximum IAM password lengths in each candidate Region.
choices.explanation: This does not determine where the required service can be deployed or where the data can be stored.

choices.text: Check only whether CloudFront edge locations are near the users.
choices.explanation: Edge locations are not a substitute for a Region where the application’s data can be stored.

choices.text: Check whether each candidate Region meets the company’s data-location requirements.
choices.explanation: This is a required condition for narrowing down the locations where the in-scope data can be stored.

choices.text: Assume that the same services are available in every Region and choose only the least expensive location.
choices.explanation: Service availability and fit with the requirements must be checked.

choices.text: Check whether the required service is available in each candidate Region.
choices.explanation: A Region without the required service cannot meet the stated requirements.

source.label: AWSクラウド基盤 — リージョンの選定

learning.reason: Check that the candidate Region meets the company’s data-location requirements and offers the required services.
learning.concept: Geographic proximity, measured network performance, and cost can also affect Region selection. Here, narrow the candidates using the two explicitly stated mandatory requirements.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Metric for how far back data must be recoverable
prompt: If an internal system fails, staff require that data be retained up to a point no more than 15 minutes before the failure. The application’s allowable time to resume is set separately at 2 hours. Which metric represents the 15-minute requirement?

choices.text: RTO
choices.explanation: This indicates how quickly the service should be restored. In this question, it corresponds to 2 hours.

choices.text: SLA
choices.explanation: This is an agreement on service conditions, not the term for specifying the acceptable age of recoverable data in time.

choices.text: RPO
choices.explanation: This is the target for how far back data must be recoverable from before a failure.

choices.text: Mean recovery time
choices.explanation: This is the average time taken for past recoveries, not a target for the point in time to which data must be recoverable.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected — 障害復旧目標

learning.reason: RPO expresses the acceptable data loss in time. RTO, the allowable time to resume, is defined separately.
learning.concept: The recoverable data point and the time when service resumes are independent design targets. They help evaluate backup intervals and recovery procedures.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Reduce environmental impact while retaining required data
prompt: A service retains temporary files and business records that must be kept long term. The temporary files are no longer needed after a few days and are not used in investigations. Which approach reduces the storage resources needed for the workload while meeting the retention requirements for business records?

choices.text: Replicate all data, including temporary files, to another Region permanently.
choices.explanation: This adds copies that do not need protection and conflicts with the goal of reducing storage resources.

choices.text: Separate data by retention requirement and use a lifecycle policy to delete temporary files after their expiration date.
choices.explanation: This preserves the required records while reducing data that no longer needs to be stored.

choices.text: Keep everything in the same storage class regardless of its lifespan.
choices.explanation: Temporary files remain after they are no longer needed, so unnecessary resource use is not reduced.

choices.text: Delete temporary files and business records after the same short retention period.
choices.explanation: This would delete business records that must be kept and fail to meet the retention requirements.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected — 不要なデータの削除

learning.reason: Classify the required records separately from temporary data with a limited lifetime, then automatically delete only the temporary data when it is no longer needed.
learning.concept: Sustainable design avoids using resources to retain or replicate data that is no longer needed, while honoring business value and retention obligations.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Verify that recovery from backups works in practice
prompt: Automated backups of a business database succeed every day. An administrator wants to confirm that the data and application can actually be recovered after a failure and that recovery can meet the business resumption target. What is the most direct way to obtain this evidence without affecting production?

choices.text: Increase the number of backups and confirm that every job succeeds.
choices.explanation: This can provide more available recovery points, but it does not measure whether restored data can be used or how long recovery takes.

choices.text: Extend the backup retention period and increase the frequency of success notifications.
choices.explanation: Keeping recovery points longer does not show whether they can be restored or whether recovery can meet the resumption target.

choices.text: Calculate the recent production database’s availability and use it in place of the time needed to recover from a failure.
choices.explanation: Availability during normal operation does not measure whether recovery from a backup will succeed.

choices.text: Restore backups regularly in an isolated environment and check the restored contents, application behavior, and recovery time.
choices.explanation: This measures whether the data and recovery procedure meet the target without switching production over.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected — バックアップからの定期的な復元検証

learning.reason: Restore from backups in an isolated environment and verify that the data is readable, the application works, and the recovery time is acceptable.
learning.concept: A successful backup job and demonstrated recoverability are different things. Repeat restore tests to validate the recovery procedure and targets.

sourceLabel: AWS Well-Architected — Periodic restore testing from backups

category: クラウドの概念
title: Shortening the time to start testing new ideas
prompt: In the past, ordering equipment for testing a new product idea took several weeks. With the cloud, a small team can quickly provision the environment it needs and try another idea based on the results. Which benefit describes shortening the time from planning to experimentation, rather than scaling traffic up or down in the same environment?

choices.text: Increased agility
choices.explanation: The team can test new ideas with little preparation time and iterate quickly.

choices.text: Elasticity
choices.explanation: This means increasing or decreasing capacity in response to actual demand. The time measured here is from preparing the environment to running the test.

choices.text: Capacity reservation
choices.explanation: This is a way to secure capacity that meets specific conditions; it is not the general name for the benefit of starting hypothesis testing quickly.

choices.text: Fault isolation
choices.explanation: This is the principle of limiting the impact of a failure on other components, which is separate from shortening the time from planning to experimentation.

source.label: AWS概要 — クラウドによるアジリティの向上

learning.reason: The scenario describes increased agility: resources can be provisioned quickly, allowing the team to move faster from experimentation to a decision.
learning.concept: Agility focuses on the speed of launching or changing something. Elasticity focuses on increasing or decreasing allocated capacity to match traffic volume.

sourceLabel: AWS Overview — Increased agility through cloud computing

category: クラウドの概念
title: Validating value through a small production pilot before scaling across the organization
prompt: A company is progressing through a cloud migration in line with the AWS CAF. Executives have set objectives, and the relevant teams have assessed the capabilities they need and their readiness. Next, the company plans to run a small pilot in production, confirm its value from user feedback, and then expand it. Which phase of the transformation does this plan represent?

choices.text: Envision
choices.explanation: This phase defines the desired business outcomes and envisions the value of the cloud. The scenario says this work is already complete.

choices.text: Align
choices.explanation: This phase identifies capability gaps and assesses organizational readiness to align stakeholders.

choices.text: Launch
choices.explanation: This phase runs a small production pilot to validate business value.

choices.text: Scale
choices.explanation: This phase extends the results of a validated pilot to a broader scope. It follows the pilot described here.

source.label: AWS CAF — クラウド変革の各段階

learning.reason: Running a small production pilot and validating its value are activities in the Launch phase.
learning.concept: Envision focuses on desired outcomes, Align on capabilities and readiness, Launch on validation through a pilot, and Scale on expanding proven value.

sourceLabel: AWS CAF — Phases of cloud transformation

category: クラウドの概念
title: The pillar that addresses operational improvement
prompt: Production changes sometimes disrupt operations. The operations team breaks changes into small units, prepares a rollback procedure, and reviews incidents to improve its operating procedures. Which Well-Architected pillar primarily addresses these practices?

choices.text: Performance efficiency
choices.explanation: This pillar focuses on resource efficiency.

choices.text: Cost optimization
choices.explanation: This pillar focuses on managing spending.

choices.text: Operational excellence
choices.explanation: Correct. This pillar addresses operations, automation, and continual improvement.

choices.text: Sustainability
choices.explanation: This pillar focuses on environmental impact.

learning.reason: Making small, reversible changes and improving procedures based on operational experience are practices addressed by the Operational Excellence pillar.
learning.concept: Performance efficiency concerns selecting and using resources to meet demand. Cost optimization concerns designing to obtain the needed value while managing costs.

category: クラウドの概念
title: The perspective for developing cloud talent
prompt: An organization is beginning a phased migration to the cloud. Its technology is nearly ready, but employees do not understand their new roles, and the organization needs to plan training and collaboration. Which AWS CAF perspective primarily addresses this?

choices.text: Platform
choices.explanation: This perspective addresses building the cloud platform.

choices.text: People
choices.explanation: Correct. This perspective addresses organizational capabilities, roles, skills, and engagement in transformation.

choices.text: Security
choices.explanation: This perspective addresses security controls.

choices.text: Governance
choices.explanation: This perspective addresses investment value and risk governance.

learning.reason: Successful adoption requires people capabilities as well as technology.
learning.concept: The CAF addresses organizational transformation from multiple perspectives.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Economies of scale in the cloud
prompt: Many customers use as much of a cloud provider’s infrastructure as they need. Because the provider can aggregate customer demand, it can often lower the cost per unit compared with an individual company operating similar infrastructure on its own. What is this effect called?

choices.text: Fixed capital expenditure
choices.explanation: This is an initial investment in equipment, not an economy of scale in the cloud.

choices.text: Vertical scaling
choices.explanation: This means increasing the capacity of a single resource.

choices.text: Lift and shift
choices.explanation: This is a migration approach.

choices.text: Economies of scale
choices.explanation: Correct. Aggregating usage at a large scale can lower the cost per unit.

source.label: AWS: Six Advantages of Cloud Computing

learning.reason: A cloud provider’s large-scale usage can lead to lower costs per unit.
learning.concept: Economies of scale are one of the economic advantages of adopting cloud computing.

sourceLabel: AWS: Six Advantages of Cloud Computing

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Manage encryption keys and permissions to use them
prompt: You store data subject to an audit. In the encryption settings of the applicable AWS service, you want to select a company-managed encryption key and control which principals can use that key to encrypt and decrypt data. In which service should you create the key?

choices.text: AWS Secrets Manager
choices.explanation: It stores secrets such as passwords and tokens. KMS manages the key itself that AWS services use for encryption at rest.

choices.text: AWS Key Management Service
choices.explanation: It lets you create and manage encryption keys and control access to them.

choices.text: AWS Certificate Manager
choices.explanation: It primarily issues and manages TLS certificates. It does not manage the KMS keys specified for encryption at rest in AWS services.

choices.text: AWS Artifact
choices.explanation: It provides access to audit reports and similar documents; it does not create encryption keys.

source.label: AWS KMS — 暗号化キーとアクセス制御

learning.reason: Create a customer managed key in AWS KMS and use it for encryption in the target service. You can control permissions to use the key.
learning.concept: Managing keys used for encryption is different from storing database passwords or issuing TLS certificates.

sourceLabel: AWS KMS — Encryption keys and access control

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Rotate database passwords without embedding them in an application
prompt: A business application uses a database password. You want only the application that needs the value at runtime to be able to retrieve it, and you want to rotate the password periodically for a supported database. The password must not be included in the application’s source code or image. Which service should you use?

choices.text: AWS CloudTrail
choices.explanation: It records AWS activity. It is not a store for passwords retrieved by an application or a password rotation service.

choices.text: Use AWS KMS alone.
choices.explanation: It can manage encryption keys, but it does not meet the requirement to store and retrieve a database password and rotate it periodically.

choices.text: Embed the password in an Amazon ECR image.
choices.explanation: This does not separate the application from the secret, and every password change would also require updating the image.

choices.text: AWS Secrets Manager
choices.explanation: It lets you control who can retrieve credentials and configure automatic rotation for passwords of supported databases.

source.label: AWS Secrets Manager — シークレットの保管とローテーション

learning.reason: Store the credentials in Secrets Manager, limit retrieval permissions, and configure a supported rotation.
learning.concept: Encrypting a password with KMS alone does not update both the database password and the value retrieved by the application as part of the same rotation process.

sourceLabel: AWS Secrets Manager — Secret storage and rotation

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Allow only the actions and resources needed for the task
prompt: An application that aggregates billing data only needs to read existing objects under a specific S3 prefix. It does not need to upload or delete objects, or read other prefixes. Which IAM permissions best follow the principle of least privilege?

choices.text: Allow read access to all S3 buckets and objects in the same AWS account.
choices.explanation: This limits access to read operations, but also allows reading outside the target prefix.

choices.text: Allow read, write, and delete access to objects under the target prefix.
choices.explanation: The scope is limited, but it includes write and delete operations that the aggregation task does not need.

choices.text: Allow only GetObject for objects under the target prefix.
choices.explanation: This limits both the actions and the resources to what is needed.

choices.text: Allow all S3 actions and use CloudTrail to find out which actions were used.
choices.explanation: Auditing is possible, but unnecessary permissions have not been removed in advance.

source.label: AWS IAM — 最小権限の原則

learning.reason: Allow only the required actions on objects under the specified prefix in the target bucket.
learning.concept: Least privilege means limiting not only the services but also the actions and resources to what is needed.

sourceLabel: AWS IAM — Principle of least privilege

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Provide an EC2 application with temporary credentials for AWS APIs
prompt: An application running on EC2 records processing results in an approved DynamoDB table. It must receive the permissions needed for AWS API calls without distributing long-term access keys in application or server configuration files. Which method should be used?

choices.text: Associate an IAM role that allows only the required DynamoDB operations with EC2 through an instance profile.
choices.explanation: The application can obtain the role's temporary credentials and call AWS APIs.

choices.text: Include an IAM user's long-term access keys in a shared image.
choices.explanation: The keys would remain in the distributed image, which does not meet the requirement to use short-term role credentials.

choices.text: Only allow outbound traffic from the EC2 security group to DynamoDB.
choices.explanation: Allowing a network path does not authenticate the caller or grant permission to use AWS APIs.

choices.text: Obtain the AWS account root user's keys and share them across the instances.
choices.explanation: This would share long-term credentials with permissions far beyond what the application needs.

source.label: Amazon EC2 — インスタンス向けのIAMロール

learning.reason: Attach an IAM role with the required permissions to EC2 through an instance profile. The application can use temporary credentials.
learning.concept: Give AWS workloads roles and temporary credentials. There is no need to share employees' login credentials or long-term keys.

sourceLabel: Amazon EC2 — IAM roles for EC2 instances

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Control traffic per EC2 instance and allow response traffic
prompt: An administrator wants to configure inbound rules per EC2 instance for approved source addresses and ports. They want a control that automatically allows responses to permitted connections without requiring additional rules in the reverse direction. Which control is appropriate?

choices.text: A network ACL
choices.explanation: It controls traffic at the subnet level and is stateless, so rules are also needed for the return direction.

choices.text: A security group
choices.explanation: It controls instance traffic and can automatically handle responses to permitted traffic.

choices.text: An IAM identity-based policy
choices.explanation: It authorizes actions such as AWS API calls. It does not allow network packets based on source addresses or ports.

choices.text: A VPC route table
choices.explanation: It selects a path to a destination. It does not provide the requested traffic-permission rules or state tracking.

source.label: Amazon VPC — セキュリティグループ

learning.reason: Apply a security group to the EC2 network interface. Because it is stateful, response traffic for permitted connections is also allowed.
learning.concept: Network ACLs are evaluated statelessly at the subnet level, while security groups are applied at the resource level.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Encrypt data in transit and after it is stored
prompt: A customer is developing a web service that lets users upload documents. The contents must be encrypted both while they are in transit between the browser and the service and after the service stores the files. Choose two controls that directly meet these requirements.

choices.text: Require HTTPS for users' upload traffic.
choices.explanation: TLS protects data in transit.

choices.text: Use multi-factor authentication at the upload destination.
choices.explanation: This strengthens authentication but does not configure encryption for documents in transit or at rest.

choices.text: Enable audit logs for operations.
choices.explanation: This tracks who performed which operations and when; it does not encrypt the documents.

choices.text: Use the storage service's encryption at rest for stored files.
choices.explanation: This directly meets the requirement to encrypt data after it is stored.

choices.text: Use storage versioning.
choices.explanation: This retains previous versions; it does not encrypt stored files.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected — 転送中の暗号化と保存時の暗号化

learning.reason: Use HTTPS/TLS for traffic and enable encryption at rest at the storage destination.
learning.concept: Data in transit and data in storage need protection in different places. Choose appropriate encryption for each and manage access permissions separately.

sourceLabel: AWS Well-Architected — Encryption in transit and encryption at rest

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Identify tasks that require root user authentication in a standalone AWS account
prompt: You operate a standalone AWS account that is not part of AWS Organizations. Administrators with appropriate permissions handle routine operations. Which operation requires authentication as the root user?

choices.text: Create an S3 bucket for backups.
choices.explanation: This is routine resource management that an IAM user or role with the required permissions can perform.

choices.text: Create a CloudWatch alarm.
choices.explanation: A principal granted the required permissions in IAM can perform this action.

choices.text: Update the account's technical contact to a new owner.
choices.explanation: This is a routine alternate-contact update, not an authentication operation restricted to the root user.

choices.text: Update the primary email address of the standalone account's root user.
choices.explanation: In a standalone account, root authentication is required to change this account setting.

source.label: AWS IAM — ルートユーザー認証が必要なアカウント操作

learning.reason: Changing the primary email address of the root user of a standalone account requires root authentication.
learning.concept: The account email address is distinct from general contact information and alternate contacts. Use an administrator with the necessary permissions for routine tasks.

sourceLabel: AWS IAM — Account operations that require root user authentication

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Set an organization-wide permissions boundary for development accounts
prompt: AWS Organizations groups the development member accounts into a single OU. The administrators of those accounts must not be able to use prohibited AWS services even if they add IAM permissions to their own identities. At the same time, existing policies on each member account should continue to grant ordinary permissions. Which mechanism should you use?

choices.text: Apply an SCP to the development OU.
choices.explanation: An SCP sets the maximum permissions available to principals in the member accounts, above their individual permissions.

choices.text: Add only read-only IAM policies for all developers.
choices.explanation: This does not centrally set a maximum on actions already allowed by other policies.

choices.text: Record usage outcomes with AWS Config.
choices.explanation: This can help detect policy violations, but it does not block use of the service when a request is made.

choices.text: Configure service-specific notifications with AWS Budgets.
choices.explanation: AWS Budgets can notify you about costs after usage, but it does not set an authorization boundary for member account API actions.

source.label: AWS Organizations — サービスコントロールポリシー

learning.reason: Apply a service control policy to the development OU to set the maximum permissions available to principals in its member accounts.
learning.concept: Actions within the scope allowed by an SCP still require an appropriate individual permission to be performed. An SCP does not grant permissions.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Use a maintenance shell without opening an inbound SSH port
prompt: You need to maintain an EC2 instance that is a Systems Manager managed node. Operators must connect interactively with IAM authorization, but you do not want an inbound SSH port or an SSH bastion on the instance. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Connect directly to the Amazon EC2 public IP address over SSH.
choices.explanation: This requires accepting SSH connections and does not meet the requirement to keep the inbound port closed.

choices.text: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager
choices.explanation: It provides maintenance sessions without an SSH inbound port or bastion, while access is controlled with IAM.

choices.text: AWS CloudTrail event history
choices.explanation: It records AWS API events; it is not an interactive feature for running commands on the operating system.

choices.text: Configure only AWS Client VPN.
choices.explanation: This provides network connectivity and, by itself, does not provide an IAM-authorized shell on an EC2 instance.

learning.reason: With Session Manager, operators authorized by IAM can open a shell session on the managed node without opening an inbound SSH port.
learning.concept: The managed node needs an agent and connectivity to Systems Manager. Configure audit logging separately if required.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Multi-factor authentication for AWS accounts
prompt: A team uses passwords to sign in to the AWS Management Console as IAM users. In addition to a password, the team wants to require verification using a device or authenticator the user possesses. Which measure should they choose?

choices.text: Increase the minimum password length.
choices.explanation: This can make passwords harder to guess, but it does not add an authentication factor separate from the password.

choices.text: Require MFA at sign-in.
choices.explanation: In addition to the password, this verifies another factor, such as a registered authenticator.

choices.text: Shorten the console session duration.
choices.explanation: This controls how long the console can be used after authentication; it does not verify an additional factor at sign-in.

choices.text: Record sign-in activity with CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: This can support auditing and detection, but it does not require another authentication factor at sign-in.

learning.reason: MFA protects sign-ins without relying solely on a password.
learning.concept: Enable MFA especially for privileged accounts, and use individual credentials.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Obtain AWS compliance documents
prompt: An auditor wants to obtain official reports about the regulations and certifications supported by AWS services and use them in the organization's compliance assessment. Which AWS service is most appropriate?

choices.text: Amazon GuardDuty
choices.explanation: GuardDuty is a threat detection service, not a service for distributing AWS audit reports.

choices.text: AWS Config
choices.explanation: Config records and evaluates AWS resource configurations; it does not provide AWS certification reports.

choices.text: AWS Artifact
choices.explanation: AWS Artifact provides self-service access to AWS compliance reports and contractual documents.

choices.text: Amazon Inspector
choices.explanation: Inspector is a vulnerability management service for workloads.

learning.reason: Artifact is the place to obtain AWS compliance-related documents.
learning.concept: Evidence of AWS compliance and audits of your own resource configurations serve different purposes.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Ongoing Assessment of AWS Resource Configurations
prompt: A company wants to continuously record and assess whether AWS resource configurations, such as encryption settings on S3 buckets, comply with its internal policies. Which service is the best fit?

choices.text: AWS CloudTrail
choices.explanation: CloudTrail records API activity history; continuously assessing configuration compliance is not its primary purpose.

choices.text: AWS Artifact
choices.explanation: Artifact provides AWS compliance documents; it does not assess the company's resource configurations.

choices.text: Amazon Inspector
choices.explanation: Inspector focuses on vulnerability management; it is not a general service for tracking configuration history and evaluating rules.

choices.text: AWS Config
choices.explanation: AWS Config records resource configurations and can assess compliance using rules.

learning.reason: Config provides change history for AWS resource configurations and evaluates compliance.
learning.concept: Distinguish CloudTrail's operational auditing from Config's configuration compliance assessment.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Choosing Services for Threat Detection and Vulnerability Management
prompt: The security team has two goals: continuously detect suspicious activity in AWS accounts and check EC2 software packages for known vulnerabilities. Which two services meet these goals?

choices.text: Amazon GuardDuty
choices.explanation: It detects potential threats and anomalies using account and workload data.

choices.text: AWS Artifact
choices.explanation: It provides audit reports and other AWS documents; it does not inspect packages on the company's EC2 instances.

choices.text: AWS CloudTrail
choices.explanation: It records API activity. The records alone do not replace the two analysis services requested here.

choices.text: Amazon Inspector
choices.explanation: It detects vulnerabilities in software packages and other supported resources on eligible EC2 instances.

choices.text: AWS Shield
choices.explanation: It protects against DDoS attacks; it does not continuously assess OS package vulnerabilities.

learning.reason: Use GuardDuty to detect suspicious activity and Inspector to check software vulnerabilities on eligible EC2 instances.
learning.concept: Threat detection finds attacks or anomalies, while vulnerability assessment finds weaknesses that are present.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Centralizing Employee Access Across Multiple AWS Accounts
prompt: A company wants to use its existing IdP to centrally manage employee sign-ins to multiple AWS accounts and the assignment of permission sets. Which service is the best fit?

choices.text: Create separate IAM users in each account.
choices.explanation: Managing users separately does not meet the requirement to centrally manage existing identities across multiple accounts.

choices.text: AWS IAM Identity Center
choices.explanation: It can use an existing identity provider and assign permission sets for multiple accounts to employees and groups.

choices.text: Amazon Cognito user pools
choices.explanation: They authenticate users accessing applications; they do not assign account-specific permission sets to employees for AWS access.

choices.text: Use only consolidated billing in AWS Organizations.
choices.explanation: Billing is consolidated, but that alone does not configure employee sign-in or permission assignments.

learning.reason: IAM Identity Center centralizes workforce access across multiple accounts.
learning.concept: Distinguish human access management from IAM roles used by workloads.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Finding Sensitive Data in Documents Stored in S3
prompt: A team stores transaction documents in S3. In addition to checking public access settings, it wants an AWS managed service to detect whether file contents contain personally identifiable information. Which service should it use?

choices.text: AWS Config
choices.explanation: It assesses AWS resource configurations and compliance, but it does not search file contents in S3 for personal information.

choices.text: Amazon GuardDuty
choices.explanation: It detects suspicious activity and threats; it is not intended to classify personal information in file contents.

choices.text: Amazon Macie
choices.explanation: It inspects S3 object contents and identifies supported sensitive data.

choices.text: AWS CloudTrail
choices.explanation: It can audit API activity in services such as S3, but it does not classify the contents of stored files.

source.label: Amazon Macie — S3の機密データの検出

learning.reason: Amazon Macie's sensitive data discovery analyzes supported objects in S3 and detects personally identifiable information and other sensitive data.
learning.concept: Changing access controls or recording API activity serves a different purpose from examining stored file contents for sensitive data.

sourceLabel: Amazon Macie — Discovering Sensitive Data in S3

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Centralize findings from multiple security services
prompt: A security team wants to review and prioritize findings from multiple AWS security services in one place. Which service is the best fit?

choices.text: AWS Config
choices.explanation: Config records and evaluates resource configurations and compliance status.

choices.text: AWS Artifact
choices.explanation: Artifact provides AWS compliance documents.

choices.text: AWS Budgets
choices.explanation: Budgets is used to notify you about cost and usage budgets.

choices.text: AWS Security Hub
choices.explanation: Security Hub aggregates findings from multiple AWS security services and helps provide a view of security posture.

learning.reason: Security Hub is a central service for aggregating security findings.
learning.concept: Understand the difference between individual services that detect findings and the role of aggregating and prioritizing them.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Choose DDoS protection and web request controls
prompt: A company wants to protect its AWS applications from large-scale DDoS attacks. At the same time, it wants to distinguish this goal from fine-grained controls for SQL injection and per-IP request rates. Which service is primarily intended for DDoS protection?

choices.text: AWS WAF
choices.explanation: AWS WAF focuses on controls implemented through Web ACL rules for HTTP requests.

choices.text: Amazon GuardDuty
choices.explanation: GuardDuty detects potential threats.

choices.text: AWS Shield
choices.explanation: AWS Shield protects AWS applications from DDoS attacks.

choices.text: AWS Config
choices.explanation: Config records and evaluates resource configurations.

learning.reason: Shield provides DDoS protection, while WAF controls HTTP requests through Web ACLs.
learning.concept: Choose between DDoS protection and application-layer defenses based on the type of threat.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Choose a managed database that uses SQL and relational tables
prompt: A new order-processing application needs to relate customer and order tables, run SQL aggregations, and update individual orders. The team uses PostgreSQL and wants a managed service to handle server maintenance and backups. Which service is the best fit?

choices.text: Amazon DynamoDB
choices.explanation: This is a NoSQL database typically accessed by key. It does not fit the requirement to use PostgreSQL connections and joins across tables as-is.

choices.text: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
choices.explanation: This is a managed relational database that lets you use the specified engine.

choices.text: Amazon ElastiCache
choices.explanation: This is a high-speed in-memory data store, not a service for continuing to use an existing PostgreSQL database as-is.

choices.text: Amazon Athena
choices.explanation: This service can analyze data such as data in S3 with SQL. It is not a replacement for a PostgreSQL server that updates order records.

source.label: Amazon RDS — マネージドのリレーショナルデータベース

learning.reason: RDS for PostgreSQL provides a managed PostgreSQL relational database. You can use existing connection methods and SQL while relying on AWS for the operational tasks it manages.
learning.concept: RDS is a relational database, but customer responsibilities such as table design and database user management remain.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Store variable attributes and retrieve items by key
prompt: A mobile app stores settings by user ID and reads and writes one item at a time. The settings differ from user to user. Table joins are unnecessary, and the team wants to respond to changing demand without operating database instances. Which service is the best fit?

choices.text: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
choices.explanation: It can handle keys and variable attributes, but when there is no requirement for existing SQL and the use case calls for a serverless key-value database, DynamoDB is a more direct fit.

choices.text: Amazon Redshift
choices.explanation: This is for data warehouse analytics, not primarily for an application to read and write settings one item at a time.

choices.text: Amazon DynamoDB
choices.explanation: It can be used as a managed NoSQL database that uses user IDs as keys and stores setting attributes in items.

choices.text: AWS Glue Data Catalog
choices.explanation: This manages dataset metadata. It is not a database for reading and writing application settings.

source.label: Amazon DynamoDB — マネージドのNoSQLデータベース

learning.reason: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL database that supports key-value and document access patterns, making it suitable for reading and writing items by user ID.
learning.concept: Choose a database based on the data model and access pattern. The right choice differs between items with variable attributes and SQL workloads with many joins across existing tables.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Cache frequently read product data for a short time
prompt: Keep the product database in place. Many users repeatedly view the same product information, and you want to reduce the load from querying the database on every read. A few minutes of staleness is acceptable, and you want to add a managed in-memory cache. Which service should you use?

choices.text: Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive
choices.explanation: Its primary use is long-term storage. It is not a service for returning product information quickly from memory.

choices.text: Amazon RDS Proxy
choices.explanation: It manages and reuses database connections. It does not store product read results in memory.

choices.text: Amazon Redshift
choices.explanation: It is a data warehouse for analytics, not a service that provides a short-lived value cache for an application.

choices.text: Amazon ElastiCache
choices.explanation: It is a managed in-memory cache that can reduce repeated retrievals of frequently read data.

source.label: Amazon ElastiCache — インメモリキャッシュ

learning.reason: Use ElastiCache to cache frequently read product information in memory. When a value is in the cache, the application can avoid querying the source database.
learning.concept: A cache serves a different purpose from storing the source data. Set an expiration time and decide how to handle updates based on the freshness you can tolerate.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Migrate an active database to AWS in stages
prompt: Migrate a compatible on-premises database to a database on AWS. After copying the existing data initially, you also want subsequent changes to be applied to the target until cutover. You do not need to analyze SQL and want a managed service dedicated to database migration. Which service should you choose?

choices.text: AWS Database Migration Service
choices.explanation: It provides database-aware migration capabilities and can migrate existing data while applying ongoing changes.

choices.text: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration
choices.explanation: It optimizes the transfer path for files to Amazon S3. It does not apply database changes from a change log to a target database.

choices.text: AWS DataSync
choices.explanation: It transfers files and objects between supported storage systems. It does not replicate database changes as a database service.

choices.text: Amazon RDS Proxy
choices.explanation: It manages database connections. It does not continuously migrate data to another database.

source.label: AWS DMS — データベース移行サービス

learning.reason: AWS DMS can migrate existing data and ongoing changes between supported sources and targets.
learning.concept: Moving changes from an active database is different from transferring files or hosting a database.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Deliver the same static content quickly around the world
prompt: A news site's images and CSS are stored at a single origin. You want users overseas to retrieve the same static files from a nearby edge location without deploying origin servers in each region. Which service should you use?

choices.text: Amazon Route 53
choices.explanation: It provides DNS resolution. It does not cache image content at edge locations.

choices.text: Amazon CloudFront
choices.explanation: It uses multiple edge locations to retrieve static files from the origin, cache them, and deliver them.

choices.text: AWS Global Accelerator
choices.explanation: It routes traffic to endpoints over the global network. Caching and delivering static files is not its purpose.

choices.text: AWS Direct Connect
choices.explanation: It provides a dedicated connection between AWS and facilities such as corporate sites. It does not cache images for web users around the world.

source.label: Amazon CloudFront — グローバルなコンテンツ配信

learning.reason: CloudFront uses edge locations to cache and deliver origin content, so it can return files from locations near users.
learning.concept: A CDN delivers content from an origin. Authoritative DNS resolution and TCP traffic path optimization are different functions from serving responses from a cache.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Manage public DNS records for a custom domain
prompt: A company uses a custom domain it has already registered. It wants to manage public DNS records in AWS so users can connect to its website by name, and update the name resolution target when the application's deployment location changes. Which service is appropriate?

choices.text: AWS Certificate Manager
choices.explanation: It manages TLS certificates for domains. It does not manage public DNS records.

choices.text: Amazon VPC
choices.explanation: It isolates networks within AWS. Route 53 is used to operate authoritative public DNS for a custom domain.

choices.text: Elastic Load Balancing
choices.explanation: It can distribute connections among multiple destinations, but it does not manage public DNS records for an entire custom domain.

choices.text: Amazon Route 53
choices.explanation: You can configure DNS records in a public hosted zone and answer name-resolution requests from users.

source.label: Amazon Route 53 — DNSとパブリックホストゾーン

learning.reason: A Route 53 public hosted zone lets you manage DNS records and resolution targets for an internet-facing domain.
learning.concept: DNS records map a name to a connection destination. They serve a different role from TLS certificates or mechanisms that control network destinations.

sourceLabel: Amazon Route 53 — DNS and Public Hosted Zones

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Distinguish public and internal subnets by their routes
prompt: A public load balancer and internal processing servers run in the same VPC. The internal subnet is designed to have no direct route to an internet gateway. What should you check first to determine whether a subnet is public?

choices.text: Whether the subnet name contains public.
choices.explanation: A tag name is for management and does not create a route to the internet.

choices.text: Whether the resource's security group allows HTTPS.
choices.explanation: Allow rules control traffic, but they do not determine the subnet's route to the internet.

choices.text: Whether the associated route table has a direct route to an internet gateway.
choices.explanation: A subnet's public status is determined by the route table it uses and the route to an internet gateway.

choices.text: Whether the subnet's address range is larger than those of other subnets.
choices.explanation: The number of addresses and the type of route used to reach a destination are separate settings.

source.label: Amazon VPC — サブネットの種類と経路

learning.reason: Check whether the route table associated with the subnet has a direct route to an internet gateway.
learning.concept: Even when a subnet is public, resources still need other settings, such as public addresses and appropriate permissions, to connect as intended.

sourceLabel: Amazon VPC — Subnet types and routes

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Connect an on-premises site to AWS over a dedicated connection
prompt: A company sends large amounts of data from its data center to AWS over an extended period. It wants to arrange a dedicated network connection to AWS with a network provider, without relying on its existing connection over the public internet. Which service should it choose?

choices.text: AWS Direct Connect
choices.explanation: It can be used to establish a dedicated connection to the AWS network.

choices.text: AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the public internet
choices.explanation: It can provide an encrypted site-to-site connection, but this option uses an internet path.

choices.text: AWS Client VPN
choices.explanation: It enables individual clients to connect; it is not a service for procuring a dedicated connection from a site.

choices.text: Amazon CloudFront
choices.explanation: It is a CDN for delivering web content and other content; it does not establish a dedicated connection between a site and AWS.

source.label: AWS Direct Connect — 専用ネットワーク接続

learning.reason: Direct Connect is a service for establishing a dedicated network connection from a site or other location to AWS.
learning.concept: A dedicated connection and encryption are separate requirements. Combine the connection with an appropriate encryption method if needed.

sourceLabel: AWS Direct Connect — Dedicated network connection

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Choose persistent storage that an EC2 operating system uses as a disk
prompt: An existing application on EC2 requires a local block device and creates a standard file system on it. The data must remain available after the instance is stopped normally and then restarted. There is no requirement for multiple servers to use the same files concurrently. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: An Amazon S3 general purpose bucket
choices.explanation: It is an object storage service and does not provide EC2 with a local block device.

choices.text: An Amazon EBS volume
choices.explanation: It can be used as a persistent block device attached to EC2.

choices.text: EC2 instance store
choices.explanation: It can be used as a disk, but it does not meet the requirement to retain data through a normal stop.

choices.text: An Amazon EFS file system
choices.explanation: It provides shared files over NFS; it is not a block device that the operating system initializes as a local disk.

source.label: Amazon EBS — EC2用の永続ブロックストレージ

learning.reason: An EBS volume can be attached to EC2 and used as a disk. It retains data when the instance is stopped.
learning.concept: Storage can be used as block storage, shared file storage, or object storage. Choose the type that matches how the existing application needs to read and write data.

sourceLabel: Amazon EBS — Persistent block storage for EC2

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Use the same files from multiple Linux servers
prompt: Linux applications running on multiple EC2 instances read and write the same files and directories over NFS. The same file system must remain available as servers are added or removed, and the company does not want to operate a shared storage server. Which service should it choose?

choices.text: Attach a separate EBS volume to each EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: Each volume stores files separately, so this does not provide the same shared file system across servers.

choices.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
choices.explanation: It provides Windows SMB shares and is not the option for the specified Linux application's NFS share.

choices.text: Amazon EFS
choices.explanation: Multiple clients can mount the same NFS file system.

choices.text: Access an Amazon S3 bucket over HTTP.
choices.explanation: Data can be shared across multiple servers this way, but it does not preserve the existing NFS interface.

source.label: Amazon EFS — Linux向けマネージド共有ファイルシステム

learning.reason: EFS provides a managed shared NFS file system. Multiple EC2 instances can access the same namespace.
learning.concept: Linux NFS shares, Windows SMB shares, and S3 object access use different interfaces.

sourceLabel: Amazon EFS — Managed shared file system for Linux

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Choose a storage class for long-term record retention
prompt: To meet a legally required retention period, store records in S3 for the long term. They are rarely accessed, and you can wait up to 48 hours after a request for them to be restored. You want a storage class designed for long-term archiving and prioritize storage cost per unit. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: S3 Standard
choices.explanation: Designed for frequently accessed data. It is not the best fit when low storage cost for long-term archiving is the priority.

choices.text: S3 Express One Zone
choices.explanation: Designed for low-latency access in a single Availability Zone. It is not intended for long-term, infrequently accessed archival data.

choices.text: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
choices.explanation: Designed for data that is accessed rarely but must be retrieved immediately. Immediate retrieval is not a requirement here.

choices.text: S3 Glacier Deep Archive
choices.explanation: Suitable for long-term, infrequently accessed storage when restoration time is acceptable.

source.label: Amazon S3 — ストレージクラスの用途

learning.reason: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is designed for long-term archiving when access is extremely rare and waiting for restoration is acceptable.
learning.concept: Compare not only storage cost, but also retrieval time and fees and the minimum storage duration for the intended use.

sourceLabel: Amazon S3 — Storage Class Use Cases

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Buffer incoming requests in a queue for sequential processing
prompt: An application receives many image-processing requests in a short time. You want to separate intake from transformation so that workers retrieve requests at the rate they can process them. There is no requirement to deliver the same notification to many specific destinations. Which service is appropriate?

choices.text: Amazon SQS
choices.explanation: Holds processing requests until they are consumed, and workers can receive them.

choices.text: Use only an HTTPS subscription to Amazon SNS.
choices.explanation: This delivers messages from a topic to its subscribers; it is not a dedicated queue from which workers retrieve requests at their own pace.

choices.text: Elastic Load Balancing
choices.explanation: Distributes incoming connections or requests to destinations. It is not a service for explicitly holding requests in a queue over time for workers to consume.

choices.text: Amazon Route 53
choices.explanation: Resolves DNS names. It does not store processing requests and pass them to workers.

source.label: Amazon SQS — マネージドメッセージキュー

learning.reason: Queue requests in SQS so available workers can retrieve them according to their processing capacity.
learning.concept: SQS decouples the operating rates of senders and receivers. An SNS topic delivers messages to subscribers; these services can also be combined to serve multiple purposes.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Choose a virtual server that you manage at the OS level
prompt: A company wants to install its proprietary business software on a Linux OS and manage the OS and network settings itself. Which AWS service is the best fit?

choices.text: AWS Lambda
choices.explanation: Provides a managed function execution environment and is not used to manage a guest OS.

choices.text: AWS Elastic Beanstalk managed platform
choices.explanation: Simplifies application deployment management. For directly managing a general-purpose virtual server where arbitrary business software can be installed, EC2 is appropriate.

choices.text: Amazon EC2
choices.explanation: You can choose the virtual server to launch and manage the guest OS and application settings yourself.

choices.text: Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate
choices.explanation: Provides a managed container execution environment. It is not a service where users directly manage a server with arbitrary OS settings.

learning.reason: EC2 provides virtual servers whose operating systems users manage.
learning.concept: Distinguish EC2, an IaaS service, from serverless execution.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Run containers without managing servers
prompt: A team will run a long-running, containerized web application. It does not want to manage EC2 operating system updates or allocate runtime capacity. Which option should it choose?

choices.text: Create only an EC2 Auto Scaling group.
choices.explanation: You can adjust the number of instances, but operations for the EC2 instances that run the containers and container management remain.

choices.text: Use AWS Fargate with Amazon ECS.
choices.explanation: Manage containers with ECS and leave the execution hosts to Fargate.

choices.text: Use the EC2 launch type in Amazon ECS.
choices.explanation: ECS can manage the containers, but the operations team must manage the EC2 capacity on which they run.

choices.text: Create only the Amazon EKS control plane.
choices.explanation: You can have a Kubernetes control plane, but you must configure separately where the containers run.

learning.reason: Use ECS to manage the containers and Fargate to manage the servers that run them.
learning.concept: ECS orchestrates containers, and Fargate provides a managed runtime for running them.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Analyze S3 logs with SQL without managing servers
prompt: An operations team wants to inspect logs stored in S3 with SQL only when needed. It does not want to manage database servers or an ETL cluster continuously. Which service is the best fit?

choices.text: An Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster
choices.explanation: It supports SQL, but this choice requires configuring a cluster. For serverless, on-demand analysis of logs in S3, Athena is more direct.

choices.text: Build a query engine on Amazon EC2
choices.explanation: You can configure it to analyze S3, but you must operate the servers.

choices.text: Create only an AWS Glue Data Catalog
choices.explanation: It manages data metadata. The catalog alone does not run SQL against the logs.

choices.text: Amazon Athena
choices.explanation: It runs SQL against data in S3 without requiring you to operate a dedicated query server.

learning.reason: Amazon Athena runs SQL against data in S3 without requiring users to operate an analytics server.
learning.concept: S3 stores data, a catalog manages data definitions, and Athena runs SQL; these services have different roles.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Repeatedly create the same environments from a template
prompt: You want to repeatedly create the same VPC and application foundation in development, test, and production, reducing configuration differences caused by manual work. Which AWS service is the best fit?

choices.text: Create each environment manually in the AWS Management Console
choices.explanation: You can configure individual settings, but you cannot manage them as a template that reproduces the environment from the same inputs.

choices.text: AWS CloudFormation
