choices.explanation: It lets you describe infrastructure in declarative templates and apply the same definition to different environments.

choices.text: Record existing configurations with AWS Config
choices.explanation: It records and evaluates the configuration of existing resources. It does not create resources from a template.

choices.text: Save the creation operations for the first environment with AWS CloudTrail
choices.explanation: The records are useful for auditing, but the logs are not infrastructure templates for creating other environments.

learning.reason: Use AWS CloudFormation templates to manage the configuration and apply it repeatedly across environments.
learning.concept: With Infrastructure as Code (IaC), you declare the configuration and can review changes instead of configuring each environment separately in a management console.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Extract text and form fields from invoice images
prompt: An accounting department wants to extract printed text, tables of amounts, and field name–value pairs from scanned invoices. Which service is the best fit for using invoice images as data input?

choices.text: Amazon Rekognition
choices.explanation: It can recognize objects and scenes in images. Textract is better suited to structuring tables and key-value relationships in documents.

choices.text: Amazon Transcribe
choices.explanation: It converts speech to text; it does not extract tables from scanned documents.

choices.text: Amazon Textract
choices.explanation: It can extract text and tables, as well as form field names and values, from scanned documents.

choices.text: Amazon Comprehend
choices.explanation: It analyzes documents that are already in text form. This differs from reading text and tables from scanned images.

learning.reason: Amazon Textract can extract text, tables, and form field names and values from scanned documents.
learning.concept: Document analysis can extract structure as well as text. This differs from image classification labels and speech transcription.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Automatically classify objects and places in photos
prompt: You want to automatically classify photos for a product catalog by their content, such as furniture, food, or outdoor scenes. You do not need to verify anyone’s identity; you want labels based on the objects and scenes in the images. Which service is appropriate?

choices.text: Amazon Textract
choices.explanation: It is suited to extracting text and tables from documents, not classifying objects and scenes in photos.

choices.text: Amazon Comprehend
choices.explanation: It analyzes text and entities; it does not detect objects from image pixels.

choices.text: Amazon Translate
choices.explanation: It translates text into another language; it does not classify image content into labels.

choices.text: Amazon Rekognition
choices.explanation: It detects objects and scenes in images and returns labels that describe their content.

source.label: Amazon Rekognition — 画像内の物体とシーンの検出

learning.reason: Amazon Rekognition can detect labels for objects and scenes in images.
learning.concept: Distinguish identifying objects and places in images from extracting text and tables from forms.

sourceLabel: Amazon Rekognition — Detecting objects and scenes in images

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Create searchable transcripts from training recordings
prompt: A company wants to make recordings of internal training sessions searchable. It needs to convert the spoken content in the recordings into text and create records that a search system can read. Which AWS service should it use?

choices.text: Amazon Polly
choices.explanation: It converts existing text into speech, the reverse of converting recorded speech into text.

choices.text: Amazon Transcribe
choices.explanation: It converts recorded speech into text, which can then be used for search.

choices.text: Amazon Translate
choices.explanation: It converts text from one language to another. It does not transcribe recordings.

choices.text: Amazon Comprehend
choices.explanation: It analyzes the content of text documents. It does not directly convert recordings into text.

learning.reason: Amazon Transcribe can automatically transcribe recorded speech.
learning.concept: Transcribe converts speech to text; Polly converts text to speech. Translate converts text from one language to another.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Manage S3 data table definitions in one place
prompt: An analytics team uses data in an S3 data lake with multiple analytics services. The team wants to register the data locations, column names, and data types in a shared location so the services can reference the table definitions without moving the underlying files. Which AWS feature is appropriate?

choices.text: Tables in an Amazon Redshift cluster
choices.explanation: These can manage analytics tables, but they are not a shared catalog for multiple services to reference data that remains in S3.

choices.text: AWS CloudFormation
choices.explanation: It manages infrastructure configurations with templates. It does not provide a shared service for analytics data columns and types.

choices.text: AWS Glue Data Catalog
choices.explanation: It centrally manages table definitions and schemas that analytics services can reference.

choices.text: AWS Glue data transformation jobs
choices.explanation: These process inputs and transform them into outputs. Their role differs from centrally managing table definitions.

learning.reason: You can register metadata such as table columns, data types, and S3 locations in the AWS Glue Data Catalog.
learning.concept: A data catalog manages definitions while the data itself remains in storage such as S3.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Estimate the total cost of maintaining the current environment
prompt: A company is comparing the costs of its on-premises equipment with AWS costs. The finance team knows how much it currently spends to purchase servers, but it also wants to include the costs required to operate the current environment in its total cost of ownership (TCO). Which two additional items should it evaluate?

choices.text: The cost of electricity and cooling for the facilities that house the servers
choices.explanation: These costs continue after the hardware is purchased because the facilities must be operated.

choices.text: The cost of running a data transfer test on AWS for the migration
choices.explanation: This is a migration-planning cost, not a cost of owning and operating the current environment.

choices.text: The estimated AWS usage charges after reservation-based discounts for the target environment
choices.explanation: These are usage charges for a potential target configuration, not costs of the current environment.

choices.text: Staff labor required to maintain and monitor the company's facilities
choices.explanation: This is part of the cost of continuously operating the facilities.

choices.text: AWS training for the operations team that will support the target environment
choices.explanation: This can be evaluated as a target-environment preparation cost, but it is separate from the cost of maintaining the current facilities.

source.label: AWS Prescriptive Guidance — 移行のビジネスケースとTCO

learning.reason: Operating existing servers also requires facilities, electricity, cooling, and operations staff. A current-cost estimate should include more than the price of the equipment.
learning.concept: For a useful TCO assessment, compare costs that continue to occur with costs that change as a result of migration, using the same scope and time period.

sourceLabel: AWS Prescriptive Guidance — Migration Business Case and TCO

category: クラウドの概念
title: Limit the impact of a failure affecting some customers
prompt: In a SaaS environment, a configuration error in one customer group made the same shared processing system unavailable to other customers. For the next design, the company wants other customer groups to continue processing even if one processing system stops. Which design most directly serves this purpose?

choices.text: Configure automatic scaling for a single processing system used by all customers.
choices.explanation: This can handle increased demand, but all customers still depend on one processing system.

choices.text: Assign customers to multiple independent processing systems.
choices.explanation: If one system fails, the impact can be limited to the customers assigned to that system.

choices.text: Distribute the same processing system used by all customers across multiple Availability Zones.
choices.explanation: This can protect against a single Availability Zone failure, but applying the same configuration to everyone does not isolate customers from the effects of a configuration error.

choices.text: Configure customer-specific logs and notifications while continuing to share the processing system.
choices.explanation: This makes failures easier to identify, but it does not isolate other customers from their effects.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected — 障害の影響を分離する設計

learning.reason: Separate customer groups into independent processing units so a failure in one unit is less likely to affect another.
learning.concept: Fault isolation limits the scope of a problem. Increasing the capacity of a single shared dependency does not, by itself, change that scope.

sourceLabel: AWS Well-Architected — Designing for fault isolation

category: クラウドの概念
title: Distinguish data durability from data availability
prompt: The stored photos are not corrupted, but users could not retrieve them during a brief outage. The operations team sets separate objectives for preventing permanent data loss and for making data easy to retrieve on request. Select two correct pairings of evaluation dimension and what it measures.

choices.text: Durability measures whether stored data can be retained without being lost.
choices.explanation: Even when a temporary outage prevents use, whether the data itself was lost can be evaluated separately.

choices.text: Availability measures the amount of data rollback time that is acceptable when recovering from an outage.
choices.explanation: The acceptable rollback, expressed as time, is the RPO. Availability measures whether a service can be used.

choices.text: Availability measures whether stored data can be retrieved on request.
choices.explanation: This evaluates how consistently the service keeps data in a readable state.

choices.text: Durability measures the recovery time that can be accepted before failed requests succeed again.
choices.explanation: The target for acceptable recovery time is the RTO. It is a separate dimension from keeping data intact.

choices.text: Retention period measures the read-success rate during an outage.
choices.explanation: A retention period specifies how long data must be kept; it does not measure the proportion of time it is available during an outage.

source.label: Amazon S3 — データの耐久性と可用性

learning.reason: Durability measures whether data is kept without permanent loss, while availability measures whether the service can be used when requested. The same outage can be assessed along both dimensions.
learning.concept: Data can remain intact even when access to the service or retrieval temporarily fails. Consider both measures according to the use case.

sourceLabel: Amazon S3 — Data durability and availability

category: クラウドの概念
title: Protect systems in layers from the entry point to the data
prompt: A transaction application combines a filter at its public entry point, restrictions on internal communications, application authorization, and access controls for data. The aim is for controls in other layers to remain effective if one protection has a problem. Which design principle is being applied?

choices.text: Run the same configuration in two Regions for high availability.
choices.explanation: Distributing across Regions helps prepare for outages, but it is not the principle of layering controls from the network through to the data.

choices.text: Grant only the minimum permissions needed for the task.
choices.explanation: This is useful for authorization in each layer, but the question focuses on layering protections across distinct layers.

choices.text: Use the same audit-log format for every application.
choices.explanation: This helps with traceability, but it is different from placing access controls in each layer.

choices.text: Apply security at all layers.
choices.explanation: This fits the decision to place distinct controls at the entry point, within the network, in the application, and at the data layer.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected — セキュリティの設計原則

learning.reason: The design does not rely only on the entry point; it applies security controls across several independent layers.
learning.concept: Each layer controls something different. Combining network controls, application authorization, and data protection strengthens the overall protection.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Evaluate a cost-saving proposal against the business recovery-time tolerance
prompt: As a way to reduce cloud costs, someone proposes reducing the capacity of a standby environment. Scaling down the standby environment could slow recovery. The business recovery-time objective cannot change. Which decision is consistent with the Well-Architected approach?

choices.text: Evaluate recovery time and cost after the reduction, then choose from the proposals that meet the recovery objective.
choices.explanation: This determines whether costs can be improved while still meeting the business requirements for reliability.

choices.text: Adopt the least expensive proposal before checking recovery time.
choices.explanation: It is not yet known whether the business requirement for recovery time will be met.

choices.text: Ignore cost and always adopt only the proposal that promises the fastest recovery.
choices.explanation: This prevents comparing the costs of multiple proposals that meet the requirements.

choices.text: Set the acceptable recovery time only when an incident occurs.
choices.explanation: This gives up the benefit of setting a clear objective in advance and evaluating the design before adopting it.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected — トレードオフの判断

learning.reason: Do not decide based on cost alone. Evaluate recovery time after the reduction, then compare costs among the options that meet the business objective.
learning.concept: Objectives across different pillars can involve trade-offs. Clarify the requirements that matter and choose a design that meets them within those constraints.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Decide whether to retire an unnecessary system before migration
prompt: During a migration inventory, the team finds an old application that has not been used for years and is not referenced by any downstream systems. The responsible department has approved its retirement, and any required history has already been saved. Which migration strategy should be selected for this application to avoid bringing unnecessary operations to AWS?

choices.text: Rehost
choices.explanation: Move it with few changes. Operations will continue even after the unnecessary system has been moved.

choices.text: Retire
choices.explanation: After confirming required history and dependencies, decommission an unnecessary application.

choices.text: Retain
choices.explanation: Continue running it in the existing environment; this does not meet the condition of ending unnecessary operations.

choices.text: Replatform
choices.explanation: This is a way to migrate by changing the platform, not a way to decommission an application that is no longer used.

source.label: AWS Prescriptive Guidance — 移行前の不要アプリの評価

learning.reason: After confirming that the application is unnecessary and checking its dependencies, do not migrate it; decommission it using the retire strategy.
learning.concept: Retain means continuing to use an application in its current environment while deferring migration. Retire means ending use of an application that no longer has business value.

sourceLabel: AWS Prescriptive Guidance — Assessing unnecessary applications before migration

category: クラウドの概念
title: Provide a production-scale test environment only when needed
prompt: A company wants to test a new application at its expected production scale. The cost of keeping an equally large test environment on premises at all times was prohibitive. Which approach makes the best use of cloud characteristics?

choices.text: Test with a small configuration and assume it will produce the same results under peak production load.
choices.explanation: A small environment cannot directly confirm how the application behaves at its maximum scale.

choices.text: Keep a full-scale test environment running, including during periods when no test is planned.
choices.explanation: This provides production-scale capacity but does not take advantage of paying for cloud resources only when needed.

choices.text: Provision a production-scale environment only for the time needed, then release it after testing.
choices.explanation: This lets the company test at the required scale without maintaining excess resources outside the test period.

choices.text: Size production resources above the forecast so testing is no longer necessary.
choices.explanation: Buying extra capacity does not verify that the application actually works at the intended scale.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected — クラウド設計の一般原則

learning.reason: Provision an environment at production scale only during testing, then remove the resources when they are no longer needed. This verifies real-scale behavior without maintaining excess capacity full time.
learning.concept: Whether a test is production-like depends on its scale and conditions. The ability to create and release an environment when needed can improve the test conditions.

sourceLabel: AWS Well-Architected — General Design Principles for Cloud Computing

category: クラウドの概念
title: Keep user sessions when replacing a server
prompt: A web application stores a user's logged-in session in the memory of the server that handled it. When that server is replaced during an update, the session is lost. Which change follows the design principle that any server should be able to handle the next request?

choices.text: Add processing capacity to the existing server while preserving its sessions.
choices.explanation: Increasing capacity does not prevent state from being lost when the server that holds the session is replaced.

choices.text: Use a load balancer to keep each user on the first server they reached.
choices.explanation: Routing can keep a user on the same server while it is available, but replacing it does not transfer its in-memory state.

choices.text: Create an image of the server configuration before replacement and launch a new server from the same image.
choices.explanation: The configuration can be reproduced, but sessions stored only in the memory of running processes are not preserved.

choices.text: Store sessions in a shared store that any application server can access.
choices.explanation: This avoids tying state to an individual server.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected — ステートレスな処理の設計

learning.reason: Separate the required session state from application servers and store it in a data store that multiple servers can access.
learning.concept: Decoupling request handling from state reduces the need to pin users to a particular server during replacement or scaling.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Scale up a smaller recovery environment after a disaster
prompt: A company keeps its entire application running in another Region at lower capacity than usual. During a production outage, it can scale up the recovery environment to accept requests. This limits normal operating costs and avoids building the configuration from scratch after an outage. What is this recovery approach called?

choices.text: Backup and restore
choices.explanation: After an outage, data is restored and the required environment is prepared. That does not match the condition of keeping the entire application running at reduced capacity during normal operations.

choices.text: Warm standby
choices.explanation: A complete copy runs at reduced capacity and can be scaled up when an outage occurs.

choices.text: Pilot light
choices.explanation: Core services are kept running, and the rest of the configuration is launched after an outage. This differs from keeping the entire application running during normal operations.

choices.text: Multi-site active-active
choices.explanation: This assumes multiple sites process production traffic during normal operations, unlike the smaller recovery environment described here.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected — クラウドでの災害復旧方式

learning.reason: Warm standby keeps a copy of the entire application running at smaller scale and expands it during a disaster.
learning.concept: Backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, and multi-site operation differ in how much of the recovery site runs continuously.

sourceLabel: AWS Well-Architected — Disaster Recovery Options in the Cloud

category: クラウドの概念
title: Keep core functionality available during failure of a supporting service
prompt: An online store cannot open its order page when the supporting service that generates product recommendations stops responding. Orders can be completed without recommendations. Which design lets the core functionality continue during a temporary outage of the supporting service?

choices.text: Keep waiting to respond to order requests until the recommendation service recovers.
choices.explanation: The core functionality continues to depend on the supporting feature being available.

choices.text: If recommendations are unavailable, increase the wait time and retry until they succeed.
choices.explanation: Continuing to wait does not meet the goal of completing orders.

choices.text: If recommendations cannot be retrieved, omit that part and provide the ordering functionality.
choices.explanation: The required core functionality can continue even when the supporting feature is unavailable.

choices.text: If the supporting service has an error, also fail the order service's health check.
choices.explanation: This does not isolate the failure and makes the core functionality unavailable too.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected — 正常に縮退できる設計

learning.reason: If recommendations cannot be retrieved, omit them or show default content while allowing orders to proceed independently.
learning.concept: Distinguishing required dependencies from those that can be absent while core functionality remains available helps keep a partial failure from becoming a complete outage.

sourceLabel: AWS Well-Architected — Designing for Graceful Degradation

category: クラウドの概念
title: The pillar for choosing technology as demand changes
prompt: An analytics team’s data volume has grown, and its usage patterns have shifted throughout the day. The team wants to benchmark storage formats and compute types, then choose resources again effectively while meeting its processing-time target. Which Well-Architected pillar addresses this central concern?

choices.text: Cost Optimization
choices.explanation: This pillar focuses on avoiding unnecessary spending.

choices.text: Operational Excellence
choices.explanation: This pillar focuses on operating procedures and continuous improvement.

choices.text: Performance Efficiency
choices.explanation: Correct. It covers resource selection, adapting to changing demand, and making use of evolving technologies.

choices.text: Reliability
choices.explanation: This pillar focuses on recovering from failures and maintaining availability.

learning.reason: The Performance Efficiency pillar covers selecting and using resources that meet service requirements, and maintaining that efficiency as demand and technology change.
learning.concept: Performance and cost are related, but they are addressed by different pillars.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Measuring the value of cloud investment
prompt: Executives want to continuously measure and govern the investment value, risks, and compliance of cloud adoption. Which AWS CAF perspective is most relevant?

choices.text: People
choices.explanation: It covers roles and skills.

choices.text: Governance
choices.explanation: Correct. It covers value realization, risk management, compliance, and measuring outcomes.

choices.text: Platform
choices.explanation: It covers building the cloud foundation.

choices.text: Operations
choices.explanation: It covers day-to-day service operations.

learning.reason: Governance connects investment value and risk to business objectives.
learning.concept: CAF addresses organizational cloud adoption as well as technology.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Optimizing an application for the cloud during migration
prompt: A company is migrating an existing application that runs as a single process. During the migration, it will separate order and notification processing and run each on managed services, requiring substantial changes to the code and integration approach. What is this migration strategy called?

choices.text: Rehost
choices.explanation: This approach moves the application as-is, without major changes.

choices.text: Replatform
choices.explanation: This approach changes the runtime environment for optimization but does not substantially redesign the original architecture or major portions of the code.

choices.text: Repurchase
choices.explanation: This approach switches to a different product, such as SaaS; it is distinct from rebuilding the architecture and code of the existing application.

choices.text: Refactor / Re-architect
choices.explanation: Correct. This strategy substantially changes the application to take advantage of cloud-native capabilities.

learning.reason: Refactoring involves substantial changes to take advantage of cloud capabilities.
learning.concept: Rehost and Refactor differ in the extent of change and the cloud optimization they enable.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Reducing undifferentiated operational work
prompt: A retailer wants developers to focus on improving product features. Meanwhile, they spend a great deal of time patching server operating systems, replacing hardware, and maintaining backup infrastructure. Which primary benefit is the company seeking through its use of the AWS Cloud?

choices.text: Purchase capacity in advance and keep additional headroom for extra load.
choices.explanation: This secures capacity, but the team still has to operate the hardware and operating systems.

choices.text: Shift undifferentiated heavy lifting to AWS and focus on product value
choices.explanation: Correct. Managed services reduce the operational burden of the underlying infrastructure, allowing staff to focus on business-specific value.

choices.text: Switch from paying for equipment up front to paying based on usage.
choices.explanation: This changes the cost structure, but changing the payment model alone does not reduce work such as OS patching.

choices.text: Deploy services across multiple Regions and place them closer to users.
choices.explanation: This can help with user proximity and recovery, but it does not address the goal of delegating maintenance work to cloud services.

source.label: AWS Overview: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers

learning.reason: One benefit of the cloud is reducing the burden of operating undifferentiated infrastructure so teams can focus on work specific to the business.
learning.concept: Using managed services does not transfer responsibility for data and access.

sourceLabel: AWS Overview: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers

category: クラウドの概念
title: Review the design before and after changes
prompt: The team has a major change to a production workload coming up. It wants to build Well-Architected Reviews into its operations so it can identify priority risks before the change and decide on improvements after usage patterns change. What is the most appropriate approach?

choices.text: Review every question only at the initial release and reuse the results for the next project.
choices.explanation: This preserves the assessment from the release, but it does not keep pace with changes to this workload or shifts in how it is used.

choices.text: Review the workload only if an incident occurs after the change, and record the incident's direct cause.
choices.explanation: This can support learning after an incident, but it does not meet the goal of finding risks in advance and continuing to improve after changes.

choices.text: Repeat the review at milestones such as before and after major changes, and track improvement items.
choices.explanation: Correct. Repeating the review helps prioritize improvements and adapt the design as conditions change.

choices.text: Review costs only when the budget changes, and address design issues separately.
choices.explanation: A cost-only review cannot track risks such as reliability or security issues associated with major design changes.

learning.reason: A Well-Architected Review is an iterative improvement activity aligned with changes and learning, not a one-time audit.
learning.concept: Reviews at key milestones and tracking improvement items help raise design quality continuously.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Measure resource use against business outcomes
prompt: A video streaming company wants to set goals to reduce its environmental impact while maintaining quality. It wants to measure improvements in relation to business value, not only its total monthly consumption. Which metric is most useful from a sustainability perspective?

choices.text: Monthly infrastructure costs, tracked separately from the hours of content streamed
choices.explanation: Costs are also affected by changes such as unit prices, and they do not directly measure resource use per viewing hour.

choices.text: Compute resource use per hour of content streamed
choices.explanation: Correct. Tracking resource use per unit of business outcome makes it possible to improve efficiency while preserving value.

choices.text: The streaming platform's total monthly CPU hours, without adjusting for viewing hours
choices.explanation: Total CPU use can be a useful reference, but if the volume of streaming also changes, it is difficult to tell whether fewer resources are needed to deliver the same service.

choices.text: The number of Regions used, counted without reference to streaming volume
choices.explanation: This indicates the scale of the configuration but not the resources used to deliver a given number of viewing hours.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected Sustainability Pillar: Establish sustainability goals

learning.reason: For sustainability, goals and measurements that connect business value with resource efficiency, such as resource use per business outcome, are useful.
learning.concept: Assess efficiency against business value over time, rather than looking only at absolute totals.

sourceLabel: AWS Well-Architected Sustainability Pillar: Establish sustainability goals

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Registration and sign-in for a consumer app
prompt: A retailer is launching an app for consumers. It wants a managed service to provide email-based user registration, password resets, and token issuance after sign-in. Which feature is appropriate?

choices.text: Assign users to company accounts with AWS IAM Identity Center
choices.explanation: This is suited to employee access to AWS accounts and business applications. It serves a different purpose from features that let consumers self-register in an app.

choices.text: Issue temporary AWS credentials to users with an Amazon Cognito identity pool
choices.explanation: This feature grants credentials for accessing AWS resources to users, such as authenticated users; it does not handle user registration or password resets.

choices.text: Manage app users with an Amazon Cognito user pool
choices.explanation: A user pool can accept customer registration and sign-in and issue tokens for the app after successful authentication.

choices.text: Manage the company's domain with AWS Managed Microsoft AD
choices.explanation: This is intended for domain joins and Active Directory integration, not for consumers to register their own accounts in an app.

source.label: Amazon Cognito ユーザープール

learning.reason: A user pool provides an app's user directory for registration, authentication, and token issuance.
learning.concept: Distinguish authentication of app users from granting access to AWS resources.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Manage users and keys on a dedicated HSM
prompt: A payment provider cannot share the hardware used for its app's cryptographic operations with other customers. It wants to create and manage its own cryptographic users for using keys, and to use them from the app through standard cryptographic libraries. Which service should it choose?

choices.text: Create a customer managed key in the AWS KMS standard key store
choices.explanation: The key policy can be managed, but customers do not directly manage the users of HSMs in the standard key store.

choices.text: Store the cryptographic user's credentials in AWS Secrets Manager
choices.explanation: Storing credentials does not provide cryptographic operations on dedicated hardware.

choices.text: Manage a certificate with a private key in AWS Certificate Manager
choices.explanation: This can manage TLS certificates, but it does not provide a dedicated HSM or HSM users for the app.

choices.text: Use a dedicated HSM with AWS CloudHSM
choices.explanation: AWS CloudHSM provides single-tenant HSMs and lets an organization manage cryptographic users and keys for its apps.

learning.reason: AWS CloudHSM provides single-tenant HSMs and lets customers manage users and keys within the HSM.
learning.concept: The permissions to operate a dedicated HSM and the permissions to use managed cryptographic keys are managed at different layers.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Manage application settings by environment
prompt: The URLs for external services used by an application differ between the development and production environments. You want to register the URLs under environment-specific names on AWS and control read access through the application's IAM permissions. The values are fixed strings that contain no sensitive information, and staged rollout and rotation are not needed. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Collect the settings with AWS Systems Manager Inventory
choices.explanation: This feature collects information such as software details from managed nodes; it is not a mechanism for registering settings that an application reads.

choices.text: Store the settings under environment-specific paths in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
choices.explanation: You can separate environments with a hierarchy and use IAM to manage access to the corresponding parameter names or paths.

choices.text: Enable rotation for each URL in AWS Secrets Manager
choices.explanation: Secrets Manager can store URLs, but adding rotation is unnecessary for fixed settings.

choices.text: Have the application read the configuration history in AWS Config
choices.explanation: AWS Config tracks the history of AWS resource configurations; it is not a configuration store for registering application-specific URLs by environment.

learning.reason: Parameter Store manages setting names, values, and versions, and lets you organize reads using hierarchical names and IAM.
learning.concept: Distinguish storing fixed configuration values from distributing configuration through a release process.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Group permissions for existing IAM users by job function
prompt: In a single AWS account, individual IAM users already exist for the accounting staff. You want to preserve how these users sign in and be able to attach or replace the same read-only policy for everyone in one place. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Add the users to an IAM group and attach the shared policy to the group
choices.explanation: This keeps the individual IAM users while providing one place to attach the shared policy.

choices.text: Create the same inline policy separately for each IAM user
choices.explanation: This can allow the required actions, but the policy must still be changed for each user.

choices.text: Apply an accounting service control policy to the target account
choices.explanation: An SCP limits the maximum permissions in an account; it cannot grant read permissions only to the accounting staff.

choices.text: Set only an IAM permissions boundary on the target users
choices.explanation: A permissions boundary sets the maximum permissions that can be granted. The boundary itself does not grant the required read actions.

learning.reason: Attaching a policy to an IAM user group applies shared permissions to the group's members.
learning.concept: A group centralizes permission assignments for IAM users in the same account.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Use centrally managed subnets across multiple accounts
prompt: A company that uses AWS Organizations has an account for its network team, which manages a VPC and its routes. An application team wants to create its own EC2 instances in specified subnets of that VPC from a separate member account. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Connect an application VPC to the central VPC with VPC peering
choices.explanation: This enables communication between VPCs, but peering does not grant permission to create EC2 instances in the other VPC's subnets.

choices.text: Create a VPC for each application and connect them with AWS Transit Gateway
choices.explanation: This can connect multiple VPCs, but the application team's EC2 instances would be placed in their respective VPCs' subnets.

choices.text: Share the central VPC's subnets with the target account using AWS Resource Access Manager
choices.explanation: Participants can create resources in shared subnets while the VPC owner continues to manage routes and other network settings.

choices.text: Move the application account into the same OU in AWS Organizations
choices.explanation: An OU groups accounts; placing accounts in the same OU does not make the central VPC's subnets available.

source.label: AWS Resource Access Managerとサブネット共有

learning.reason: With a shared VPC, the owner shares subnets using AWS RAM, and participants can place resources they own in those shared subnets.
learning.concept: Distinguish connecting accounts for communication from sharing the subnets themselves.

sourceLabel: AWS Resource Access Manager and subnet sharing

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Inventory the credential status of existing IAM users
prompt: An auditor wants a tabular view, for each existing IAM user in a single AWS account, of whether MFA is enabled and when the access key was last created or rotated. Where can the auditor retrieve this information for the users in one operation?

choices.text: AWS CloudTrail event history
choices.explanation: This can be used to investigate past API activity, but it does not provide a consolidated inventory of every user's current MFA and credential status.

choices.text: IAM service last accessed information
choices.explanation: This is used to review access to services for which permissions exist; it does not provide a consolidated view of MFA status or key rotation dates.

choices.text: AWS Config resource configuration history
choices.explanation: This tracks resource changes, but IAM provides a report that consolidates the requested credential information.

choices.text: An IAM credential report
choices.explanation: It includes each user's MFA status, access key status, and information such as the last rotation time.

learning.reason: IAM credential reports export credential status for IAM users as a CSV, including MFA and access key status and dates.
learning.concept: Credential-state inventory, API activity investigations, and permission-usage reviews serve different purposes.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Preparing a New AWS Account with a Standard Configuration
prompt: A company provisions new AWS accounts every month. It wants a multi-account environment with a shared configuration for security logs and audit access, and it wants to create new accounts from preapproved settings. Which service combines AWS management capabilities to meet these needs?

choices.text: Consolidated billing in AWS Organizations
choices.explanation: It consolidates account charges, but billing does not provide a shared audit configuration or account configuration templates.

choices.text: An AWS Control Tower landing zone and Account Factory
choices.explanation: They establish a standardized multi-account environment and provision accounts from configured templates.

choices.text: An AWS Config conformance pack
choices.explanation: It can deploy a set of configuration assessment rules, but it does not issue new accounts and build the foundation as an integrated capability.

choices.text: An AWS Security Hub delegated administrator
choices.explanation: It centralizes security findings, but it does not provision member accounts from standard settings.

learning.reason: Control Tower provides a landing zone, controls, and account creation capabilities to help standardize a multi-account environment.
learning.concept: When both a standard environment and account creation are required, deploying an individual service alone is not enough.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Protecting the Original Version of Stored Audit Records During the Retention Period
prompt: Audit records are stored in Amazon S3. Regulations require that even an administrator be unable to delete the original version of a record until its specified retention period expires. Which feature is appropriate?

choices.text: Set a retention period with S3 Object Lock in compliance mode
choices.explanation: It protects retained object versions until the deadline and prevents even highly privileged principals from deleting them.

choices.text: Enable S3 Versioning alone
choices.explanation: It retains versions from before an overwrite, but does not prevent an authorized principal from permanently deleting a specific version by specifying its version ID.

choices.text: Set a retention deadline with S3 Lifecycle
choices.explanation: It automates transitions and expiration according to a schedule, but does not prohibit earlier manual deletion.

choices.text: Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode
choices.explanation: It protects objects against ordinary operations, but principals with the required permissions can bypass governance retention.

learning.reason: In Object Lock compliance mode, even the AWS account root user cannot delete a protected version during its retention period.
learning.concept: Distinguish retaining object versions from prohibiting their deletion during a retention period.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Recording Allowed and Rejected Traffic in a VPC
prompt: An auditor wants to review later the source, destination, and allow-or-reject status of IP traffic observed at network interfaces in a VPC. The auditor does not want to collect application payloads. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Record AWS CloudTrail management events
choices.explanation: These can be used to investigate changes such as security group updates, but they do not record IP traffic passing through network interfaces.

choices.text: Record security group configurations with AWS Config
choices.explanation: This can show the configuration at a given time, but does not record the actual observed source or destination.

choices.text: Record allowed and rejected traffic with VPC Flow Logs
choices.explanation: They collect flow records suited to this purpose and do not record packet payloads.

choices.text: Monitor the EC2 NetworkIn metric with Amazon CloudWatch
choices.explanation: This shows traffic volume, but it is not a metric that records the source, destination, and allow-or-reject status of each flow.

learning.reason: VPC Flow Logs collect IP traffic metadata and, depending on the configuration, record allowed and rejected traffic.
learning.concept: Distinguish records of actual network traffic from records of configuration changes made through AWS APIs.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Using Cross-Account Audit Permissions for a Short Time
prompt: An auditor is signed in to their own AWS account as an existing IAM principal. They need to review resource configurations across multiple services in another business unit's account. How can read-only access be granted without issuing long-term credentials for the auditor in the target account?

choices.text: Add the target business unit's administrative actions to an IAM policy in the audit account
choices.explanation: A policy in the audit account alone does not establish permissions for resources in another account.

choices.text: Create a dedicated IAM user for the auditor in the target account and provide access keys
choices.explanation: Read permissions can be restricted, but issuing long-term credentials does not meet the requirement.

choices.text: Place both accounts in the same OU and apply an SCP that allows read access
choices.explanation: An SCP sets permission boundaries; it does not grant cross-account role assumption or read permissions.

choices.text: Create a read-only IAM role in the target account and allow the audit account principal to assume it
choices.explanation: The auditor can use their existing credentials to obtain a short-term role session, with actions in the target account limited to read access.

source.label: IAMロールでアカウント間アクセスを委任する

learning.reason: Create a role with read permissions in the target account and allow the audit account principal to assume it; the auditor can then act with temporary credentials.
learning.concept: The role's trust relationship controls who can assume it, while its permissions policy controls actions after assumption.

sourceLabel: Delegate access across AWS accounts using IAM roles

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Evaluate a proposed permission change before applying it in production
prompt: An operations team is reviewing an identity-based policy to attach to its IAM role. Before making changes in production, the team wants to verify whether the proposed policy allows a specified combination of AWS API action and resource. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Check CloudTrail for records of calls to the API in question.
choices.explanation: This can show operations that have occurred so far, but it does not evaluate how a policy that has not yet been attached to the production role would behave.

choices.text: Enter the proposal in the IAM Policy Simulator and specify the action and resource to evaluate it.
choices.explanation: This lets the team check whether access is allowed or denied under the specified conditions without changing actual AWS resources.

choices.text: Check shared-resource findings in IAM Access Analyzer's external access analyzer.
choices.explanation: This is used to find external sharing; it does not evaluate an arbitrary action and resource combination against a proposed role policy.

choices.text: Query AWS Config for the configuration history of existing resources.
choices.explanation: This can track changes to actual configurations, but it does not determine API permissions for a hypothetical identity-based policy.

source.label: IAMポリシーシミュレーター

learning.reason: The IAM Policy Simulator can evaluate whether a policy allows specified actions on specified resources without calling an API in the live environment.
learning.concept: Use different mechanisms to evaluate proposed permissions and audit operations that have actually occurred in production.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Detect unintended external sharing
prompt: A company regularly audits settings that share S3 buckets and IAM roles with external AWS accounts. It wants to detect when a resource policy allows access by a principal outside the organization before that principal actually performs an operation. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Use AWS CloudTrail to look for resource operations performed by external principals.
choices.explanation: Usage can be investigated from operation records, but this does not identify sharing that no one has exercised yet.

choices.text: Enable IAM Access Analyzer external access analysis with the organization as the zone of trust.
choices.explanation: It evaluates policies on supported resources and can detect access allowed for principals outside the zone of trust.

choices.text: List IAM service last accessed information.
choices.explanation: This is useful for reviewing how permissions attached to IAM principals are used; it does not determine whether resources are shared externally.

choices.text: Run an Amazon Macie sensitive data discovery job for S3.
choices.explanation: This checks whether object contents contain sensitive data; it does not analyze both the specified S3 bucket and the IAM role's trust policy.

learning.reason: IAM Access Analyzer external access analysis examines policies on supported resources and detects configurations that allow access by principals outside the zone of trust.
learning.concept: After detection, check whether the sharing is intentional and revise permissions that are not needed.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Continuously check stored container images for vulnerabilities
prompt: A company wants to check container images stored in ECR for known vulnerabilities in the OS and programming language dependency packages. It also wants findings to update automatically for newly disclosed vulnerabilities, even while an image remains unchanged. Which setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Run ECR basic scanning at image push.
choices.explanation: Basic scanning covers OS vulnerabilities. Configuring it to run only at push does not continuously evaluate an image that remains unchanged.

choices.text: Configure ECR enhanced scanning with scan frequency set to scan on push.
choices.explanation: The scan covers the required package types, but this frequency does not continuously check an unchanged image for newly disclosed vulnerabilities.

choices.text: Configure continuous scanning for the target repositories with ECR enhanced scanning.
choices.explanation: Through integration with Amazon Inspector, it checks OS and language packages for configured targets and can update findings when new vulnerabilities are disclosed.

choices.text: Monitor running containers with Amazon GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring.
choices.explanation: This can detect runtime threats, but it does not continuously assess vulnerabilities in images stored in ECR.

learning.reason: When continuous scanning is selected for ECR enhanced scanning, Inspector evaluates the target images and can reflect updated vulnerability information in scan results.
learning.concept: Distinguish assessing dependency packages in stored images from monitoring behavior at runtime.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Visualize related events during a security investigation
prompt: GuardDuty has generated a finding about the behavior of a production role. A security analyst wants to visualize relationships and activity over time among the related AWS account, role session, and IP address to continue the investigation. Which service can help with this task?

choices.text: Use AWS Security Hub CSPM to check whether controls pass.
choices.explanation: It can be used for standards-based configuration checks, but that purpose differs from a graph for analyzing the finding and the behavior of related entities.

choices.text: Use AWS Config to check when the IAM role was configured.
choices.explanation: Configuration changes can be investigated, but AWS Config does not provide a graph for analyzing relationships across sessions and network activity.

choices.text: Enable GuardDuty threat detection again.
choices.explanation: This may produce new findings, but it is different from investigating related entities and their past activity based on an existing finding.

choices.text: Use Amazon Detective to investigate the activity of related entities.
choices.explanation: Using a graph built from AWS log data and findings, it can help investigate related entities and their actions.

learning.reason: Amazon Detective graphs entity relationships and activity based on evidence such as AWS logs, helping analysts trace the context behind findings.
learning.concept: Use GuardDuty for threat findings and Detective to investigate them.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Centrally applying WAF policies across multiple accounts
prompt: Multiple accounts in AWS Organizations use ALBs. The security team plans to centrally manage common AWS WAF rules and continue applying the policy to newly in-scope accounts and ALBs. Choose the appropriate service and use case combination.

choices.text: Apply an AWS WAF policy to the organization’s targets with AWS Firewall Manager.
choices.explanation: The organization’s administrators can centrally manage WAF policies for in-scope accounts and resources.

choices.text: Deploy an AWS Config conformance pack to the organization.
choices.explanation: A set of rules for evaluating configuration compliance can be deployed, but this alone does not continuously apply WAF rules to each ALB.

choices.text: Write HTTP request conditions into an AWS Organizations SCP.
choices.explanation: An SCP sets the maximum permissions for AWS API actions. It does not define traffic rules for HTTP requests passing through a load balancer.

choices.text: Add common WAF rules to each ALB with AWS Shield Standard.
choices.explanation: Shield Standard provides DDoS protection, but it does not manage AWS WAF rules across multiple accounts.

learning.reason: Firewall Manager lets you specify the scope in AWS Organizations and centrally apply policies such as WAF policies to accounts and AWS resources.
learning.concept: Distinguish individual WAF rule configuration from organization-wide policy governance.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Automatically renewing an ACM public certificate in use
prompt: You want an ACM-issued public certificate used by an ALB to renew without manual work at each expiration. The organization will continue to own the domain. When using DNS validation, choose two conditions that must be maintained for automatic renewal.

choices.text: Keep the certificate in use by a supported AWS service.
choices.explanation: An ACM-issued certificate integrated with an ALB is eligible for ACM managed renewal while it remains in use.

choices.text: Enable ALB access logs and retain them for the same period as the certificate’s validity.
choices.explanation: Access logs help analyze traffic, but they are not a condition ACM uses to verify the certificate’s in-use status or domain.

choices.text: Delete the DNS validation CNAME before the certificate’s renewal deadline.
choices.explanation: The CNAME is also used during renewal, so deleting it may cause DNS validation to fail.

choices.text: Keep the validation CNAME requested by ACM resolvable in public DNS.
choices.explanation: At renewal time, ACM uses DNS to confirm that you still control the certificate’s domain.

choices.text: Reissue the ACM-issued certificate externally each time and import it into ACM.
choices.explanation: Importing an external certificate leaves renewal management to you and is not a condition for automatic renewal of an ACM-issued certificate.

source.label: DNS検証した証明書のACM自動更新

learning.reason: An ACM-issued certificate in use by a supported service can be domain-validated during automatic renewal if its DNS validation record remains available in public DNS.
learning.concept: The party responsible for renewal differs between imported certificates and ACM-issued certificates.

sourceLabel: ACM managed renewal for DNS-validated certificates

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Using a Microsoft Active Directory managed by AWS
prompt: A company is moving Windows applications to AWS. It wants application servers to join an Active Directory domain and use LDAP and Group Policy, so it needs a new Microsoft AD running in AWS. Which option avoids operating the domain controller infrastructure itself?

choices.text: AWS Directory Service AD Connector
choices.explanation: It relays authentication and other requests to an existing Microsoft AD; it does not provide new domain controllers in AWS.

choices.text: AWS IAM Identity Center
choices.explanation: It can manage access to AWS accounts and business applications, but it does not provide a Microsoft AD domain for joining Windows machines.

choices.text: AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory
choices.explanation: AWS Managed Microsoft AD provides Microsoft Active Directory whose underlying infrastructure is operated by AWS.

choices.text: Launch Windows Server on Amazon EC2 and configure it as a domain controller.
choices.explanation: This can provide the required functionality, but you must configure and operate the domain controller on Windows Server.

learning.reason: AWS Managed Microsoft AD provides managed Microsoft Active Directory and supports domain joins and Group Policy.
learning.concept: Distinguish directory services from services that manage employees’ access to AWS.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Reviewing checks against an AWS security standard
prompt: The security team is using the AWS-provided AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard. It wants to enable the controls associated with the standard, without creating rules one by one, and review results for each check and the score for the standard as a whole. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Review the configuration timeline for recorded resources in AWS Config.
choices.explanation: This tracks changes to individual configurations, but does not provide checks for controls in a specified standard or an overall score for that standard.

choices.text: Enable the relevant security standard in AWS Security Hub CSPM.
choices.explanation: It runs checks based on the standard’s controls and lets you review results and the score for that standard.

choices.text: Retrieve AWS audit reports from AWS Artifact.
choices.explanation: You can obtain third-party audit materials for AWS, but they do not provide control-by-control inspection results for your own resources.

choices.text: Review the response status in AWS Well-Architected Tool.
choices.explanation: It helps teams manage architecture reviews and improvements, but does not run automated checks against the specified standard.

learning.reason: Security Hub CSPM evaluates controls for enabled security standards and calculates a score for the applicable standard.
learning.concept: In addition to aggregating findings from external sources, it can assess your AWS environment against defined standards.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Audit AWS account API activity across all Regions
prompt: An auditor needs to continuously store management events recorded across all enabled Regions for a single AWS account in one Amazon S3 bucket. The events must remain queryable beyond the retention period of Event history in the console. Which configuration should be selected?

choices.text: Create a single-Region trail for only the Region with the most activity.
choices.explanation: It can deliver logs to the specified destination, but the same trail will not cover management events from other Regions.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail Event history and search it in the console regularly.
choices.explanation: It allows you to inspect eligible management events from the last 90 days in the selected Region, but this method does not continuously store them in S3.

choices.text: Create only a CloudTrail Lake event data store.
choices.explanation: Events can be retained and queried in CloudTrail Lake, but this does not configure continuous delivery of trail logs to the specified S3 bucket.

choices.text: Select management events in a multi-Region trail and specify the destination S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: This continuously records the selected management events from all enabled Regions in the specified bucket.

learning.reason: A multi-Region trail covers events from all enabled Regions and can deliver logs to a selected S3 bucket.
learning.concept: Distinguish Event history, which is used to inspect recent activity, from a trail that continuously collects events across Regions.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Automatically replace an unhealthy EC2 instance
prompt: An internal processing server must always run three EC2 instances with the same configuration. If an instance becomes unhealthy, the healthy capacity must return to three without an operator starting an instance manually. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Use Elastic Load Balancing to remove the unhealthy target from the routing pool.
choices.explanation: This changes which targets receive requests, but it does not launch a replacement instance to maintain the count.

choices.text: Set the desired capacity to three in Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling.
choices.explanation: Replacement based on health checks can automate keeping the specified number of instances running.

choices.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch to notify the team when a status check fails.
choices.explanation: This makes the issue visible, but a notification alone does not replace an instance.

choices.text: Reserve capacity for three instances with an EC2 On-Demand Capacity Reservation.
choices.explanation: This can reserve capacity for launches, but it does not replace an instance when one becomes unhealthy.

learning.reason: An Auto Scaling group manages desired capacity and can replace instances it determines to be unhealthy.
learning.concept: Distinguish routing traffic from maintaining the number of running instances.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Route requests by HTTP path on the same host
prompt: A company web service uses one host name. For incoming HTTPS requests, paths beginning with /catalog should be sent to the product team's EC2 fleet, while paths beginning with /orders should be sent to the order team's EC2 fleet. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Use a TCP listener on a Network Load Balancer.
choices.explanation: It can forward TCP traffic through the same entry point, but it cannot inspect HTTP paths to route requests.

choices.text: Use weighted routing in Amazon Route 53.
choices.explanation: It can vary the DNS records returned according to the proportion configured, but DNS queries do not include HTTPS paths.

choices.text: Create an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group for each team.
choices.explanation: This manages EC2 instance counts and replacement; it does not route requests according to HTTP paths.

choices.text: Configure listener rules on an Application Load Balancer.
choices.explanation: Path conditions can be set on the same HTTPS listener, and requests can be forwarded to the corresponding target group.

learning.reason: An Application Load Balancer can inspect HTTP/HTTPS request information and forward requests to target groups according to path rules.
learning.concept: Identify whether the required routing condition comes from HTTP information or network connection information.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Run AWS compute at a factory site
prompt: An application’s compute must be located inside a factory so that control equipment can access it within a few milliseconds. The company wants to use its existing factory network together with AWS-managed hardware and some AWS services. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Install AWS Outposts at the factory.
choices.explanation: This lets the application run on AWS-managed infrastructure located at the factory.

choices.text: Connect the factory to a Region with AWS Direct Connect.
choices.explanation: This provides a dedicated connection, but by itself it does not locate compute at the factory.

choices.text: Use the AWS Local Zone closest to the factory.
choices.explanation: Processing can run in a nearby AWS facility, but the compute would not be located inside the company’s factory.

choices.text: Apply AWS Systems Manager to the company’s server fleet.
choices.explanation: This can manage existing servers, but it does not provide AWS-managed compute hardware at the factory.

learning.reason: Outposts places AWS-managed infrastructure at a customer site and extends supported AWS services locally.
learning.concept: Distinguish accessing a Region through a network connection from locating compute infrastructure at the company’s own site.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Providing a Fixed Entry Point for a Multi-Region TCP Service
prompt: A company runs a TCP-based application in two AWS Regions. Its business partners allowlist the public IPv4 address used to connect. Which option is appropriate for routing traffic to a healthy regional destination while keeping the fixed IP address registered by the partners unchanged?

choices.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution
choices.explanation: It is suitable for HTTP and HTTPS distributions, but it cannot serve as the entry point for an arbitrary TCP application.

choices.text: Use Amazon Route 53 to fail over between the IP addresses in the two Regions
choices.explanation: DNS can switch destinations, but it does not provide a shared fixed entry IP before and after the switch.

choices.text: Create a standard accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator
choices.explanation: It can use public static IP addresses as a shared entry point and direct TCP traffic to healthy regional endpoints.

choices.text: Deploy a Network Load Balancer in each Region and use each one’s fixed IP address
choices.explanation: This provides a fixed entry point in each Region, but not a shared entry point with automatic routing between Regions.

learning.reason: Global Accelerator provides fixed Anycast IP addresses as an entry point and sends traffic to healthy endpoints based on their status and other factors.
learning.concept: Distinguish TCP applications that need a global static entry point from HTTP content delivery.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Routing Events to Different Processes Based on Their Content
prompt: An ecommerce site sends order creation, cancellation, and shipment events to the same entry point. The inventory process should receive only cancellations, and the shipping analytics process should receive only shipments. Which option routes events by type using rules, without requiring changes to the order system’s code when a new process is added?

choices.text: Put all events in one Amazon SQS queue, and have each process receive from that same queue
choices.explanation: Consumers compete to retrieve messages. The queue does not select consumers based on event content.

choices.text: Set up rules for each event type on an Amazon EventBridge event bus
choices.explanation: Rules can match events sent to a single bus by type and deliver them to the corresponding processes.

choices.text: Register all processes on the same Amazon SNS topic without filters
choices.explanation: This delivers notifications to all subscribers and does not send only the relevant event types to each process.

choices.text: Use AWS Step Functions to process every received event with the same fixed workflow
choices.explanation: It can manage a sequence of steps, but as described, it does not route events to separate processes based on event type.

learning.reason: On an EventBridge event bus, rules can match event content and deliver matching events to targets.
learning.concept: Distinguish a queue that stores messages, notification delivery, and rule-based event routing.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Managing Multi-Step Execution Status and Retries
prompt: A document-processing workflow must inspect a file, then transform it after inspection succeeds, and then register it. It should retry only temporary transformation failures a few times, and operators should be able to check how far each execution has progressed in a management console. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Define the steps and retries in an AWS Step Functions state machine
choices.explanation: It can manage processing order, retries, and state for each execution.

choices.text: Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to start the three processes at separate times
choices.explanation: A schedule alone cannot make the preceding process’s success a condition for running the next one.

choices.text: Queue three process requests in an Amazon SQS FIFO queue
choices.explanation: It can manage delivery order within the same message group, but the success conditions for the processing steps and the overall execution state must be managed separately.

choices.text: Aggregate the logs for the three processes in Amazon CloudWatch Logs
choices.explanation: The logs can be used to investigate execution status afterward, but they do not control step order or retries on failure.

learning.reason: Step Functions lets you define processing order and retries in a state machine, and track each step’s result in execution history.
learning.concept: Distinguish a workflow that tracks a sequence of processes from a feature that delivers individual events.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Managing a Public API and Throttling Before Lambda
prompt: A company exposes an HTTP-based API that uses an existing Lambda function. It wants to manage the integration for each HTTP route and limit requests at the API entry point when they arrive in a burst. Which option is suitable?

choices.text: Set only the reserved concurrency for AWS Lambda
choices.explanation: This controls a function’s concurrency, but it does not provide a shared HTTP entry point that exposes functions by route.

choices.text: Route requests to a Lambda target with an Application Load Balancer
choices.explanation: It can route HTTP requests to Lambda, but this configuration alone does not provide API rate limiting.

choices.text: Create an API record in Amazon Route 53
choices.explanation: It can resolve the API’s name, but it cannot select by HTTP route or control the request rate.

choices.text: Configure routes and throttling in Amazon API Gateway
choices.explanation: It can integrate Lambda with HTTP routes and control request flow at the entry point.

learning.reason: API Gateway provides an entry point for HTTP-based APIs and supports routing and throttling.
learning.concept: Distinguish limiting API traffic at the entry point from limiting only the number of backend function executions.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Send personalized emails to individual buyers
prompt: Whenever a purchase is completed, an e-commerce site must send the customer who made that purchase an HTML email containing the item details. The sender must use the company's verified email domain, and customers must not have to subscribe to a notification topic in advance. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Send a topic notification to Amazon SNS email subscribers
choices.explanation: Topic delivery requires prior subscription, so it is not suited to transactional email whose recipient address is specified for each purchase.

choices.text: Send an email notification about an AWS Support case
choices.explanation: Support case notifications are for Support communications; they do not let an application send purchase details to customers.

choices.text: Use Amazon SES to send the purchase details to the customer
choices.explanation: A verified sender identity can be used to send individualized content to the relevant customer for each purchase. For production sending, also check the account's sending limits and usage requirements.

choices.text: Store the item details email in Amazon SQS
choices.explanation: This can make sending asynchronous, but the queue itself does not deliver messages to external email addresses.

learning.reason: Amazon SES lets an application send transactional email by specifying the recipient, a verified sender identity, and the message content.
learning.concept: Distinguish topic notifications sent to a fixed set of subscribers from email whose recipient and content vary with each transaction.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Manage backups for multiple services under one policy
prompt: A team has decided to use AWS Backup to protect EBS, RDS, and EFS. It wants to create backups every night and retain each recovery point for 35 days. In addition to assigning the resources, choose two settings specified in the backup plan's rules.

choices.text: Set the recovery point retention period to 35 days.
choices.explanation: The lifecycle in a backup rule can specify when recovery points expire.

choices.text: Choose the IAM principals allowed to access the backup vault.
choices.explanation: Vault access control is part of permissions management; it does not set the desired backup schedule or retention period.

choices.text: Copy resources with tags to another Region.
choices.explanation: Cross-Region copy can be configured as additional protection, but it is not required to create backups every night and retain the same recovery points for 35 days.

choices.text: Set the backup schedule to run every night.
choices.explanation: The rule's schedule determines when backup jobs start.

choices.text: Configure a restore testing plan with a 35-day cycle.
choices.explanation: Restore testing prepares for recovery; it does not determine when these backups are created or how long they are retained.

source.label: AWS Backupのバックアッププラン

learning.reason: In a backup rule, the schedule sets when recovery points are created, and the lifecycle sets how long they are retained.
learning.concept: Consider backup frequency and retention period separately. Copying and restore testing use separate settings.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Use an existing AD for authentication to a Windows SMB share
prompt: An application that a company is migrating to AWS uses Windows SMB file shares. It must authenticate users with the existing Active Directory and set Windows access permissions at the file level. Which service can reduce the need to manage the file server's operating system?

choices.text: Use an Amazon EFS file system
choices.explanation: EFS can provide shared files, but its standard sharing protocol is NFS, not the same access method as Windows SMB.

choices.text: Attach Amazon EBS volumes to each Windows client
choices.explanation: Windows can use block devices, but EBS alone does not provide SMB shares or AD integration.

choices.text: Connect the application directly to an Amazon S3 bucket
choices.explanation: The S3 object API cannot be used as-is as a replacement for an existing SMB share or Windows file access permissions.

choices.text: Join Amazon FSx for Windows File Server to the AD
choices.explanation: It can provide SMB shares, support existing AD users and Windows access permissions, and leave server management to AWS.

source.label: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

learning.reason: FSx for Windows File Server provides a managed SMB file system and supports Active Directory authentication and Windows access controls.
learning.concept: Check the sharing protocol and existing access-permission model the application requires.

sourceLabel: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Store files in S3 while keeping existing NFS operations
prompt: A warehouse's Linux application cannot be changed from writing files over NFS. Newly generated files must be stored as objects in S3, and employees want to keep using a familiar shared path and a local cache. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Expose an NFS share with Amazon S3 File Gateway
choices.explanation: It lets the application keep using existing file operations while storing files in S3 through the gateway.

choices.text: Copy the existing NFS share to S3 nightly with AWS DataSync
choices.explanation: Data transfer can be automated, but DataSync does not provide the NFS share itself with a local cache.

choices.text: Mount Amazon EFS over NFS and store files there directly
choices.explanation: Files can be accessed over NFS, but they would be stored in EFS, not as S3 objects.

choices.text: Create an S3 bucket and change only the application's NFS endpoint
choices.explanation: The S3 API does not provide the NFS protocol, so a bucket cannot be accessed directly over NFS.

learning.reason: S3 File Gateway provides a file share backed by S3 over protocols such as NFS and can use a local cache.
learning.concept: Distinguish periodic copying from an active file share that uses S3 as its storage destination.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Connecting many VPCs with centralized routing
prompt: Several departments have VPCs in the same Region, and more will be added as the organization grows. The organization wants to centrally manage which VPCs are allowed to connect and reduce the need to add peering for each pair of VPCs that needs to communicate. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Create a VPC peering connection for each pair of VPCs
choices.explanation: This establishes connectivity, but the organization still has to manage connections and routes for each VPC pair.

choices.text: Use AWS PrivateLink to expose each application's endpoint
choices.explanation: This provides access to specific services, but it is different from centrally managing general routing between VPCs.

choices.text: Attach the VPCs to AWS Transit Gateway and manage routes centrally
choices.explanation: The VPCs can connect to a common hub, and route tables can control the scope of connectivity.

choices.text: Share name resolution through Amazon Route 53 Resolver
choices.explanation: Name resolution does not create network paths for communication between VPCs.

learning.reason: Transit Gateway is a central hub that connects VPCs and other networks, allowing routing to attachments to be managed centrally.
learning.concept: Distinguish many-to-many VPC connectivity from access to individual services and network name resolution.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Reading the same stream independently in multiple analytics applications
prompt: Manufacturing equipment continuously sends measurements. One application performs immediate anomaly detection, while another aggregates the data. Both applications must read the same measurement records independently, and after recovery, each must be able to resume reading from an earlier position within the retention period. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Use one Amazon SQS standard queue and have both applications delete messages when processing them
choices.explanation: Sharing a queue does not ensure that both applications receive the same message, and it does not support rereading from an arbitrary position after deletion.

choices.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, with each application reading the stream independently
choices.explanation: Each application can retrieve records independently within the retention period and reread them from the required position.

choices.text: Subscribe to an Amazon SNS standard topic and push messages directly to the subscribers
