choices.explanation: Messages can be delivered to multiple destinations, but a standard topic does not provide a stream that each subscriber can reread from an arbitrary earlier position.

choices.text: Use only Amazon Data Firehose to deliver measurements to a destination
choices.explanation: It can deliver data to a destination, but it does not provide two applications with native stream read positions.

learning.reason: Kinesis Data Streams retains data in a stream, allowing applications to read independently from their own positions and reprocess data that is still within the retention period.
learning.concept: Distinguish event delivery and processing queues from a retained stream whose continuous data can be reread independently.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Training and deploying an image classification model with your own data
prompt: A company is developing an image classifier for use in its factories. It wants to use data labeled for facility-specific defects and training code maintained by its team, run a training job, and deploy the resulting model to a managed inference endpoint. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Use the standard label detection API in Amazon Rekognition as is
choices.explanation: It can detect labels with a pretrained model, but it does not run training code maintained by the team.

choices.text: Analyze the inspection images with Amazon Textract
choices.explanation: This service is designed to extract text and structure from documents; it is not a platform for running arbitrary image-classification training code.

choices.text: Store the images and model files in Amazon S3
choices.explanation: S3 can store training data and models, but it does not itself run training jobs or inference endpoints.

choices.text: Use training jobs and managed inference in Amazon SageMaker AI
choices.explanation: The team can create a model using its training code and deploy it to an inference endpoint for operation.

learning.reason: SageMaker AI can run custom training jobs and deploy trained models to managed inference endpoints.
learning.concept: Distinguish AI APIs that use pretrained models from an ML platform that can run your own training process.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Managing a Kubernetes application on AWS
prompt: An organization wants to move its existing Kubernetes manifests and kubectl-based operations to AWS. It wants AWS to operate the cluster's Kubernetes API server and maintain control plane availability, while the organization manages the workloads it deploys. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Deploy the existing Kubernetes manifests with Amazon ECS.
choices.explanation: ECS has its own task definitions and management API; it is not a managed service that uses the Kubernetes API as is.

choices.text: Build the Kubernetes control plane on Amazon EC2.
choices.explanation: This can preserve the existing operating model, but the customer must operate the API server and control plane.

choices.text: Use an Amazon EKS Kubernetes cluster.
choices.explanation: The organization can use the Kubernetes API and manifests while delegating operation of the control plane to AWS.

choices.text: Store container images in Amazon ECR and use it as the cluster.
choices.explanation: ECR is a container image registry; it does not provide a Kubernetes control plane.

learning.reason: Amazon EKS provides a managed Kubernetes control plane. Users manage workloads with standard Kubernetes tools.
learning.concept: Distinguish Kubernetes requirements from AWS-native container orchestration.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Centralize OS patching for EC2
prompt: You need to apply OS patches to EC2 instances across multiple AWS accounts according to approved baselines and scheduled maintenance windows, and view which servers are missing patches in a management console. Which feature should you use to do this without signing in to each server?

choices.text: Use Amazon Inspector to assess EC2 vulnerabilities.
choices.explanation: It can detect vulnerabilities, but this feature alone does not apply OS patches according to approval rules.

choices.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager.
choices.explanation: You can select managed nodes to scan and apply patches, then review their patch status.

choices.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to open a shell session on each EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: It lets you maintain instances without opening an inbound SSH port, but per-server operations do not meet the requirement to manage patching without handling each server individually.

choices.text: Use AWS Config to review EC2 configuration history.
choices.explanation: It lets you review configuration changes to AWS resources, but it does not apply OS patches.

learning.reason: Patch Manager can be configured to scan and apply patches to managed nodes and to check patch compliance.
learning.concept: Distinguish vulnerability detection and auditing from patch execution.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Translate app text into other languages
prompt: An e-commerce site wants to convert English product descriptions received from suppliers into text in several languages before publication while preserving the structure of the original text. Both input and output are text, and the company wants to avoid building its own translation model. Which service should it use?

choices.text: Amazon Polly
choices.explanation: It synthesizes speech from text; it does not translate input text into text in another language.

choices.text: Amazon Comprehend
choices.explanation: It can analyze language, key phrases, and sentiment, but it does not translate product descriptions into a specified language.

choices.text: Amazon Transcribe
choices.explanation: It transcribes recordings and audio streams; it does not translate input text.

choices.text: Amazon Translate
choices.explanation: It is a managed service that translates input text into a supported target language.

learning.reason: Amazon Translate translates text between supported languages. Speech recognition and sentiment analysis are not part of the requirement.
learning.concept: Identify the input and output media, and whether the goal is translation, speech synthesis, or language analysis.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Transfer on-premises files to AWS at high speed
prompt: A company wants to copy new and changed files from an active on-premises NFS share to Amazon S3 every night without changing how the share is operated. It wants to use a managed service to validate the data after transfer and monitor the jobs. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Run a scheduled transfer task in AWS DataSync with the NFS share and S3 as the locations.
choices.explanation: You can use the existing share as the source and manage scheduling, transfers of changed files, data verification, and transfer monitoring.

choices.text: Deploy Amazon S3 File Gateway and move users' NFS mount point to it.
choices.explanation: It can provide access to S3 through a new share, but it does not meet the requirement to operate nightly transfer tasks without changing the existing share.

choices.text: Use AWS Database Migration Service with the NFS share as the source.
choices.explanation: This is a database migration service, not a file transfer feature for synchronizing an NFS share to S3 nightly.

choices.text: Create only an AWS Transfer Family SFTP endpoint.
choices.explanation: It can provide an upload destination over SFTP, but it does not provide a task that periodically scans an existing NFS share and transfers files with verification.

learning.reason: AWS DataSync lets you create a task to transfer files from an existing file share to S3 and manage scheduling, transfers of changed files, and verification.
learning.concept: Distinguish ongoing network transfers from transfers using offline devices.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Analyze large volumes of historical data with BI
prompt: A company wants to consolidate sales line items from multiple business units into a common table, store them, and run daily BI queries across several years of history. Which managed data warehouse is purpose-built to ingest and store data and analyze it with SQL?

choices.text: Amazon Athena
choices.explanation: It can query data such as data in S3 directly with SQL, but this service alone is not a purpose-built data warehouse for ingesting and managing sales line items.

choices.text: Amazon Redshift
choices.explanation: It can ingest data for large-scale SQL aggregation and analysis and can connect to BI tools.

choices.text: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
choices.explanation: It is a general-purpose relational database that supports SQL, but it is not the purpose-built analytics data warehouse required here.

choices.text: Amazon DynamoDB
choices.explanation: It is designed for workloads that access individual items by key, not as a dedicated service for SQL analytics across years of relational data.

learning.reason: Amazon Redshift is a managed data warehouse for SQL analytics, making it suitable for analyzing consolidated historical data with BI tools.
learning.concept: Choose among an operational database, a way to query data directly in S3, and a purpose-built data warehouse.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Using a shell script to list AWS resources
prompt: An operations team periodically retrieves lists of AWS resources. The team wants to repeat AWS operations from its existing in-house shell scripts without manually using the console. It does not plan to develop an application that incorporates a library for a particular programming language. Which access method is appropriate?

choices.text: Create a new application that uses an AWS SDK to call AWS APIs.
choices.explanation: This can automate operations, but it requires writing a program in the chosen language and is not a good fit for calling AWS directly from an existing script.

choices.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console and open the resource list for the relevant service.
choices.explanation: This lets the team view the list, but someone still has to operate the console each time.

choices.text: Review AWS CloudTrail management events.
choices.explanation: This is a way to review logs of past management operations; it does not retrieve the current resource list for each service.

choices.text: Include AWS Command Line Interface commands in the shell script.
choices.explanation: The script can call the commands needed to retrieve lists from AWS services and repeat the same operations.

learning.reason: AWS CLI exposes service APIs as shell commands, so AWS operations can be incorporated into existing scripts.
learning.concept: Distinguish the interactive console, the CLI used as shell commands, and the SDK incorporated into an application.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Choosing an EC2 family for CPU-intensive batch processing
prompt: A company is reviewing the EC2 instance family used for a video conversion batch job. Current measurements show that memory and local disk have spare capacity, and the software does not use a GPU. During conversion, CPU utilization remains near its upper limit. Which type should the company evaluate first?

choices.text: Memory optimized instances
choices.explanation: These are suited to workloads that keep large amounts of data in memory; no memory shortage has been observed here.

choices.text: Storage optimized instances
choices.explanation: These suit workloads that need high local I/O performance, but local storage is not the constraint for this batch job.

choices.text: Compute optimized instances
choices.explanation: These instances are designed for CPU-dependent workloads, making them a candidate for this batch job's CPU load.

choices.text: Accelerated computing instances
choices.explanation: These suit workloads that use hardware accelerators, but the conversion software in this scenario does not use a GPU.

learning.reason: Compute optimized instances are suited to CPU-intensive workloads that need high processor performance.
learning.concept: Choose instance candidates based on the resource that is actually constrained: CPU, memory, storage I/O, or accelerators.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Detecting and notifying about abnormal EC2 CPU utilization
prompt: A monitoring team wants an alarm to enter the ALARM state when EC2 CPU utilization stays above 90% for a specified evaluation period, and to notify an existing notification target. Which service should it configure to evaluate the standard CPU metric?

choices.text: An Amazon CloudWatch metric alarm
choices.explanation: It can evaluate the CPU utilization metric against a threshold over an evaluation period and send a notification to a destination such as SNS when its state changes.

choices.text: An Amazon EventBridge schedule
choices.explanation: It can start recurring tasks, but this configuration alone does not evaluate CPU utilization values over each measurement period.

choices.text: EC2 recommendations in AWS Compute Optimizer
choices.explanation: These can suggest changes such as instance sizing based on usage history, but they do not provide notifications based on a specified CPU threshold.

choices.text: An Amazon EC2 system status check
choices.explanation: It detects underlying infrastructure problems, but it is not an alarm based on a CPU utilization threshold.

learning.reason: A CloudWatch metric alarm evaluates measurements against a threshold and evaluation period, determines its state, and performs configured actions.
learning.concept: Distinguish operational monitoring, auditing, and security assessment.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Notifying the team about spending that deviates from usual patterns
prompt: Development environment costs vary by day of the week. The team wants to notify the responsible team when spending deviates substantially from its usual pattern, rather than when a monthly budget reaches a certain percentage. Monitoring a threshold based only on a fixed amount is not required. Which service is appropriate?

choices.text: AWS Pricing Calculator
choices.explanation: It is used to estimate costs before creating resources; it does not monitor unusual costs in an existing account.

choices.text: Use AWS Budgets to send a notification when a certain percentage of the monthly budget is reached.
choices.explanation: Budget-based notifications are available, but this does not detect deviations from usual spending patterns that vary by day of the week.

choices.text: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection
choices.explanation: It can detect costs that deviate from historical spending patterns and send notifications.

choices.text: Manually compare this month's usage with last month's in AWS Cost Explorer.
choices.explanation: This helps review spending trends, but it does not automatically detect spending that deviates from usual patterns and notify the responsible team.

source.label: AWS Cost Management — AWS Cost Anomaly Detection

learning.reason: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection learns spending patterns, detects unusual spending, and can notify the responsible team.
learning.concept: A budget threshold and detecting anomalies against historical patterns are different. Anomaly detection does not automatically stop spending.

sourceLabel: AWS Cost Management — AWS Cost Anomaly Detection

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Exporting detailed AWS usage statements to S3 on a recurring basis
prompt: The finance team needs to ingest billing details into its existing analytics platform. It needs more than monthly service-level cost charts: it must continuously export detailed AWS usage and charges to S3 so they can be reconciled with other data. Which AWS feature is most appropriate?

choices.text: AWS Budgets threshold notifications
choices.explanation: These can notify you when spending is likely to exceed a budget, but they do not continuously export detailed billing line items.

choices.text: Create a CUR 2.0 export with AWS Data Exports.
choices.explanation: It can deliver detailed AWS cost and usage line items to S3.

choices.text: Save a Cost Explorer chart from the console.
choices.explanation: This is useful for analyzing trends, but it does not configure automatic delivery of line-item data to S3.

choices.text: Export a cost estimate from AWS Pricing Calculator.
choices.explanation: This is an estimate based on a configuration, not a statement of charges billed and usage actually incurred.

source.label: AWS Data Exports — Cost and Usage Report 2.0

learning.reason: AWS Data Exports can use CUR 2.0 to deliver detailed cost and usage data to S3 on a recurring basis.
learning.concept: Exporting detailed line items and exploring spending trends in a default console view serve different purposes.

sourceLabel: AWS Data Exports — Cost and Usage Report 2.0

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Avoiding a long-term commitment for a short, non-interruptible test
prompt: A product test using EC2 will run for about 10 days. The number of instances and their run times will vary from day to day, and interruption by AWS reclaiming Spot capacity is not acceptable. There is no need for a one-year usage commitment or a capacity reservation in a specific Availability Zone. Which purchasing option is appropriate?

choices.text: On-Demand Instances
choices.explanation: You can use them without a long-term commitment and pay for the usage you need.

choices.text: Spot Instances
choices.explanation: They can be interrupted when AWS reclaims capacity, which does not meet the requirement that interruptions are unacceptable.

choices.text: A one-year Compute Savings Plan
choices.explanation: It requires a usage commitment and is not a good fit for a test lasting only 10 days.

choices.text: A one-year Standard Reserved Instance
choices.explanation: Its long-term discount is designed for longer-term usage and does not fit this short, variable usage pattern.

learning.reason: On-Demand Instances let you use EC2 for the time you need without a long-term commitment.
learning.concept: On-Demand usage can still be affected by ordinary failures. It is distinct from a purchasing option that allows interruptions due to Spot capacity reclamation.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Combining long-term EC2 discounts with capacity reservation in a specific AZ
prompt: You plan to use the same EC2 configuration in a specific Availability Zone (AZ) for one year. When your usage meets the requirements, you want a single purchase option to provide a pricing discount and reserve launch capacity in that AZ, without combining it with a separate reservation. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Regional Reserved Instances
choices.explanation: They discount eligible usage but do not also reserve launch capacity in a specific AZ.

choices.text: Compute Savings Plans
choices.explanation: They discount eligible compute usage but do not reserve launch capacity in a specific AZ.

choices.text: On-Demand Capacity Reservations alone
choices.explanation: They reserve capacity in a specific AZ, but on their own they do not provide the long-term Reserved Instance discount.

choices.text: Zonal Reserved Instances
choices.explanation: They provide both the Reserved Instance discount and launch capacity reservation in the specified AZ.

source.label: Amazon EC2 — リージョンとゾーンのリザーブドインスタンス

learning.reason: Choose Zonal Reserved Instances. They apply a discount to eligible usage that matches the specified AZ and also reserve capacity in that AZ.
learning.concept: Regional Reserved Instances can discount eligible usage in a Region, but they do not by themselves reserve capacity in a specific AZ.

sourceLabel: Amazon EC2 — Regional and Zonal Reserved Instances

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Procuring a third-party product for AWS
prompt: A company is looking for third-party monitoring software to use on AWS. It wants to compare features and vendors, then contract for and pay for the selected paid product through AWS's procurement mechanism. Where should it go?

choices.text: AWS Artifact
choices.explanation: It is used to access compliance documents and manage agreements, not to purchase third-party monitoring software.

choices.text: AWS Marketplace
choices.explanation: It is the purchasing channel for discovering third-party products for AWS, subscribing to them, and managing billing.

choices.text: AWS Support Center
choices.explanation: It is used to manage AWS support cases. Managing a catalog or subscriptions for third-party products is not its primary purpose.

choices.text: AWS Cost Explorer
choices.explanation: It can analyze existing costs, but it cannot be used to sign up for or purchase third-party products.

source.label: AWS Marketplace — 製品の購入と支払い

learning.reason: AWS Marketplace lets you find third-party software, subscribe to or purchase eligible products, and manage billing.
learning.concept: Purchasing products is separate from analyzing costs or obtaining compliance documents.

sourceLabel: AWS Marketplace — Purchasing and Paying for Products

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Privately asking about an AWS account bill
prompt: A finance employee wants to ask AWS about line items on an AWS bill. The account has no additional technical support plan, and the billing information must not be posted on a public Q&A forum. Which support channel should they use?

choices.text: Search AWS re:Post for answered billing questions.
choices.explanation: This can help with general billing questions, but it is not a private channel for asking about line items on your own bill.

choices.text: Ask an AWS Marketplace seller about the entire bill.
choices.explanation: You can ask a seller about a product, but the seller is not the support channel for an AWS account bill.

choices.text: Create an account and billing case in AWS Support Center.
choices.explanation: You can submit a billing inquiry even without a technical support plan.

choices.text: Download the bill again in AWS Billing and review its line items.
choices.explanation: Reviewing the line items does not submit a question to AWS about the basis for the charges.

source.label: AWS Billing — 請求と支払いに関するサポート

learning.reason: Create an account and billing support case in AWS Support Center. Billing support is available separately from technical support plans.
learning.concept: Choose the appropriate case type when opening a support case. Use public communities for general questions, not to share account-specific billing information.

sourceLabel: AWS Billing — Support for billing and payments

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Checking when the Free Tier free account plan ends
prompt: A new customer selected the free account plan in the current AWS Free Tier and has not switched to a paid plan. They want to know when the free plan ends so they can review their plans before testing is complete. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: It ends when both the free period has ended and the credits have been used up.
choices.explanation: The free plan ends when the first of these conditions is met, so both do not have to occur.

choices.text: It continues until the free period ends, even if the credits have already been used up.
choices.explanation: If the credits are used up first, the free account plan ends at that point.

choices.text: It continues after the free period ends as long as credits remain.
choices.explanation: Even if credits remain, the plan ends if the free period expires first.

choices.text: It ends at whichever comes first: the end of the free period or the credits being used up.
choices.explanation: Both the duration of the free plan and the available credits have limits.

source.label: AWS Billing — AWS Free Tierの無料プラン

learning.reason: The free plan ends at whichever comes first: the end of the applicable free period or the use of all granted credits.
learning.concept: The current free account plan and the terms offered to new accounts in the past may differ. Check the plan for the account in question.

sourceLabel: AWS Billing — AWS Free Tier free plan

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Estimating data transfer charges for external delivery
prompt: A file delivery service on EC2 stores delivery files on EBS, and many users download large files over the internet. It runs in a single Availability Zone in the same Region and does not use a CDN. Which two items should normally be estimated as direct costs for this configuration, excluding EC2 compute hours?

choices.text: Amazon CloudFront data delivery volume
choices.explanation: This would apply if the configuration used CloudFront, but users access the EC2 origin directly here.

choices.text: Data transferred from EC2 to the internet
choices.explanation: Downloads are data transferred from AWS to the internet, and data transfer out charges can apply depending on usage.

choices.text: Data transferred between EC2 Availability Zones
choices.explanation: This is a consideration when data is transferred between AZs. This configuration uses a single AZ, and that is distinct from delivery over the internet.

choices.text: Data transferred through AWS Direct Connect
choices.explanation: This would apply if the configuration used Direct Connect, but delivery here is over the internet.

choices.text: Capacity allocated to the EBS volume that stores the delivery files
choices.explanation: EBS volume storage is calculated based on provisioned capacity, separately from changes in delivery frequency.

source.label: Amazon EC2のオンデマンド料金

learning.reason: Estimate the amount of data sent to the internet and the storage capacity allocated to EBS for the files.
learning.concept: Separate compute costs, storage costs, and costs based on the network path and direction of data transfer.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Starting application processing near a new market
prompt: A company operates a video conferencing control API in Asia and is starting service in Europe. The control API returns different results for each user, and the company intends to run the processing in Europe. Which cloud approach avoids the time required to procure a local data center?

choices.text: Use another Availability Zone in the current Region in Asia.
choices.explanation: This can help with resilience within the same Region, but it does not move dynamic processing to Europe.

choices.text: Deploy the same application's runtime environment in a European AWS Region.
choices.explanation: The application can process requests in Europe using AWS facilities and services that are already available. The company does not need to build its own facility.

choices.text: Add an edge cache for static files to the runtime environment in Asia.
choices.explanation: This can make static files easier to retrieve from Europe, but processing for the user-specific API remains in the existing Region.

choices.text: Add a DNS record for users in Europe that points to the runtime environment in Asia.
choices.explanation: This changes the name used to connect, but it does not run application processing in Europe.

learning.reason: The company can deploy the existing application configuration in an AWS Region in Europe and move processing closer to its users without setting up its own local facility.
learning.concept: Running dynamic processing in a Region is different from adding an entry point or cache for processing that remains in an existing location.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Make operational settings repeatable
prompt: Applying the same monitoring settings across multiple environments currently requires manual console work, and differences in manual input lead to omissions. Future changes should be reviewed before application and be repeatable. Which improvement does the Well-Architected Framework recommend?

choices.text: Share recordings of the monitoring configuration steps and repeat the same console actions in each environment.
choices.explanation: This makes the steps available to everyone, but leaves room for differences in input and execution.

choices.text: Assign one administrator to enter the monitoring settings for all environments once a week.
choices.explanation: This clarifies ownership, but does not make the process repeatable through automation or allow changes to be reviewed as code.

choices.text: Centrally collect work logs for configuration changes and audit differences after they are applied.
choices.explanation: This can make discrepancies easier to find later, but does not provide a way to review the procedure in advance and reproduce the same actions.

choices.text: Manage operational settings and the steps for applying them as version-controlled code, then execute them after review.
choices.explanation: The application procedure can be shared across environments, enabling review of changes and repeatable execution.

source.label: Well-Architectedのコードとしての運用

learning.reason: Representing operational procedures as code makes changes reviewable and allows the same procedure to be run in each environment.
learning.concept: Distinguish improving records of manual work from turning the work itself into reproducible code.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Make release changes smaller and easier to roll back
prompt: A team releases changes to several features together once a quarter. When a problem occurs, it is difficult to tell which change caused it, and everything must be rolled back. Which release approach makes it easier to isolate the cause and limit the impact of a problem?

choices.text: Extend the testing period and continue releasing approved changes together as before.
choices.explanation: More testing can help detect problems, but the release remains large, making individual changes harder to roll back when something goes wrong.

choices.text: Group all features whose impact is unclear into the next release.
choices.explanation: Introducing uncertain changes at the same time makes it even harder to isolate the cause.

choices.text: Break changes into units that can be tested individually, and prepare a rollback method for each change before release.
choices.explanation: When changes are independent and reversible, the changes associated with an incident can be narrowed down and recovery can limit the impact.

choices.text: Release more frequently, but combine dependent changes without rollback procedures.
choices.explanation: Increasing release frequency alone does not meet the requirement to isolate and roll back individual changes after a failure.

source.label: 運用上の優秀性の設計原則

learning.reason: Frequent, small, reversible changes narrow the scope of impact and make it easier to identify and roll back a failed change.
learning.concept: The size of a change, its dependencies on other changes, and its reversibility all affect incident response.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Compare horizontal and vertical scaling
prompt: A web application that handles independent requests runs on one server. The requirements are to increase processing capacity and to keep accepting requests on the remaining servers if one running server stops. Which approach improves both capacity and availability?

choices.text: Add equivalent application servers and process requests across multiple running servers.
choices.explanation: This increases the capacity available for concurrent processing and allows another server to continue processing if one stops.

choices.text: Increase the CPU and memory of the single server without adding any others.
choices.explanation: This increases capacity vertically, but no server remains to process requests if the single server stops.

choices.text: Keep the current server size and prepare one standby server to start during a failure.
choices.explanation: The standby can support recovery after it starts, but normal processing capacity does not increase, and request handling may be interrupted until startup.

choices.text: Take snapshots of the current server more frequently.
choices.explanation: This provides recovery data, but does not improve processing capacity or request handling immediately after an outage.

learning.reason: Horizontal scaling across multiple running servers adds capacity while reducing dependence on a single processing server.
learning.concept: Adding servers through horizontal scaling differs from increasing the capacity of one server through vertical scaling, including in its effect during a failure.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Use a post-incident analysis to prevent recurrence
prompt: A service outage has been resolved. The team found that monitoring alarms were suppressed during a release and that team members interpreted the procedures differently. Choose two actions that are appropriate for a post-incident analysis aimed at driving future improvements.

choices.text: Record only the first configuration error found as the cause, and omit the detection and response timeline.
choices.explanation: Focusing only on the initial technical cause can miss factors that delayed detection or recovery and opportunities to improve.

choices.text: Document the people involved, the timeline, the impact on users, and how procedures and monitoring affected the outcome.
choices.explanation: This provides a fact-based understanding of multiple contributing factors and helps identify improvements to both technology and operations.

choices.text: Identify the person responsible for the outage and make a warning to that individual the prevention measure.
choices.explanation: Assigning the cause to an individual misses the opportunity to review the monitoring and procedures that allowed the incident to occur.

choices.text: After documenting the timeline, consider the analysis complete once service is restored and leave countermeasures to each team’s discretion.
choices.explanation: The events may be shared, but ownership and completion criteria for improvements remain unclear.

choices.text: Assign an owner and a due date to each alarm or procedure change, then track its completion.
choices.explanation: This puts the analysis into practice and verifies that the measures have been implemented.

source.label: Well-Architectedのインシデント後分析

learning.reason: A post-incident analysis examines the people involved, timeline, impact, and contributing conditions, then tracks improvements with owners and due dates.
learning.concept: The purpose of a post-incident analysis is to learn from an incident and make concrete improvements to detection, response, and prevention.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Validate Cross-Team Incident Coordination Through a Controlled Exercise
prompt: Two operations teams share responsibility for responding to incidents in the same application. They have a short runbook, but have never confirmed whether the contact chain after an alert and the handoff between the teams work. Which approach lets them practice while avoiding impact on production?

choices.text: Have representatives reread the runbook and correct only obvious typos.
choices.explanation: This improves the wording, but does not exercise alert-triggered communication or the handoff between the two teams.

choices.text: Wait for a real incident in production and try the response procedures for the first time then.
choices.explanation: The procedures might be validated in the live environment, but this does not meet the goal of practicing without affecting users.

choices.text: Have each team test its own department's alerts separately, without performing a handoff.
choices.explanation: This can help validate individual detection, but it does not confirm that the cross-team response path works.

choices.text: Simulate an event in an exercise environment and have both teams practice detection, communication, handoff, and recovery verification from start to finish.
choices.explanation: Running the exercise in a controlled setting lets the teams verify and improve their coordination while avoiding impact on production.

learning.reason: A game day recreates a scenario in a controlled environment so teams can assess both the system and the human response procedures at the same time.
learning.concept: Incident detection and team handoffs are difficult to validate through a runbook review or tests of technical components alone.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Set Criteria for Continuing or Reversing a Migration Cutover
prompt: An order-processing system is about to be migrated to AWS. Business data validation and connectivity checks remain on the target environment. If the cutover cannot be completed within the planned window, the team must return to the source environment. How should the team prepare before starting?

choices.text: Record only when the data copy to the target finishes and treat that as completion of the business cutover.
choices.explanation: Finishing the copy does not confirm that the data is ready to be used correctly in business operations.

choices.text: Define order-processing validation, the deadline for deciding whether to continue, the conditions for starting rollback, and the people responsible.
choices.explanation: This makes it possible to decide based on the business state and time remaining, and clarifies who will roll back if validation fails.

choices.text: Shut down the old environment until the cutover is complete, and discuss what to do if validation fails at that point.
choices.explanation: This makes rollback harder and leaves unclear how much time is available to make a decision if the cutover fails.

choices.text: The cutover start conditions are met, so leave business validation to routine monitoring after launch.
choices.explanation: This leaves acceptance criteria to be set before users are switched over, as well as decision criteria in case of failure.

source.label: AWS Prescriptive Guidanceの切り替え段階

learning.reason: Before a migration cutover, define business validation checks, who decides and by when, and the rollback action if acceptance criteria are not met.
learning.concept: Confirming that data has been transferred and confirming that users can be switched over are separate checks.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Reduce Data Storage and Transfer While Meeting Retention Requirements
prompt: An analytics platform must retain every audit detail and be able to recover the same information as in the original. The team wants to reduce transfer volume and storage capacity, but cannot extend the daily processing window. Which improvement is sustainable and meets the business requirements?

choices.text: Sample a fixed proportion of old details and store only the sampled rows.
choices.explanation: This reduces the amount stored, but does not meet the requirement to retain every detail and recover the original information.

choices.text: Choose the setting that produces the smallest compressed size and do not evaluate processing time.
choices.explanation: A high compression ratio may be achieved, but compression and decompression use compute resources, so the team must check whether the time limit can still be met.

choices.text: Evaluate lossless compression and compare storage capacity, transfer volume, and daily processing time.
choices.explanation: This can improve efficiency while preserving the information, and lets the team validate the deadline and additional compute load before choosing an approach.

choices.text: Replicate uncompressed details to multiple storage locations and divide the processing among them.
choices.explanation: This may make parallel processing easier, but replicating the details increases storage capacity and does not reduce transfer volume.

source.label: ファイル形式と圧縮の選択

learning.reason: Evaluate lossless compression, measure the reductions in storage capacity and transfer volume along with the compute load for compression and decompression, and adopt an approach that meets the deadline.
learning.concept: Changes that improve storage and communication efficiency should be assessed alongside their additional compute load and business performance requirements.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Considerations for Establishing a Shared Cloud Foundation
prompt: Several development teams are beginning to use AWS. The technology organization wants to establish a scalable shared cloud foundation and provisioning approach rather than having each team rebuild its own foundation. Which AWS CAF perspective primarily addresses this?

choices.text: Business
choices.explanation: Primarily addresses aligning investments with business outcomes and digital transformation goals.

choices.text: Platform
choices.explanation: Correct. It focuses on building an enterprise-grade, scalable cloud foundation and accelerating workload provisioning.

choices.text: People
choices.explanation: Addresses the organizational culture, roles, skills, and other capabilities needed for transformation.

choices.text: Governance
choices.explanation: Addresses maximizing the value of investments and minimizing transformation risks.

learning.reason: Establishing a shared, scalable foundation to accelerate cloud workload provisioning is the responsibility of the Platform perspective in the CAF.
learning.concept: Each CAF perspective addresses different organizational capabilities and stakeholders.

category: クラウドの概念
title: The CIA of Data and Workloads
prompt: As it migrates to the cloud, a company wants to build its organization-wide ability to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of its data and workloads. Which AWS CAF perspective primarily addresses this?

choices.text: Operations
choices.explanation: This perspective focuses on delivering service levels that meet business needs.

choices.text: Platform
choices.explanation: This perspective focuses on building a scalable hybrid cloud environment.

choices.text: Security
choices.explanation: Correct. This perspective focuses on achieving the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data and cloud workloads.

choices.text: Business
choices.explanation: This perspective aligns cloud investments with business transformation goals and outcomes.

learning.reason: Achieving confidentiality, integrity, and availability (CIA) is a core objective of the CAF Security perspective.
learning.concept: CAF Security addresses organization-wide security capabilities, not just individual product settings.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Defining the Target State for Cloud Transformation
prompt: Before beginning cloud adoption, executives want to clarify the business outcomes they seek and the future target state, then align stakeholders on the direction. Which AWS CAF transformation phase is most appropriate?

choices.text: Envision
choices.explanation: Correct. This phase defines the outcomes and target state for cloud transformation.

choices.text: Align
choices.explanation: This phase identifies capability gaps, cross-organizational dependencies, and stakeholder concerns.

choices.text: Launch
choices.explanation: This phase delivers production pilots and demonstrates incremental business value.

choices.text: Scale
choices.explanation: This phase expands proven production pilots and business value to the desired scale.

source.label: AWS CAF cloud operating model journey

learning.reason: Envision clarifies the target state and desired outcomes of cloud transformation before assessing the organization's current state.
learning.concept: The CAF phases treat envisioning, aligning capabilities, demonstrating value, and scaling results as distinct steps.

sourceLabel: AWS CAF cloud operating model journey

category: クラウドの概念
title: Identifying Capability Gaps and Dependencies
prompt: The organization has agreed on its target state for cloud transformation. Next, it wants to identify and prioritize current capability gaps across the six CAF perspectives, cross-department dependencies, and stakeholder concerns. Which phase is most appropriate?

choices.text: Envision
choices.explanation: This phase defines the target state and desired business outcomes; detailed capability-gap analysis is not its primary focus.

choices.text: Launch
choices.explanation: This phase delivers production pilots and demonstrates incremental value.

choices.text: Scale
choices.explanation: This phase expands proven pilots and business value while sustaining the outcomes.

choices.text: Align
choices.explanation: Correct. This phase identifies capability gaps across the six perspectives, cross-organizational dependencies, and stakeholder concerns.

source.label: AWS CAF cloud operating model journey

learning.reason: Align connects the target state to current capabilities by identifying gaps and dependencies and setting priorities for addressing them.
learning.concept: Piloting is the purpose of Launch, and expanding proven results is the purpose of Scale; both differ from Align.

sourceLabel: AWS CAF cloud operating model journey

category: クラウドの概念
title: Scaling Proven Value
prompt: A production pilot has demonstrated business value, and operating procedures are in place. The organization wants to expand to more departments and sustain the value of its cloud investment at the desired scale. Which AWS CAF transformation phase is most appropriate?

choices.text: Envision
choices.explanation: This is the initial phase in which the target state and business outcomes are defined.

choices.text: Align
choices.explanation: This phase identifies capability gaps and cross-organizational dependencies.

choices.text: Scale
choices.explanation: Correct. This phase expands proven production pilots and business value while sustaining the outcomes.

choices.text: Launch
choices.explanation: This phase demonstrates incremental value through high-impact production pilots.

source.label: AWS CAF cloud operating model journey

learning.reason: Scale builds on successful pilots to expand production use and business value to the desired scale and sustain the results.
learning.concept: Launch demonstrates value through pilots; Scale expands that proven value.

sourceLabel: AWS CAF cloud operating model journey

category: クラウドの概念
title: Migration strategy for moving an entire virtualization environment
prompt: A company wants to move many servers on a virtualization platform together to a cloud environment that uses the same virtualization platform. It wants to preserve the way it operates the existing virtualized environment rather than rebuild individual servers on a different runtime platform. Which of the 7 Rs does this strategy represent?

choices.text: Rehost
choices.explanation: This strategy moves servers with few changes, but the scenario describes moving the entire virtualization environment to a cloud environment on the same platform, not moving individual servers.

choices.text: Relocate
choices.explanation: Correct. This strategy moves an application to the cloud version of its platform without changing its overall architecture.

choices.text: Repurchase
choices.explanation: This strategy replaces existing software with a different product, usually SaaS.

choices.text: Retain
choices.explanation: This strategy leaves the application in the source environment for now because it is not ready to migrate.

source.label: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: About the migration strategies

learning.reason: Relocate is a 7 Rs strategy for moving to the cloud version of a platform without substantially changing the application or its operations.
learning.concept: Relocate differs from replacing an application with SaaS or redesigning it.

sourceLabel: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: About the migration strategies

category: クラウドの概念
title: Migration strategy for deferring a move for now
prompt: A business application is needed, but its dependent core system must be migrated first. Until the conditions for running the same business operations in the cloud are in place, the application will continue running in its current environment rather than be retired. Which 7 Rs migration strategy applies at this time?

choices.text: Retire
choices.explanation: This strategy ends use of the application and retires or archives it.

choices.text: Rehost
choices.explanation: This strategy moves the current application to the cloud with few changes.

choices.text: Repurchase
choices.explanation: This strategy replaces an existing product with a different one.

choices.text: Retain
choices.explanation: Correct. This strategy keeps an application in the source environment for now because it is not ready to migrate, has dependencies, or must meet requirements.

source.label: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: About the migration strategies

learning.reason: Retain means deferring migration and keeping the application in the source environment, rather than deciding that it is no longer needed and retiring it.
learning.concept: Dependencies and compliance requirements are common reasons to choose Retain.

sourceLabel: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: About the migration strategies

category: クラウドの概念
title: Replacing existing software with SaaS
prompt: A company’s self-managed expense-management package is due for an upgrade, so the company wants to switch its contract to a SaaS product that provides the same business function. It will no longer operate an expense-management server itself. Which of the 7 Rs migration strategies applies?

choices.text: Repurchase
choices.explanation: Correct. This strategy replaces existing commercial software with a different product, such as SaaS.

choices.text: Relocate
choices.explanation: This strategy moves an existing application to the cloud version of its platform without replacing the product.

choices.text: Replatform
choices.explanation: This strategy keeps the existing application while moving it to managed cloud services or otherwise optimizing it.

choices.text: Retain
choices.explanation: This strategy keeps the application in the existing environment for now; it does not switch products.

source.label: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: About the migration strategies

learning.reason: Repurchase, also known as drop and shop, replaces an existing application with a new product or SaaS that provides equivalent business functionality instead of migrating the application itself.
learning.concept: The 7 Rs decision depends on whether the existing product is kept or replaced, not on whether the destination runs on AWS.

sourceLabel: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: About the migration strategies

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Providing AWS credentials only to authenticated application users
prompt: A mobile application lets users sign in with an existing external identity provider. The application needs to access user data on AWS directly, so it must issue short-term AWS credentials that the application can use to signed-in users. Which approach does this without storing long-term keys in the application or operating a custom credential-issuing service?

choices.text: Use only an Amazon Cognito user pool.
choices.explanation: A user pool can provide sign-in and token issuance, but user-pool tokens alone are not AWS credentials for an IAM role.

choices.text: Store long-term AWS access keys in Secrets Manager and give the same keys to every application.
choices.explanation: Changing where the keys are stored still means using long-term keys in the application, not limited-duration credentials scoped to each user.

choices.text: Register each application user as a workforce user in AWS IAM Identity Center.
choices.explanation: This is suited to workforce users signing in to AWS accounts or applications in an organization. It differs from the role of an identity pool in providing short-term AWS credentials to a customer application through existing external identities.

choices.text: Federate an Amazon Cognito identity pool with the existing identity provider.
choices.explanation: It can associate authenticated users with a defined IAM role and issue temporary AWS credentials.

learning.reason: A Cognito identity pool can use tokens from a federated identity provider to issue temporary AWS credentials for the corresponding IAM role.
learning.concept: The mechanism that authenticates users differs from the mechanism that issues credentials for AWS APIs.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Distinguishing keys with customer-defined policies from keys managed by AWS
prompt: An AWS service supports both AWS owned keys and customer managed keys for encryption. For an audit in environment A, your organization must define the policy for the key used for reads and audit key usage. Environment B uses the default encryption provided by AWS and must not require key management or incur charges for a dedicated key. Choose two appropriate combinations.

choices.text: Use an AWS owned key in environment A and change its key policy.
choices.explanation: AWS owned keys are managed on the service side, and customers cannot change their key policies.

choices.text: Use a customer managed key in environment A and manage its key policy.
choices.explanation: Your organization can manage access to a KMS key it created and audit key operations in CloudTrail.

choices.text: Use an AWS managed key in environment A and change its key policy yourself.
choices.explanation: You can audit the use of an AWS managed key, but customers cannot change its key policy.

choices.text: Create a customer managed key in environment B, assuming no key management is required.
choices.explanation: Your organization manages the permissions and lifecycle of a customer managed key, and charges typically apply for the key and its use.

choices.text: Use an AWS owned key in environment B and let the service manage the key operations.
choices.explanation: AWS manages the key. Customers do not create or manage it, and AWS owned keys themselves incur no charge.

learning.reason: Use a customer managed key in environment A because your organization needs to define its policy and audit key usage. Environment B can use a supported AWS owned key to leave key management to the service.
learning.concept: Distinguish AWS owned, AWS managed, and customer managed keys by where they are owned and who can change their policies.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Preventing public access to S3 buckets at the account level
prompt: An AWS account is dedicated to internal documents. Public access must be prevented for existing S3 buckets and any buckets created in the future. The goal is to avoid relying on each bucket owner to remember to configure the setting, while still allowing normal authenticated business access. Which setting is the most direct solution?

choices.text: Enable all S3 Block Public Access settings at the account level.
choices.explanation: The account-level settings also apply when new buckets are created and prevent public access settings.

choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer external access analysis to inspect public settings.
choices.explanation: It can detect sharing outside the intended scope, but its findings alone do not prevent public access from being enabled.

choices.text: Configure server-side encryption for all buckets.
choices.explanation: This encrypts data at rest, but is separate from whether read access from S3 has been made public.

choices.text: Add a rule to each bucket to inspect existing public access and notify you only if a setting is found.
choices.explanation: This can be used for monitoring, but it is not an account-level setting that prevents public access, including for new buckets.

learning.reason: Enabling S3 Block Public Access at the account level can prevent settings that allow public access from being created or enabled for the account's buckets.
learning.concept: Detecting an existing sharing state and preventing public access from being enabled are different controls.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Evaluating the first matching rule in a network ACL
prompt: An inbound network ACL associated with a VPC subnet has a rule numbered 100 that allows an IP range and a rule numbered 110 that denies a narrower IP range. No other rule with a lower number matches. The denied IP range is entirely within the allowed range, and the port and protocol conditions are the same. How will the ACL handle inbound traffic that matches both rules?

choices.text: It will deny the traffic because a deny rule exists, regardless of rule number.
choices.explanation: A network ACL does not collect all matching rules and give deny rules priority.

choices.text: It will deny the traffic because rule 110 is more specific due to its narrower IP range.
choices.explanation: Rules are evaluated by number, not by how specific their IP ranges are.

choices.text: It will allow the traffic because rule 100 matches first.
choices.explanation: Rule 100 is applied first, and rule 110 is not evaluated for this traffic.

choices.text: Because both allow and deny rules match, neither will apply and the default deny will take effect.
choices.explanation: A match on both rules is not treated as a conflict. The first matching rule determines the result.

source.label: VPCネットワークACLのルール評価

learning.reason: A network ACL evaluates rules in ascending numerical order and applies the first matching rule.
learning.concept: Explicit deny evaluation in IAM policies differs from network ACL evaluation by rule number.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Using individual access and audit trails for routine administration
prompt: Immediately after an AWS account is created, several operators change AWS service settings every day. Which access method is most appropriate to distinguish each operator during an audit and avoid using the account's root user for routine work?

choices.text: Share one IAM user among everyone and have the operator on duty record their name in a separate log before working.
choices.explanation: This avoids routine use of the root user, but AWS records will not identify which individual performed an operation.

choices.text: Use per-person federated authentication and assume IAM roles with permissions needed for each job.
choices.explanation: Individual authentication can provide short-term access suited to each job, with a configuration that lets you trace the operator from the session.

choices.text: For each change, have the operator borrow root credentials from an approver and record the reason for the operation.
choices.explanation: An approval process can be established, but this does not meet the requirement to avoid using the root user for routine changes.

choices.text: Give each operator the same long-term access key on their device and register it under a different alias.
choices.explanation: Adding a different alias on each device does not change the shared credentials, so AWS records cannot distinguish the operators.

source.label: AWS IAM: root user best practices

learning.reason: AWS recommends not using the root user for routine tasks and using individual access with permissions suited to each role.
learning.concept: Root-only tasks, routine operations, access approval, and individual attribution are distinct concerns.

sourceLabel: AWS IAM: root user best practices

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Evaluate an Allow and an Explicit Deny for the Same Action
prompt: In the same AWS account, an identity-based policy attached to an IAM role allows listing a business S3 bucket. Another applicable policy explicitly denies the same action on the same bucket. How will IAM evaluate the role's attempt to list the bucket?

choices.text: Allow the request because one applicable policy grants permission, which takes precedence over the deny.
choices.explanation: For an allow to take effect, there must be no applicable explicit deny.

choices.text: Allow the request because the listing permission is specific and overrides an explicit deny on the same resource.
choices.explanation: Even a narrowly scoped allow does not override an explicit deny that applies to the same request.

choices.text: Deny the listing request because an applicable explicit deny takes precedence.
choices.explanation: An explicit deny that applies to the request takes precedence even when an allow also applies to the same action.

choices.text: Use the statement in the policy with the more recent update time to decide the request.
choices.explanation: IAM does not determine precedence between allows and denies based on when a policy was created or updated.

learning.reason: In IAM evaluation, an explicit deny that applies to the request takes precedence over an allow.
learning.concept: Policy evaluation considers applicability and explicit denies. When multiple documents apply, their creation order does not determine the result.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Accept an Applicable AWS Agreement for an Organization
prompt: A legal team wants to accept an applicable agreement offered by AWS for the entire organization from the AWS Organizations management account. Separately from obtaining AWS SOC reports, which screen lets the team select the applicable organizational agreement and manage its acceptance status?

choices.text: The Reports screen in AWS Artifact
choices.explanation: It provides access to reports from third-party audits, but it is not the screen for changing an organization's agreement acceptance status.

choices.text: The subscription management screen in AWS Marketplace
choices.explanation: It can be used for subscriptions to procured products, but it does not handle organizational agreements that AWS provides through Artifact.

choices.text: The consolidated billing screen in AWS Organizations
choices.explanation: It is used for billing across organization accounts, but it does not accept applicable agreements in AWS Artifact.

choices.text: The AWS Artifact Agreements screen for agreements enabled for the organization
choices.explanation: With the required permissions, the management account can accept and manage the applicable agreement for the organization.

source.label: AWSとの対象契約を組織単位で受諾する

learning.reason: AWS Artifact Agreements lets you accept and manage applicable agreements with AWS at the account or organization level.
learning.concept: Obtaining AWS audit reports as evidence and accepting an agreement are separate functions.

sourceLabel: Accept an Applicable AWS Agreement for an Organization

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Granting a Role in Another Account Access from the Bucket Owner's Side
prompt: The owner of a business S3 bucket wants to allow a data analysis role in another AWS account to read S3 objects under a specific prefix. Assuming the necessary permissions are also configured in the account that reads the objects, where should the bucket owner specify the permission for the role and action?

choices.text: Only in an identity-based policy attached to the role in the reading account
choices.explanation: This can grant permissions on the reader's side, but the bucket owner's requirement to authorize the external role remains.

choices.text: In the bucket's resource-based policy
choices.explanation: A bucket policy can name the external role as the principal and specify the object prefix and actions.

choices.text: In the trust policy of the role in the reading account
choices.explanation: It defines who can assume the role, but it does not grant the bucket owner's permission to access S3.

choices.text: In an AWS Organizations service control policy
choices.explanation: It can set permission guardrails for accounts, but it does not grant the external role access to this bucket.

learning.reason: The bucket owner can use a resource-based bucket policy to specify the external principal, permitted S3 actions, and object scope.
learning.concept: For cross-account access, check both the caller's permissions and the permissions granted by the resource owner.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Check Policy Syntax and Quality Before Applying It
prompt: An operations team is reviewing an IAM policy that is still in draft. They want to find warnings against AWS policy grammar and best practices, not merely confirm that it is valid JSON. They will later simulate whether a specific user is allowed to perform an action. Which tool should they use first?

choices.text: Policy validation in IAM Access Analyzer
choices.explanation: It checks policy grammar and AWS best practices and reports findings such as issues and warnings.

choices.text: The IAM policy simulator to evaluate a single S3 action
choices.explanation: It can test whether a specified action is allowed or denied, but that is different from the comprehensive grammar and best-practice validation requested here.

choices.text: External access findings in IAM Access Analyzer
choices.explanation: They can reveal external sharing of existing resources, but they do not validate the grammar of a policy before it is applied.

choices.text: Search recent policy changes in AWS CloudTrail management events
choices.explanation: It can show past changes, but it does not evaluate the grammar of a policy draft that is about to be applied.

source.label: AWS IAM Access Analyzer: policy validation

learning.reason: Access Analyzer policy validation checks grammar and best practices and returns findings.
learning.concept: Distinguish reviewing syntax and configuration, simulating a specified request, and detecting external access after a policy is applied.

sourceLabel: AWS IAM Access Analyzer: policy validation

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Audit S3 object reads and writes separately from bucket settings
prompt: The audit team uses CloudTrail to record management events related to existing bucket settings. For a specific bucket, it also wants to track operations that read objects through the AWS API and operations that save new objects. Which additional configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Enable only write management events in CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: This can capture configuration changes, but object reads and writes are data events and are not captured by management events alone.

choices.text: Enable S3 Versioning on the target bucket.
choices.explanation: This helps retain previous versions, but it does not record who read an object.

choices.text: Use AWS Config to record bucket configuration changes.
choices.explanation: This can show changes to bucket settings, but it is not an audit log of object API reads and writes.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail to record both read and write data events for the target S3 objects.
choices.explanation: In addition to resource configuration, this lets the team audit API activity involving the objects.

learning.reason: S3 object operations such as GetObject and PutObject can be recorded as CloudTrail data events. Configure the target resources and select both read and write events.
learning.concept: Distinguish operations that manage an AWS resource’s configuration from operations on data inside that resource.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Renew an external CA certificate while preserving existing associations
prompt: An application imports a TLS certificate issued by an external certificate authority into AWS Certificate Manager and associates it with an ALB. The company wants to continue using the externally issued certificate, renew it before it expires, and keep the same ACM ARN and ALB association. What should it do?

choices.text: Add the domain validation CNAME and wait for ACM to renew the externally issued certificate automatically.
choices.explanation: Unlike eligible certificates issued by ACM, imported certificates are not covered by ACM managed renewal.

choices.text: Import the renewed certificate as a new certificate.
choices.explanation: A new import creates a different ARN, so this does not meet the requirement to preserve the existing ARN.

choices.text: Renew the certificate with the external certificate authority and reimport it into the existing ACM certificate.
choices.explanation: Reimporting a renewed certificate that meets the requirements into the same ACM resource preserves its ARN and associations.

choices.text: Remove the certificate from the ALB listener, then select the same external certificate again.
choices.explanation: Changing the association does not renew the expiration date of a certificate issued by an external certificate authority.

learning.reason: ACM does not automatically renew imported certificates. Renew the certificate externally and reimport it into the existing resource to preserve its associations with services.
learning.concept: The party responsible for renewal and the renewal procedure depend on whether ACM or an external certificate authority issued the certificate.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Create a hierarchy of account groups by department
prompt: A company wants to group its Logistics and Sales accounts within the same AWS Organization, then separate development and production accounts under each department. Which structure lets the company classify accounts hierarchically, apply governance policies by group, and do so without moving AWS resources?

choices.text: Tags on accounts in AWS Organizations
choices.explanation: Tags can classify attributes, but they do not create parent-child account groups.

choices.text: Use only the root in AWS Organizations.
choices.explanation: The root groups the organization at the top level, but additional structures are needed to group accounts by department and environment.

choices.text: IAM user groups
choices.explanation: These group IAM users; they are not a unit for arranging organization accounts hierarchically.

choices.text: Organizational units (OUs)
choices.explanation: OUs can contain AWS accounts and child OUs, and policies can be applied to OUs to define their scope.

learning.reason: OUs are the unit AWS Organizations uses to group accounts hierarchically, and organizational policies can be applied to a target OU.
learning.concept: Distinguish grouping items into a unit from deciding which policies apply to that unit.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Set separate security and billing contacts
prompt: A company is keeping the primary email address for its AWS account. It wants important security notifications from AWS to go to its security team and billing communications to go to its accounting team. Select two actions that can be taken through AWS account contacts, rather than service-specific alarm settings.

choices.text: Set the security team as the alternate security contact.
choices.explanation: A security contact for communications from AWS can be specified separately from the primary email address.

choices.text: Have the security and accounting teams share the root login for all account notifications.
choices.explanation: This does not specify contacts by notification type and does not meet the requirement to keep the primary address while separating responsibilities.

choices.text: Set the accounting team as the alternate billing contact.
choices.explanation: A contact can be registered to handle AWS communications about billing.

choices.text: Change the notification recipient for Amazon CloudWatch alarms to the accounting team.
choices.explanation: This changes the recipient for configured monitoring alarms, but it does not set an AWS account billing contact.

choices.text: Move the account into a security OU in AWS Organizations.
choices.explanation: This classifies the account but does not set contacts by communication type.

source.label: セキュリティと請求の連絡先を別々に指定する

learning.reason: Alternate contacts for an AWS account can be specified for billing, operations, and security.
learning.concept: Distinguish the account’s primary contact, purpose-specific alternate contacts, and workload notification recipients.

sourceLabel: Set separate security and billing contacts

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Maintain shared web protection rules through provider updates
prompt: A team wants to add baseline rules for common web threats to AWS WAF to protect a public website. They want to reduce the effort of writing every rule from scratch and maintaining the rule set themselves. Which feature should they use?

choices.text: Design all individual AWS WAF rules in-house and group them into a rule group.
choices.explanation: This supports custom requirements, but the team remains responsible for creating and maintaining the baseline individual rules.

choices.text: Create a new Web ACL in AWS WAF without adding any rules.
choices.explanation: This provides a container for configuring evaluations, but no common protection rules are applied yet.

choices.text: Add an AWS Managed Rules rule group to the Web ACL in AWS WAF.
choices.explanation: This lets the team use common rules managed by the provider and apply a group suited to its needs.

choices.text: Enable AWS Firewall Manager and defer creating Web ACL rules.
choices.explanation: This helps govern multiple accounts, but this choice does not configure any shared AWS-managed rules to use.

learning.reason: AWS Managed Rules lets you add AWS-managed rule groups to a Web ACL and leave maintenance of the baseline rules to the provider.
learning.concept: Distinguish the feature that evaluates rules, the provision and maintenance of rules, and deployment across multiple accounts.

sourceLabel: AWS Managed Rules for AWS WAF

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Centrally manage root credentials in member accounts
prompt: An AWS Organizations administrator does not want long-term root credentials to remain in member accounts. When needed, a central administrator will perform root-only actions using a short-term session. Which option is appropriate if the target accounts support it?

choices.text: Register multi-factor authentication for each root user and keep the root password in each member account.
choices.explanation: This strengthens authentication, but retains long-term root credentials in the member accounts.

choices.text: Centrally manage member account root access in the organization and delete the applicable root credentials.
choices.explanation: For supported root-only tasks, a restricted short-term session can be started centrally.

choices.text: Assign AdministratorAccess to an IAM group in every account.
choices.explanation: This can be used for administrative tasks permitted through regular IAM, but it cannot perform root-only tasks or eliminate root credentials.

choices.text: Apply a cost-monitoring SCP to the member accounts.
choices.explanation: This can set permission boundaries for accounts, but does not provide a way to avoid retaining root credentials.

source.label: IAMのルートアクセスの一元管理

learning.reason: Enabling centralized root access lets you manage member account root credentials and use privileged sessions for permitted root-only tasks.
learning.concept: Distinguish operations that retain long-term root credentials from operations that use organization-provided privileges only for necessary tasks.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Decrypt older ciphertext after automatic key rotation
prompt: A team encrypts stored documents with a supported symmetric customer managed key for which AWS KMS generated the key material. Automatic rotation is enabled for the same KMS key. The key remains enabled, and access permissions remain unchanged. Which statement is correct about documents encrypted with older key material?

choices.text: Rotation deletes the previous key material, so past documents can no longer be decrypted.
choices.explanation: KMS does not delete previous material during rotation, and existing ciphertext can still be decrypted.

choices.text: Users must specify the ID of the previous key material each time they decrypt.
choices.explanation: Users do not select the key material; AWS KMS uses the required material.

choices.text: When rotation occurs, AWS KMS re-encrypts existing documents in bulk with the latest key material.
choices.explanation: Rotation does not rewrite existing ciphertext. New encryption operations use the new material.

choices.text: AWS KMS can use older key material to decrypt previous ciphertext.
choices.explanation: Past key material for the same KMS key is retained for decryption.

source.label: AWS KMSのキーローテーション

learning.reason: AWS KMS retains a key's previous key material and uses the appropriate material to decrypt data encrypted with that key.
learning.concept: Distinguish updating key material for the same key from migrating ciphertext to a different key.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Forward authentication to an existing directory
prompt: A company wants users from its existing on-premises Microsoft Active Directory to sign in to supported AWS business applications. It does not want to copy users to a new directory and wants AWS authentication requests forwarded to the existing directory. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Connect AWS Directory Service AD Connector to the existing directory.
choices.explanation: It forwards requests from supported services to the existing Active Directory, without requiring user information to be copied to the cloud.

choices.text: Create a new, unconnected directory with AWS Managed Microsoft AD.
choices.explanation: This delegates management of a new domain, but forwarding requests to the existing directory is not part of this configuration.

choices.text: Migrate the existing users to an Amazon Cognito user pool.
choices.explanation: This can configure a user directory for customer-facing applications, but it does not forward directory requests directly to the existing AD.

choices.text: Create existing AD users as IAM users in each AWS account.
choices.explanation: This requires creating new IAM identities and does not meet the requirement to forward authentication to the existing directory.

learning.reason: AD Connector redirects directory requests from supported AWS services to an existing Microsoft Active Directory.
learning.concept: Distinguish providing a new managed directory from forwarding requests to an existing directory.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Restore an S3 object hidden by a delete marker
prompt: In a bucket with S3 Versioning enabled, an operator deleted a document without specifying a version ID. The delete marker is the latest version, and the immediately preceding document version still exists. What should the operator do to make that same document version readable again by specifying only its usual key?

choices.text: Specify the preceding document version that remains and delete that version itself.
choices.explanation: This would delete the required data version and would not remove the delete marker.

choices.text: Delete the same object key again without specifying a version ID.
choices.explanation: The current delete marker remains, and deleting an object without a version ID in a versioning-enabled bucket creates another delete marker.

choices.text: Specify the version ID of the latest delete marker and delete only that marker.
choices.explanation: The existing data version behind the latest marker can then be retrieved again by specifying only its usual key.

choices.text: Suspend versioning on the bucket.
choices.explanation: This changes future behavior but does not delete the latest delete marker that already exists.

learning.reason: Deleting the latest delete marker by its version ID makes the preceding data version that remains the latest version.
learning.concept: Distinguish a delete marker for an object key from permanently deleting a version that contains the object data.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Identify the role an AWS service uses to operate other services
prompt: An operations team uses Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling.
