During an audit, the team learned that, separately from the application's role, there is a role used when Auto Scaling itself launches instances. Which type of IAM role is directly associated with an AWS service and is normally assumed by that service?

choices.text: An application role assigned to an EC2 instance profile
choices.explanation: This role lets an application on an instance perform AWS operations after launch; its purpose differs from a role used by the Auto Scaling service itself to launch instances.

choices.text: A service-linked role
choices.explanation: A service-linked role is associated with an AWS service and grants the permissions that service needs to perform AWS operations.

choices.text: A permissions policy assigned to an IAM group
choices.explanation: This can group permissions for IAM users, but it is not a role assumed by a service.

choices.text: An AWS Organizations service control policy
choices.explanation: This policy sets a permissions boundary for member accounts; it is not a mechanism for a service to assume a role.

source.label: IAMのサービスにリンクされたロール

learning.reason: A service-linked role is directly associated with an AWS service and provides permissions for the service to operate on other AWS resources.
learning.concept: Distinguish a role that grants permissions to an application on an instance from a service-linked role used by an AWS service.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Run existing Spark jobs on an AWS-managed platform
prompt: A data analytics team analyzes a large volume of events overnight using existing jobs that incorporate Spark libraries and processing. The team wants to reduce the effort of building and managing a distributed processing platform while keeping its Spark execution approach. Which service is appropriate?

choices.text: Run SQL queries on stored data with Amazon Athena.
choices.explanation: This supports SQL queries, but it does not run the existing Spark jobs as-is.

choices.text: Run Apache Spark jobs with Amazon EMR.
choices.explanation: The team can move Spark jobs to a managed execution environment on AWS.

choices.text: Register table definitions in the AWS Glue Data Catalog.
choices.explanation: This organizes metadata, but the Data Catalog alone does not run Spark processing.

choices.text: Load aggregated data into Amazon Redshift.
choices.explanation: The team can analyze aggregated data with SQL, but this option does not run the existing Spark processing.

learning.reason: Amazon EMR provides a managed platform for running distributed processing frameworks such as Apache Spark.
learning.concept: Distinguish querying stored data with SQL from running existing distributed processing jobs.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Share a dashboard for exploring aggregated data
prompt: A company already has sales data in Amazon Redshift. The sales department wants to share a business dashboard that lets users view charts in a browser and change the time period or region on screen. Which option meets this requirement without the company providing its own dashboard server?

choices.text: Store the business data in Amazon Redshift and give viewers access to a SQL editor.
choices.explanation: Users can query the data, but this does not meet the requirement for a shared BI dashboard where they can interactively change the time period or region.

choices.text: Register the source data definitions in the AWS Glue Data Catalog.
choices.explanation: This manages data structure but does not provide charts or a viewer-facing interface.

choices.text: Connect Quick Sight in AWS Quick to Redshift and publish a dashboard.
choices.explanation: This can visualize sales data in Redshift and share a dashboard that lets users change parameters on screen.

choices.text: Run monthly aggregations from Amazon Athena and distribute CSV files to stakeholders.
choices.explanation: This shares aggregated results, but it does not provide a dashboard where viewers can change the time period or region in a browser.

learning.reason: Quick Sight in AWS Quick can connect to supported data sources and create and share interactive BI dashboards.
learning.concept: Distinguish a platform for storing analytics data from a BI interface where viewers can interact with charts and filters.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Search Internal Articles and Rank Results by Relevance
prompt: An editorial team's business portal needs to search the titles and bodies of published articles. Search should find candidate documents based on their words and rank them by relevance without rereading each document's body from scratch for every search. Which service provides a managed search index?

choices.text: Search for article IDs using Amazon DynamoDB primary keys.
choices.explanation: This is suitable for retrieving an item directly when its article ID is known, but it does not find documents by words in their bodies and rank them by relevance.

choices.text: Register the data types of article bodies in the AWS Glue Data Catalog.
choices.explanation: This can manage table structures and column definitions, but it does not provide an index for document search or relevance-ranked results.

choices.text: Store article files in Amazon S3 and list them by object name.
choices.explanation: S3 can store the files, but listing objects does not index words in their stored bodies.

choices.text: Index the articles in Amazon OpenSearch Service.
choices.explanation: It can index document text and return results based on search terms and relevance.

learning.reason: OpenSearch Service provides a foundation for indexing documents, performing full-text searches, and retrieving results by relevance.
learning.concept: Direct retrieval by a known key, ad hoc analytical queries, and index-based full-text search are different operations.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Collect Missing Booking Details Through a Conversation
prompt: A facility booking site needs a chat feature that lets users describe what they want in everyday language. It must determine whether a user wants to make a new booking or change one, and ask a follow-up question in the conversation if the time is missing. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Define intents and slots in Amazon Lex.
choices.explanation: It can determine the user's intent from an utterance, ask for missing slots, and pass the information to booking processing.

choices.text: Classify the sentiment of input text with Amazon Comprehend.
choices.explanation: It can analyze sentiment and terms, but it does not manage the conversational state needed to collect booking details.

choices.text: Turn booking instructions into speech with Amazon Polly.
choices.explanation: It can provide spoken guidance, but it does not control a conversation that identifies new bookings or changes and asks for missing information.

choices.text: Translate input into a standard language with Amazon Translate.
choices.explanation: It can standardize the language, but another mechanism is needed to determine intent and collect the required booking details through a conversation.

learning.reason: Amazon Lex can determine intent from a conversation and interactively collect required details such as a booking time.
learning.concept: The requirement is to manage a conversation that asks for missing details based on intent, not merely classify text.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Generate Narration from Article Text
prompt: A website already has an approved article in Japanese. It wants to publish Japanese narration audio without having a narrator rerecord the article every time its text is edited. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Submit the script to Amazon Transcribe to convert it into audio.
choices.explanation: Transcribe recognizes speech and turns it into text; it does not create speech from text.

choices.text: Send the Japanese text to Amazon Translate and translate it into Japanese.
choices.explanation: This service translates text between supported languages; its output is not narrated audio.

choices.text: Send the text to Amazon Polly to synthesize Japanese speech.
choices.explanation: A Japanese voice can be selected to generate narration audio from the updated text.

choices.text: Define a conversation intent for each article in Amazon Lex.
choices.explanation: This is for responding to conversational choices; it is not a direct way to generate audio for each article from its existing full text.

learning.reason: Amazon Polly converts input text into synthesized speech in supported languages.
learning.concept: Transcription converts speech into text, while text-to-speech creates audio from input text.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Aggregate Written Customer Reviews by Sentiment
prompt: A retailer already stores product reviews as text. It wants to automatically classify reviews in supported languages as positive, negative, neutral, and so on, and use the results for aggregation. Which service can do this without the company training its own machine learning model?

choices.text: Translate the reviews with Amazon Translate.
choices.explanation: It can translate between languages, but it does not return sentiment labels for each document.

choices.text: Define a conversational interface for inquiries in Amazon Lex.
choices.explanation: It can recognize user intent and conduct conversations, but that is different from classifying stored reviews by sentiment in batches.

choices.text: Transcribe the reviews with Amazon Transcribe.
choices.explanation: It converts speech to text, while the input is already text.

choices.text: Use sentiment detection in Amazon Comprehend.
choices.explanation: Its managed natural language processing can classify document sentiment, and the results can be used for aggregation.

learning.reason: Amazon Comprehend can detect document sentiment using natural language processing.
learning.concept: Data conversion, conversational intent detection, and sentiment analysis of written text serve different purposes.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Receive telemetry from remote equipment with device-level authentication
prompt: Measurement devices in many warehouses send data over MQTT. On the cloud side, you need to authenticate each device with a different certificate and pass the received messages to downstream services. Which approach avoids operating your own MQTT server?

choices.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams as the direct MQTT endpoint.
choices.explanation: It can support downstream stream processing, but it does not provide a managed MQTT broker for devices to connect to directly.

choices.text: Authenticate devices with AWS IoT Core and route the received messages using rules.
choices.explanation: It supports MQTT and lets you configure device-level authentication and processing after messages are received.

choices.text: Expose an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API as the MQTT endpoint.
choices.explanation: It can expose APIs over HTTP, but it is not a broker that accepts the specified MQTT connections from devices.

choices.text: Have each device connect to an Amazon EventBridge event bus over MQTT.
choices.explanation: It can route events after they are received, but it is not an entry point that accepts MQTT connections from devices.

learning.reason: AWS IoT Core accepts MQTT messages, supports device-level authentication, and uses its rules engine to route messages to downstream services.
learning.concept: Distinguish the endpoint that devices connect to and authenticate with directly from services that analyze data after it has been received.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Find recommendation candidates by traversing multistep relationships
prompt: A social networking service stores users’ friendships and shared activities. For recommendations, it needs to traverse multistep relationships, such as friends of friends and shared activities. Which managed database places relationships at the center of its data model?

choices.text: Amazon DocumentDB
choices.explanation: It is suited to flexible document data, but it is not a graph database centered on queries that traverse relationships.

choices.text: Amazon Neptune
choices.explanation: It stores graphs in which users and activities are vertices and friendships and other relationships are edges, and it supports queries that traverse those relationships.

choices.text: Amazon DynamoDB
choices.explanation: It can provide fast key-based retrieval, but the service in this choice does not offer a graph query engine for traversing relationships.

choices.text: Amazon RDS for MySQL
choices.explanation: Tables and joins can represent relationships, but it is not a graph-specific database suited to this purpose.

learning.reason: Amazon Neptune is a managed graph database for data with multiple kinds of relationships.
learning.concept: Retrieval by a known key, joins between tables, and graph relationship traversal are different access patterns.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Use a managed document database for a MongoDB-compatible application
prompt: An e-commerce site stores product information with varying attributes as documents. It wants to keep using the MongoDB API that its application is already configured to use, without operating database server setup or patching itself. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Store the data as document-style items in Amazon DynamoDB.
choices.explanation: It can store items with varying attributes, but it does not provide the MongoDB API used by the existing application.

choices.text: Use the JSON type in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.
choices.explanation: It supports a JSON type, but it is a SQL database and does not replace the MongoDB API.

choices.text: Build and operate MongoDB on Amazon EC2.
choices.explanation: It supports the MongoDB API, but the organization would be responsible for managing the instances and database.

choices.text: Use the compatibility features of Amazon DocumentDB.
choices.explanation: It supports compatible MongoDB APIs and provides a managed database infrastructure.

learning.reason: Amazon DocumentDB is a managed document database compatible with MongoDB. Confirm that the APIs you use are supported.
learning.concept: Being able to store documents and being compatible with the API used by an existing application are separate requirements.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Start a small website on a monthly virtual server plan
prompt: A small web design company is moving an existing website. It needs a standalone virtual server that users can log in to at the operating system level and wants a simple monthly plan that bundles CPU, memory, storage, and a data transfer allowance. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Choose and combine Amazon EC2, Amazon EBS, and data transfer separately.
choices.explanation: This offers flexibility, but it does not meet the requirement to choose from simple monthly plans that bundle the resources.

choices.text: Deploy the web application with AWS Elastic Beanstalk.
choices.explanation: It can provision a runtime environment, but its resources are billed by type; it is not a service for choosing a monthly virtual server plan.

choices.text: Use an Amazon Lightsail plan for a virtual server.
choices.explanation: You can choose a plan that includes a virtual server, storage, and a transfer allowance, then start configuring it in the management console.

choices.text: Configure static website hosting in Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: It can serve static files, but it does not provide a virtual server with operating system access.

learning.reason: Lightsail virtual server plans bundle compute, storage, and a data transfer allowance.
learning.concept: Compare the need to select individual resources in detail with the need to get started easily by choosing a plan.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Connect an entire site through an encrypted path over the internet
prompt: A factory needs to connect several systems to private addresses in a VPC without installing a VPN client on each device. The factory router and AWS must have an encrypted path over the internet, without waiting for a dedicated connection. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: AWS Site-to-Site VPN
choices.explanation: An IPsec tunnel between the factory’s VPN device and the AWS endpoint can connect the two networks.

choices.text: AWS Client VPN
choices.explanation: This is suited to individual devices connecting as clients, not to connecting an entire site through its factory router.

choices.text: An AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection
choices.explanation: This uses a dedicated circuit, unlike the requested connection over the existing internet.

choices.text: VPC peering
choices.explanation: This connects two VPCs; it does not provide an internet VPN between an on-premises site router and AWS.

learning.reason: Site-to-Site VPN can create an encrypted network connection between on-premises equipment and AWS.
learning.concept: Distinguish a site-to-site VPN from a VPN for individual user devices.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Deliver the same container image from the build environment to ECS
prompt: A CI process creates a container image that must be shared so that Amazon ECS in a separate AWS environment can retrieve it by release tag. Which option provides an AWS-managed private registry that supports pushing and pulling, separate from the container runtime?

choices.text: Store the container files in Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: S3 can store the files, but it does not provide the image push and pull APIs of a container registry.

choices.text: Use Amazon EFS as shared file storage for ECS tasks.
choices.explanation: EFS can provide shared files visible to tasks, but it is not a registry from which to retrieve images.

choices.text: Build the container image with AWS CodeBuild.
choices.explanation: CodeBuild can create the image, but a separate private registry is needed for ECS to retrieve it later.

choices.text: Store the image in an Amazon ECR private repository.
choices.explanation: The build environment can push the image, and authorized ECS task environments can pull it.

learning.reason: ECR is a managed registry for registering, retrieving, and distributing container images.
learning.concept: Consider image building, image storage, and container execution as separate functions.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Manage the queues and compute resources for large numbers of batch jobs
prompt: An image-processing team submits thousands of containerized jobs that run for anywhere from a few minutes to several hours. The team needs queues with different priorities and compute environments, with AWS assigning compute resources. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Process each conversion job in a single AWS Lambda invocation.
choices.explanation: Lambda can handle short tasks, but a single invocation does not meet the requirement to run work lasting several hours.

choices.text: Use AWS Batch with job queues and managed compute environments.
choices.explanation: AWS Batch runs queued jobs according to priorities and other criteria and can use compute resources based on job requirements.

choices.text: Store only the job details in Amazon SQS.
choices.explanation: SQS can hold processing requests, but a queue alone does not run jobs or assign compute resources.

choices.text: Keep the same number of workers running on Amazon EC2 and have staff decide how to assign jobs.
choices.explanation: This lets the team manage its own workers, but it does not delegate job prioritization and compute resource assignment to AWS.

learning.reason: AWS Batch receives jobs in queues and schedules them on suitable compute environments.
learning.concept: Distinguish storing jobs in a queue from scheduling batch jobs.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Provide an entry point to a specific service in another VPC
prompt: A provider team wants to make an internal API available to a consumer VPC. The API must not be accessed over the internet, and the consumer VPC must not gain a route to other subnets in the provider VPC. Which option provides access only to the API, rather than connecting the networks as a whole?

choices.text: Create VPC peering and add a route to the provider network.
choices.explanation: This connects the VPCs; this option does not create an entry point that exposes only the service.

choices.text: Connect the provider and consumer VPCs with AWS Transit Gateway.
choices.explanation: This can centrally manage network connectivity, but the option does not configure service publishing with the API as the only destination.

choices.text: Use an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service and an interface endpoint in the consumer VPC.
choices.explanation: The consumer can connect privately to the published service through an endpoint in its VPC.

choices.text: Give the provider API a public endpoint and require authentication.
choices.explanation: Authentication can restrict access, but the endpoint would still be reachable from the internet rather than being private.

learning.reason: PrivateLink can provide users in another VPC with a connection to a specific service.
learning.concept: Distinguish routes to an entire VPC network from a private entry point to a specified service.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Automatically transition S3 storage classes based on object age
prompt: Store monitoring logs in S3 as objects a few MB in size. Recent logs are read frequently, but after 90 days they are accessed only once every few months. The logs must remain available for audits. Which feature transitions them to a storage class after 90 days while keeping the same bucket and object keys?

choices.text: Automatic access tiering in S3 Intelligent-Tiering
choices.explanation: It moves objects between tiers based on access patterns, but the requirement is a rule that moves each log to a specified storage class 90 days after it was created.

choices.text: S3 Versioning
choices.explanation: It can retain multiple versions under the same key, but Versioning alone does not change the storage class after 90 days.

choices.text: Set an S3 expiration action to 90 days.
choices.explanation: Once the expiration period is reached, the data becomes eligible for deletion, which does not meet the requirement to retain it for audits.

choices.text: Set an S3 Lifecycle transition action for 90 days after object creation.
choices.explanation: It moves qualifying objects to the specified storage class while retaining the objects under the same keys.

learning.reason: S3 Lifecycle transition rules let you specify the number of days after object creation and the destination storage class.
learning.concept: Storage class transitions, automatic tiering based on access patterns, and expiration-based deletion are different.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Choose a relational database whose read replicas use the same distributed storage
prompt: A company application uses a managed, PostgreSQL-compatible relational database. It needs a single cluster storage volume distributed across multiple Availability Zones behind the DB instances, with the writer and readers sharing that cluster volume. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition
choices.explanation: It is PostgreSQL-compatible, and its cluster volume is distributed across multiple Availability Zones. DB instances that handle writes and reads share the same data.

choices.text: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with DB instances and a single read replica
choices.explanation: It supports PostgreSQL, but in the specified configuration the source and read replica do not share a single distributed storage volume like Aurora's.

choices.text: An Amazon DocumentDB cluster
choices.explanation: It has cluster storage, but it is not the PostgreSQL-compatible relational database the application requires.

choices.text: Build and operate a PostgreSQL server on Amazon EC2.
choices.explanation: It can run PostgreSQL, but this configuration does not provide the required managed distributed storage.

source.label: 読み取りレプリカが同じ分散ストレージを使うリレーショナルDBを選ぶ

learning.reason: In an Aurora DB cluster, the primary and Aurora Replicas share a cluster volume across multiple Availability Zones.
learning.concept: Check the writer and reader storage architecture, not only SQL compatibility.

sourceLabel: Choose a relational database whose read replicas use the same distributed storage

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Deploy a standard application environment by uploading code
prompt: A team has a web application for a supported platform. After uploading the code, it wants AWS to handle the initial deployment of a load balancer and compute resources, as well as health monitoring. The team also wants to be able to inspect the AWS resources that are created. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Manually create Amazon EC2 instances and deploy the code to each one.
choices.explanation: This offers flexibility, but the team must provision resources such as the load balancer.

choices.text: Upload the application code to AWS Elastic Beanstalk.
choices.explanation: For a supported platform, it creates an application environment and can configure capacity provisioning, load balancing, and health monitoring.

choices.text: Use AWS CodeBuild alone to build the application code.
choices.explanation: It can build and test the code, but it does not manage a running environment for the web application.

choices.text: Place the code in Amazon S3 static website hosting.
choices.explanation: It can serve static content, but it does not deploy and run code on a server-side platform.

learning.reason: Elastic Beanstalk deploys a supported application environment from uploaded code and manages settings such as load balancing and monitoring together.
learning.concept: Distinguish building an application from providing an environment in which a web application runs.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Move running servers to EC2 with minimal changes
prompt: A company is closing its on-premises facility and wants to move running physical or virtual servers to EC2 with minimal changes. It will launch test instances on AWS and, after cutover, continue operations on EC2. Which service is appropriate for migrating the entire original server, not only its database?

choices.text: Use AWS Database Migration Service to migrate only the data.
choices.explanation: It is suited to database migration, but it does not migrate the entire server with its application operating system environment.

choices.text: Use AWS DataSync to transfer only shared files to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: It can transfer shared data, but it does not provide a way to test-launch the server as an EC2 instance and cut over.

choices.text: Use AWS Transform MGN (formerly AWS Application Migration Service) for the migration.
choices.explanation: It replicates the source server so it can be test-launched on EC2, then cut over to EC2 during migration.

choices.text: Use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery to keep the on-premises environment as the normal production site.
choices.explanation: It is suited to recovery to AWS after a disaster, but this scenario calls for permanently moving to EC2 and closing the facility.

learning.reason: AWS Transform MGN supports rehosting physical and virtual servers to AWS.
learning.concept: Distinguish permanent migration, disaster recovery, and migration of data alone.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Advance the release process when source code changes
prompt: A development team wants a source code change to trigger the existing build and tests, followed by deployment to staging after approval. Which AWS service lets the team define each stage and track progress and failures from source retrieval through deployment?

choices.text: Use AWS CodeBuild alone to compile and run tests.
choices.explanation: It can compile code and run tests, but this configuration alone does not manage the entire release process, including approval and deployment.

choices.text: Define the staging environment configuration with AWS CloudFormation.
choices.explanation: It can manage environment resources, but it does not connect the stages for source changes, builds, and approvals.

choices.text: Define the full sequence of build, approval, and deployment stages in AWS CodePipeline.
choices.explanation: It can start the stages when source code changes and track the execution status of each stage.

choices.text: Use AWS CodeDeploy alone to deploy the application.
choices.explanation: It can perform deployments, but it does not define the entire pipeline starting with source code and builds.

learning.reason: CodePipeline lets you define stages such as source, build, approval, and deployment, and manage the end-to-end release process.
learning.concept: Distinguish the service that performs build and test work from the service that organizes individual release stages in execution order.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Let developers provision approved configurations themselves
prompt: A central operations team defines an approved development environment that includes monitoring and tag settings. Developers want to select from a catalog of available configurations to provision AWS resources, without being able to change the original templates. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Have developers create their own AWS CloudFormation templates.
choices.explanation: This can reproduce resources, but it does not let developers select unmodifiable configurations from a centrally approved catalog.

choices.text: Have developers purchase the required individual software products through AWS Marketplace.
choices.explanation: This can be used to procure third-party products, but it is not a catalog for provisioning organization-defined, approved environments.

choices.text: Provision new accounts with Account Factory in AWS Control Tower.
choices.explanation: This can standardize new accounts, but it serves a different purpose from providing a catalog of development resources that can be selected in existing accounts.

choices.text: Register the approved development environments as products in AWS Service Catalog and authorize developers to use them.
choices.explanation: It manages available products and permissions, allowing developers to launch approved configurations through self-service.

learning.reason: AWS Service Catalog lets you register approved products in a portfolio and allow authorized users to provision them through self-service.
learning.concept: Distinguish infrastructure templates from a catalog that distributes and manages configurations authorized for use by teams.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Recover an on-premises application server in AWS
prompt: A company will continue running its production application on premises, but wants to recover its servers in AWS if a site fails. It wants to keep recovery-side resource usage low during normal operations, continuously replicate source server data, and recover the servers as EC2 instances when needed. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Use AWS DataSync to periodically copy only selected data folders to S3.
choices.explanation: It can replicate files, but it cannot launch an entire server as a recovery instance.

choices.text: Continuously replicate the source servers with AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery.
choices.explanation: It replicates data to a low-cost staging environment and can launch servers in AWS during recovery.

choices.text: Protect the application servers with Amazon RDS snapshots.
choices.explanation: It can protect supported databases, but it does not continuously replicate entire on-premises application servers.

choices.text: Add AWS Storage Gateway in the cloud for file storage.
choices.explanation: It can provide hybrid storage, but it cannot launch recovery instances for servers.

learning.reason: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates source server data at the block level and can launch recovery instances in AWS for drills or disasters.
learning.concept: Distinguish a permanent cutover after migration, individual file transfer, and continuous replication with recovery launches.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Create a working volume in another Availability Zone from an EBS snapshot
prompt: A new EC2 instance has been launched in a different Availability Zone in the same Region. Without modifying the original EC2 instance or its EBS volume, you want to use the data as of an existing EBS snapshot as a block device on the new instance for investigation. Which method is appropriate?

choices.text: Create a volume from the existing EBS snapshot in the same Availability Zone as the new EC2 instance, then attach it.
choices.explanation: A separate volume containing the data as of the snapshot can be used on the instance for investigation.

choices.text: Detach the EBS volume from the original EC2 instance and attach it directly to the instance in the other Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: The volume is in the original Availability Zone and cannot be attached directly to an instance in another Availability Zone. This also violates the requirement to leave the original environment unchanged.

choices.text: Attach an empty EBS volume to the new EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: This provides working space, but it does not contain the data as of the existing snapshot.

choices.text: Attach the EBS snapshot itself directly to the EC2 instance as a block device.
choices.explanation: The attachable resource is an EBS volume created from the snapshot, not the snapshot itself.

source.label: EBSスナップショットからのボリューム作成

learning.reason: Create an EBS volume from the existing snapshot in the target Availability Zone and attach it to an EC2 instance in that zone. This provides the snapshot data without changing the original volume.
learning.concept: EBS volumes can be attached only within the same Availability Zone, while a snapshot can be used to create a separate volume in another Availability Zone in the same Region.

sourceLabel: Creating a volume from an EBS snapshot

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Choose a plan that provides AWS technical support outside business hours
prompt: A company runs a production service in a standard commercial Region. It wants to contact AWS technical support 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, even if an incident occurs on a holiday. It does not need a designated Technical Account Manager or advanced operational support. Which of the listed current plans is the minimum plan that meets these requirements?

choices.text: Basic Support
choices.explanation: It provides assistance with billing and accounts, but does not meet the requirement for ongoing technical support for production services.

choices.text: AWS Business Support+
choices.explanation: It provides access to technical support 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. It fits this case because dedicated personnel and advanced operational support are not required.

choices.text: AWS Enterprise Support
choices.explanation: It provides technical support and includes higher-level assistance such as a Technical Account Manager. It is not the minimum plan that meets this case's requirements.

choices.text: AWS Unified Operations
choices.explanation: It includes extensive support for critical workloads. It is not required to meet the stated requirements.

learning.reason: Among the current plans, Business Support+ meets the requirement for 24-hour, 365-day access to AWS technical support.
learning.concept: Assistance with billing and accounts differs in scope from technical support for running workloads.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Check the impact of scheduled AWS maintenance
prompt: An operator has received a notification from AWS related to scheduled maintenance. In addition to the published, Region-wide service status, the operator first wants to check which resources in their AWS account are affected. Where should they look?

choices.text: Review each resource’s metrics in Amazon CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: This can be used to monitor operational status, but it is not the view that lists resources affected by AWS-scheduled maintenance as events.

choices.text: View only the public service status in AWS Health.
choices.explanation: Public events can be reviewed, but they do not show which resources in this account are affected.

choices.text: View the cost optimization checks in AWS Trusted Advisor.
choices.explanation: These checks can identify opportunities to improve resource usage, but they are not where you check resources affected by scheduled AWS maintenance.

choices.text: In the account view of the AWS Health Dashboard, review scheduled changes and the affected resources.
choices.explanation: You can review details of the relevant event and the resources AWS identifies as affected at the account level.

source.label: AWS Health Dashboardのアカウントイベント

learning.reason: The account view of the AWS Health Dashboard is used to review AWS events relevant to an account and information about the resources associated with those events.
learning.concept: Distinguish the overall status of a service from AWS events that affect resources in your own account.

sourceLabel: Account events in the AWS Health Dashboard

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Find an external company with migration experience
prompt: A company is starting a migration project to AWS. Before purchasing a product, it wants to find and compare multiple external companies in the AWS Partner Network that have expertise in its industry and in migration. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Use the official AWS Partner search to find consulting companies with migration expertise.
choices.explanation: You can review partners’ areas of expertise and compare external companies that may fit the requirements.

choices.text: Search for migration procedure documents in AWS Prescriptive Guidance.
choices.explanation: You can find technical and planning guidance, but it is not an official directory for comparing external companies that meet the stated criteria.

choices.text: Create a ticket for an AWS product issue in the AWS Support Center.
choices.explanation: This is a contact point for technical support and similar inquiries, not a way to search for external companies by expertise.

choices.text: Select only an automated data migration software contract in AWS Marketplace.
choices.explanation: You can procure migration products, but that does not meet the requirement to compare external companies that can collaborate on the design and execution.

learning.reason: The official AWS Partner search can help find consulting and implementation partners that match criteria such as expertise and location.
learning.concept: Distinguish AWS technical support from finding partners that assist with implementation in a particular field.

sourceLabel: How to find an AWS Partner

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Show costs for multiple accounts by the company’s business units
prompt: An organization has consolidated billing. The finance team wants to group multiple existing accounts into internal business categories such as “Retail business” and “Corporate business” for use in cost management views and usage reports. It wants to use account IDs as criteria without moving accounts or retagging resources. What should it use?

choices.text: Move accounts into an OU for each business unit in AWS Organizations.
choices.explanation: This changes the organization’s structure, which conflicts with the requirement to avoid moving accounts. An OU itself is not a feature for defining the requested categories in cost management.

choices.text: Activate cost allocation tags and add a business tag to every resource.
choices.explanation: Resources with tags can be classified by business unit, but this does not use the specified account IDs as the criteria.

choices.text: Create classification rules in AWS Cost Categories that use account IDs as criteria.
choices.explanation: This can assign costs from multiple accounts to one business category and make the category available in Cost Explorer, usage reports, and other supported views.

choices.text: Create a monthly AWS Budgets budget for each business unit.
choices.explanation: This can help monitor costs by business unit, but it does not define a business classification that can be shared across cost management.

learning.reason: AWS Cost Categories can map costs to custom categories based on criteria such as accounts, and those categories can be used in supported cost management views.
learning.concept: You can create an organization-specific way to group costs without changing resource placement in AWS services.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Keep discounts when changing configurations within the same EC2 family
prompt: For the next year, a team will continue using the same EC2 instance family in the same Region. It may change instance sizes and operating systems. The team wants to commit to a spend amount per hour, apply discounts despite these changes, compare the maximum discount rates AWS lists for each type of Savings Plan, and choose the type with the higher rate. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Compute Savings Plans
choices.explanation: These cover changes in size and operating system, but when the Region and family are fixed as in this scenario, EC2 Instance Savings Plans generally offer a higher discount rate.

choices.text: Regional Standard Reserved Instances
choices.explanation: These can discount eligible EC2 usage, but they are not Savings Plans based on an hourly spend commitment and have platform conditions at purchase.

choices.text: EC2 On-Demand Capacity Reservations
choices.explanation: These reserve launch capacity in a specific Availability Zone. By themselves, they do not provide a discount through a spend commitment.

choices.text: EC2 Instance Savings Plans
choices.explanation: These cover EC2 usage in a specific Region and instance family, applying discounts to eligible usage even when the size or operating system changes.

learning.reason: EC2 Instance Savings Plans cover a spend commitment for a specific instance family in a specific Region and allow size and operating-system changes within that scope.
learning.concept: Compute Savings Plans, which have broader applicability, and EC2 Instance Savings Plans, which specify a Region and family, differ in flexibility and maximum discount.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Compare more than the storage rate for infrequent access
prompt: Temporary S3 data is read multiple times starting the day after it is stored and is usually deleted after two weeks. The team has been offered a switch from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-IA. In addition to the storage rate per GB, which two Standard-IA pricing factors should it compare?

choices.text: Retrieval charges based on the amount of data read from Standard-IA
choices.explanation: For Standard-IA, charges based on the amount of data retrieved must be considered separately from request charges and other costs.

choices.text: Required CloudFront charges to serve S3 objects in both classes
choices.explanation: CloudFront is not required to use Standard-IA; objects can be retrieved directly from S3.

choices.text: Charges for the remaining minimum storage period when data is deleted early
choices.explanation: Standard-IA has a 30-day minimum storage duration. Even when data is deleted after two weeks, the cost of the minimum duration must be considered.

choices.text: A charge to start an archive restoration job before reading from Standard-IA
choices.explanation: Standard-IA provides immediate access, so a preliminary archive restoration job is not required.

choices.text: An annual spend commitment dedicated to S3 Standard-IA
choices.explanation: There is no need to purchase an annual spend commitment to use this storage class.

learning.reason: Standard-IA has data retrieval charges and a 30-day minimum storage duration. A low storage rate alone does not determine the cost of data that is read frequently and kept for a short time.
learning.concept: Consider how access frequency and retention period affect the total cost of an infrequent-access storage class.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Reserve launch capacity in a specific Availability Zone for a short period
prompt: For a three-day event, a company will launch 20 EC2 instances of the same type in a specified Availability Zone. Securing the instance count is more important than receiving a discount, and the company cannot enter into a one-year commitment. Which option is appropriate for reserving launch capacity with AWS in advance?

choices.text: An EC2 On-Demand Capacity Reservation specifying the target Availability Zone and instance attributes
choices.explanation: This can provide matching launch capacity in the specified Availability Zone. For short-term use, check the supported reservation terms and charges for unused capacity.

choices.text: Launch instances of the same type On-Demand without reservations
choices.explanation: This avoids a long-term commitment, but does not secure capacity in the specified Availability Zone for the event.

choices.text: Purchase a one-year EC2 Instance Savings Plan
choices.explanation: This discounts eligible usage but does not reserve capacity in a specific Availability Zone.

choices.text: Purchase a one-year Zonal Reserved Instance
choices.explanation: This can provide capacity and a discount in the target Availability Zone, but it violates the condition that the company cannot enter into a long-term commitment.

source.label: EC2オンデマンドキャパシティ予約

learning.reason: An EC2 On-Demand Capacity Reservation can secure launch capacity for instances matching specified attributes in a particular Availability Zone, and a reservation can be selected to fit the usage pattern.
learning.concept: Reserving capacity and receiving a long-term discount on spend are separate requirements.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Forecast AWS spending for the next few months from recent usage trends
prompt: A finance team wants to view a graph of projected costs for the next three months for an AWS environment that runs continuously, using usage trends already accumulated. It has not set a fixed budget amount and will not build its own model for analysis. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Enter planned resources manually in AWS Pricing Calculator
choices.explanation: This can estimate the cost of a new configuration, but this action does not create a forecast based on the actual usage trends of an existing environment.

choices.text: Display a forecast for a future period in AWS Cost Explorer
choices.explanation: With sufficient history, Cost Explorer can show a projection based on past cost trends; a budget amount does not need to be specified.

choices.text: Set up only an AWS Budgets notification for when actual spending exceeds a fixed amount
choices.explanation: This sends a notification against a specified amount and does not meet the goal of viewing a graph of future costs without setting a budget amount.

choices.text: Save detailed historical billing records to S3 with AWS Data Exports
choices.explanation: This can export actual usage data for analysis, but exporting data alone does not forecast future costs.

learning.reason: Cost Explorer forecasts future costs based on trends in usage history.
learning.concept: Distinguish estimates based on planned future usage, forecasts based on actual usage, and alerts against a budget amount.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Measure signup success from the user’s perspective
prompt: The site operations team is improving the service against a goal that 99.9% of user signups succeed. A signup can fail even when the server has spare capacity. Which metric directly evaluates whether this goal is being met?

choices.text: Average daily CPU utilization of the web server
choices.explanation: This shows internal load, but not the proportion of signups that completed successfully.

choices.text: Storage capacity in use in the database
choices.explanation: This shows resource utilization, but does not directly measure user signup outcomes.

choices.text: Number of times the application displays the signup page
choices.explanation: This shows how many signup opportunities there were, but processing after the page is displayed may still fail.

choices.text: The proportion of valid signups received during the measurement period that receive a successful completion response
choices.explanation: This directly evaluates the success rate of the functionality delivered to users and can be compared with the 99.9% goal.

learning.reason: Measuring the proportion of eligible signups received that complete successfully directly evaluates the service objective for users.
learning.concept: Distinguish internal metrics, such as equipment utilization, from metrics that represent the outcomes people achieve when using a service.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Check the recovery destination’s limits before switching
prompt: During a disaster, processing will move from the production Region to a recovery Region. The recovery Region normally has low utilization. To avoid reaching a Region-level service quota and causing an outage when utilization rises after the switch, choose two actions to take in advance.

choices.text: Estimate the maximum utilization that must be handled during recovery, with room for growth.
choices.explanation: Normal utilization alone does not show what will be required after the switch.

choices.text: Record the production Region’s limits and assume that the same limits automatically apply in the recovery Region.
choices.explanation: Depending on the service, quotas can be account- or Region-specific, so the recovery destination must be checked separately.

choices.text: Compare the requirements with the recovery destination’s actual quotas and request increases in advance if needed.
choices.explanation: This allows time for review and for the increase to take effect, helping ensure the required limits are available for the switch.

choices.text: Because normal utilization is low in the recovery destination, wait until after the switch to check the limits.
choices.explanation: If a limit is reached before action is taken, business recovery may be affected.

choices.text: Add a buffer to the recovery budget and assume that this alone will increase the service quotas.
choices.explanation: Changing the budget does not change service quotas.

source.label: Well-Architectedのフェイルオーバー用クォータ

learning.reason: Estimate post-switch utilization, compare it with the recovery destination’s own quotas, and request any necessary increases early enough for them to take effect.
learning.concept: Do not confuse the capacity or utilization in the current Region with the service limits in the recovery Region.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Validate a new version with a small share of live traffic
prompt: A team is introducing a feature change into production. It wants to validate the new version under real usage conditions and limit the impact to a small number of users if the error rate worsens. Which approach should it choose while keeping the old version running?

choices.text: After the version passes pre-release testing, stop the old version and switch all users to the new version.
choices.explanation: This provides pre-release assurance, but any problem with real traffic affects everyone from the start.

choices.text: Send part of the production traffic to the new version, then move the remainder after checking the error rate.
choices.explanation: This lets the team observe real usage during an initial rollout and respond to worsening metrics before expanding the change to everyone.

choices.text: Duplicate production traffic to the new version, but do not return the new version’s responses to users.
choices.explanation: This allows processing to be compared, but does not validate the result of actually providing the new functionality to some users.

choices.text: Run the new version only in a test environment and do not direct users to it.
choices.explanation: This supports pre-release testing, but does not meet the requirement for an initial rollout to real production users.

source.label: 段階的なカナリアデプロイ

learning.reason: A canary rollout first sends a portion of production traffic to the new version, evaluates its health, and then expands the share of traffic.
learning.concept: Testing in a separate environment, switching all traffic at once, and gradually exposing a small share of production users have different impact scopes.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Safely return to the original environment after disaster recovery
prompt: During a disaster, a company switched operations to a separate environment, where it processed new orders. The original environment has now been repaired, and the company wants to return operations to it without losing orders. What should it do before switching back?

choices.text: Return users as soon as the original environment is running, and check the orders from the recovery period later.
choices.explanation: Even if the original environment is healthy, it may not contain updates accepted during recovery.

choices.text: Restore a backup from before the disaster in the original environment and resume accepting orders.
choices.explanation: This can restore the pre-disaster state, but it does not bring in orders processed in the recovery environment.

choices.text: Synchronize updates made in the recovery environment to the original environment, verify consistency and readiness to accept orders, and then switch back.
choices.explanation: This lets the company decide when to switch while preserving business data created during recovery.

choices.text: First overwrite the recovery environment with updates from the original environment, then immediately switch back to the original environment.
choices.explanation: This may lose newer data that exists only in the recovery environment, and the synchronization direction is the reverse of what the scenario requires.

source.label: 障害に対応する際のフェイルバック

learning.reason: Apply data changes made in the recovery environment to the original environment, then return users after it is ready.
learning.concept: Failover moves operations away from the environment affected by a disaster. Failback must also account for data created after that move.

sourceLabel: Failback when responding to an outage

category: クラウドの概念
title: Avoid duplicate processing when a request is retried after no response
prompt: An order intake API successfully reserves inventory, but a temporary network interruption prevents the response from reaching the caller. The caller retries the same order. Which design property prevents inventory from being reserved twice for the same order?

choices.text: Idempotency
choices.explanation: A retry of the same order can be recognized as already processed, so no additional inventory is reserved.

choices.text: Availability
choices.explanation: This concerns whether a service is usable; it does not prevent the same request from being processed twice.

choices.text: Least privilege
choices.explanation: This limits permitted operations and resources; it does not control the outcome when the same permitted request arrives multiple times.

choices.text: Horizontal scaling
choices.explanation: This increases the number of servers handling requests, but does not automatically consolidate business outcomes when multiple servers receive the same order.

learning.reason: Idempotency means designing a system so that repeating the same logical request preserves a single business outcome.
learning.concept: Account for the possibility that processing completed before a retry, and prevent the same request from applying its side effects more than once.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Keep a product usable longer on existing user devices
prompt: A new version of a browsing app uses more CPU and memory on many of the devices currently in use. The goal is to meet the required features and response targets while reducing the need for users to replace their devices early. Which development approach best supports sustainability?

choices.text: Measure response targets only on new devices and exclude all others from the operating requirements.
choices.explanation: This narrows the set of devices on which targets are measured and could prompt users to replace existing devices sooner.

choices.text: Move more processing uniformly to currently used devices to reduce the load on the server.
choices.explanation: This could reduce cloud-side load, but may increase device load and encourage earlier replacement.

choices.text: Compare only cloud costs and do not measure device processing time or memory use.
choices.explanation: Cloud costs do not directly reveal device resource consumption or compatibility.

choices.text: Measure representative devices in use and reduce CPU and memory use while preserving required features.
choices.explanation: This can reduce the burden on devices while selecting changes that still meet the stated response targets.

source.label: 利用者の端末への影響を最適化する

learning.reason: Measuring processing load on representative devices and reducing client resource use while retaining requirements can extend the useful life of existing equipment.
learning.concept: A workload affects resource consumption on users' devices as well as in the cloud.

sourceLabel: Optimize the impact on user devices

category: クラウドの概念
title: Understand that updates awaiting replication may be absent from a disaster recovery site
prompt: In the primary environment, after a write for an order succeeds, the application returns success without waiting for the copy to another environment to complete. The primary environment is lost immediately afterward, and operations switch to the recovery site. Which statement about updates not yet copied is true?

choices.text: Every update for which the primary environment returned success has also been applied at the replica.
choices.explanation: This design does not wait for replication to complete, so success at the primary does not guarantee that the update has been applied at the replica.

choices.text: Even a successful update may be absent from the recovery site if it has not yet been applied there.
choices.explanation: With asynchronous replication, there can be a delay before an update is applied, and a failure during that interval can leave a gap.

choices.text: If the switch to the recovery site is fast, no updates waiting for replication will be lost.
choices.explanation: Failover time and the point in time up to which data is available at the recovery site are separate measures.

choices.text: Resuming writes at the recovery site always restores updates that had not finished copying before the failure.
choices.explanation: An update that is absent from the other environment is not restored merely by starting new writes there.

source.label: 目標復旧時点と設計の評価

learning.reason: With asynchronous replication, an update acknowledged at the primary may be missing from the recovery site if a failure occurs before it is replicated.
learning.concept: Distinguish when a write is acknowledged from the point in time represented by data available at the recovery site.

sourceLabel: Evaluate recovery point objectives and design

category: クラウドの概念
title: Use separate documents for routine operations and investigating unknown causes
prompt: A team is preparing procedures for routine operations and guidance for incident investigations. Certificate expiration checks follow the same steps every time. When an unexplained response delay occurs, the metrics or dependencies to examine next vary with the observations. Choose two appropriate uses of operational documents.

choices.text: Have each person check certificate expiration differently based on their experience, and do not document the procedure.
choices.explanation: This does not provide repeatable steps for a routine task.

choices.text: Document certificate expiration checks as a standard procedure in a runbook.
choices.explanation: This makes the actions and expected results clear, so the procedure can be repeated regardless of who performs it.

choices.text: For an unexplained delay, create a procedure that always restarts the system without investigating.
choices.explanation: This does not help identify an unknown cause and may also destroy evidence needed for the investigation.

choices.text: For delay investigations, keep only past incident reports and do not define what information to check next.
choices.explanation: Past incidents may be useful references, but this does not guide an investigation based on observations from the current incident.

choices.text: Document decision steps in a playbook so that delay investigations respond to observed results.
choices.explanation: This lets the team test possible causes and choose the next investigation step based on the results.

source.label: Well-Architectedのランブックとプレイブック

learning.reason: A runbook describes a standard procedure with clear outcomes, while a playbook provides investigation steps and decision branches.
learning.concept: Use one document to repeat known operations and another to investigate unknown causes and decide what to do next.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Connecting investment to business outcomes
prompt: A product owner is considering a new customer-facing service that uses the cloud. In particular, they want to set the product roadmap based on the value they aim to deliver to customers and align technical initiatives with the organization’s business goals. Which AWS CAF perspective is central to this effort?

choices.text: Business
choices.explanation: Correct. It connects cloud investments to digital transformation goals and business outcomes.

choices.text: Governance
choices.explanation: It addresses controls that maximize organizational benefits and minimize transformation risks.

choices.text: Operations
choices.explanation: It addresses the capabilities needed to deliver cloud services at a level that meets business needs.

choices.text: Platform
choices.explanation: It addresses building a scalable, enterprise-grade cloud foundation.

learning.reason: The Business perspective of AWS CAF addresses cloud-based product development and alignment with organizational business goals.
learning.concept: Distinguish setting business value and product direction from governing investments and tracking risk.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Aligning service delivery with business needs
prompt: After a migration, IT service managers and SREs want to establish operational capabilities so that cloud services continue to be delivered at the level required by business units. Which AWS CAF perspective primarily addresses this?

choices.text: People
choices.explanation: It addresses culture, organizational structure, skills, and leadership.

choices.text: Security
choices.explanation: It addresses capabilities for ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data and workloads.

choices.text: Operations
choices.explanation: Correct. It addresses delivering cloud services at a level that meets business needs.

choices.text: Business
choices.explanation: It addresses capabilities for connecting investments to transformation goals and business outcomes.

learning.reason: The organizational capability to maintain service delivery at a level aligned with business needs belongs to the Operations perspective of AWS CAF.
learning.concept: The Operational Excellence pillar of the Well-Architected Framework and the organizational Operations perspective of AWS CAF address different levels.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Quantifying workforce productivity
prompt: A company wants to quantify the workforce productivity gains from migrating to managed services, rather than relying on general satisfaction. Which measurement is most appropriate under the Cloud Value Framework for a team responsible for server management?

choices.text: Compare the number of virtual machines managed per administrator before and after migration
choices.explanation: Correct. The number of staff per managed workload, or the amount managed per administrator, is a quantitative workforce productivity measure.

choices.text: Compare the lead time for delivering new features to users before and after migration
choices.explanation: This can measure how quickly the product or business responds to change, but it does not directly show the efficiency of staff responsible for server management.

choices.text: Compare monthly infrastructure spending before and after migration
choices.explanation: This can show changes in IT costs, but not how much work the same number of people can manage.

choices.text: Compare the time services were unavailable because of unplanned outages before and after migration
choices.explanation: This can assess operational resilience, but it does not measure how much work each staff member can manage.

learning.reason: Workforce productivity can be measured as output per unit of effort, such as improvements in the number of VMs or amount of storage an administrator can manage.
learning.concept: Quantify the value of managed services by defining a KPI that can be compared before and after migration, rather than relying on the fact that services are managed.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Measuring the value of operational resilience
prompt: Executives want to quantify how much a cloud migration has reduced the impact of failures on the business. Which metric is most appropriate for demonstrating operational resilience in the Cloud Value Framework?

choices.text: Time required to bring new features to market
choices.explanation: This measures business agility outcomes.

choices.text: Number of managed resources per administrator
choices.explanation: This measures workforce productivity outcomes.

choices.text: Infrastructure costs as a percentage of revenue
choices.explanation: This measures the value of cost reduction.

choices.text: Reduction in unplanned downtime or business interruptions
choices.explanation: Correct. Improving availability and reducing unplanned downtime represent the value of operational resilience.

learning.reason: The value of operational resilience can be quantified by how much unplanned downtime or business interruption has been reduced, not simply by increasing the number of components.
learning.concept: The Cloud Value Framework tracks cost, workforce productivity, resilience, agility, and other outcomes using distinct metrics.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Measuring the cost savings value of cloud
prompt: A company wants to demonstrate the value of cloud use on an ongoing basis without limiting the comparison to total TCO, while also accounting for changes in business scale. Which KPI is most appropriate for measuring cost savings in the Cloud Value Framework?

choices.text: Time from detecting a production outage to restoring service
choices.explanation: This is an operational outcome metric related to resilience.

choices.text: IT infrastructure spend as a percentage of revenue
choices.explanation: Correct. This makes it possible to compare and track infrastructure cost efficiency relative to business scale.

choices.text: Average number of days until a new feature is delivered
choices.explanation: This measures the speed of enabling change; it does not measure costs in relation to business scale.

choices.text: Number of resources managed per operations staff member
choices.explanation: This measures staff productivity and does not directly measure costs in relation to business scale.

source.label: AWSのクラウド財務管理と費用最適化の指標

learning.reason: Tracking infrastructure spend relative to revenue or another measure of business scale makes comparisons easier even as the business grows.
learning.concept: The Cloud Value Framework measures and tracks migration value across multiple dimensions, not only costs.

sourceLabel: AWS metrics for cloud financial management and cost optimization

category: クラウドの概念
title: Assessing migration readiness
prompt: Before a large-scale migration, a company wants to assess its readiness to migrate to the cloud. Which approach is most appropriate for an AWS Migration Readiness Assessment (MRA)?

choices.text: Automatically collect infrastructure assets and approve the migration using only technical information.
choices.explanation: Asset information helps with planning, but it does not reflect readiness in areas such as the business and workforce.

choices.text: Have only executives calculate the expected return on investment and consider the migration readiness assessment complete.
choices.explanation: This is part of an investment decision, but it does not establish stakeholder agreement about technical, organizational, and operational capabilities.

choices.text: Use questions aligned with the CAF for cross-functional discussions, analyze the results, and agree on next steps.
choices.explanation: Correct. An MRA brings stakeholders together for an assessment aligned with the CAF, consolidates observations and steps to address gaps, and reports the results.

choices.text: Assign a technical migration strategy to each application first, then treat only those results as the organization’s overall readiness.
choices.explanation: Individual application strategies can be useful, but organizational capabilities and governance gaps also need to be assessed.

source.label: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Readiness assessment process

learning.reason: An MRA is conducted through cross-functional discussions aligned with the CAF, analysis, and a debrief to decide on actions, not just an inventory of technical assets.
learning.concept: Assessing organizational readiness is distinct from planning migration waves or choosing a migration approach for individual applications.

sourceLabel: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Readiness assessment process

category: クラウドの概念
title: Revisiting resource use for on-time batch processing
prompt: The nightly aggregation job only needs to finish by 8 a.m. the next day; it does not need to respond to each request within seconds. The team wants to reduce idle resources while meeting the business deadline. Which design decision is most appropriate from a sustainability perspective?

choices.text: Run each request individually as soon as it arrives, starting dedicated resources for every job.
choices.explanation: Running jobs individually can increase startup and idle overhead and resource use, even when immediate responses are unnecessary.

choices.text: Queue requests and process them in batches, scheduling execution to meet the agreed SLA of completion by the next morning.
choices.explanation: Correct. When immediate response is unnecessary, asynchronous, scheduled, and batch processing can improve utilization and reduce resources while meeting business requirements.

choices.text: Set the same shortest response-time target as interactive processing for every batch and reserve maximum capacity at all times.
choices.explanation: An unnecessarily stringent performance SLA beyond the agreed deadline can increase unused capacity and environmental impact.

choices.text: Set no deadline and delay processing indefinitely until resource use is minimized.
choices.explanation: Sustainability does not justify abandoning an SLA that meets business needs.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected Sustainability Pillar: Align SLAs with sustainability goals

learning.reason: SLAs affect resource use as well as availability and performance. When immediate responses are unnecessary, batching within an agreed deadline can improve resource efficiency.
learning.concept: Sustainability optimization means revisiting unnecessarily strict service levels while continuing to meet business requirements.

sourceLabel: AWS Well-Architected Sustainability Pillar: Align SLAs with sustainability goals

category: クラウドの概念
title: Including migration-period double costs in the business case
prompt: A company is migrating from its data center to AWS over 18 months. During the migration, it cannot immediately retire its on-premises equipment, facilities, or support contracts, and it must also prepare a new environment and migration resources on AWS. How should costs be handled in the migration business case?

choices.text: Include only the monthly AWS costs and assume on-premises fixed costs immediately fall to zero in proportion to the number of servers migrated.
choices.explanation: Fixed costs such as facilities and contracts may not disappear immediately when some servers are migrated.

choices.text: Include only historical on-premises hardware purchase costs and exclude AWS and migration work costs.
choices.explanation: Excluding future AWS usage and additional costs during migration prevents a comparison of the total costs needed for decision-making.

choices.text: Compare only expected costs after migration and exclude the 18-month migration period from the business case.
choices.explanation: During migration, source, target, and migration resources may need to run in parallel, affecting both cost and duration.

choices.text: Include the costs of parallel on-premises and AWS operations, migration resources, facilities, and contracts during the migration period.
choices.explanation: Correct. The business case needs to include double bubble costs during migration, migration resources, and fixed costs for existing infrastructure.

source.label: AWS Migration & Modernization Blog: Explore cost components

learning.reason: Migration costs include more than post-migration AWS charges. Estimate parallel environments, migration tools and staff, and existing facilities and contracts over the relevant period.
learning.concept: A cloud migration business case should assess the target-state TCO separately from temporary double costs incurred during migration.

sourceLabel: AWS Migration & Modernization Blog: Explore cost components

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Synchronize users and groups from an existing employee directory
prompt: A company has configured an existing external identity provider as the identity source for IAM Identity Center, and users can sign in. The company now wants to synchronize corresponding provider-side user and group information whenever someone joins or changes departments, instead of entering users and groups manually on the AWS side. What should it configure?

choices.text: Exchange the SAML metadata again and reconfigure sign-in federation only.
choices.explanation: Even if authentication is federated, this configuration alone does not provision groups or attributes in advance.

choices.text: Configure SCIM automatic provisioning between the external identity provider and IAM Identity Center.
choices.explanation: This can synchronize supported users and groups from the external directory and reduce manual entry on the AWS side.

choices.text: Create only IAM user groups in the AWS account.
choices.explanation: This can attach common policies to IAM users in the account, but it does not synchronize external groups to Identity Center.

choices.text: Create only department-specific OUs in AWS Organizations.
choices.explanation: This can organize AWS accounts, but it does not synchronize user or group information.

source.label: IAM Identity CenterのSCIM自動プロビジョニング

learning.reason: IAM Identity Center can synchronize supported user and group information from an external identity provider through SCIM.
learning.concept: SAML sign-in federation and SCIM provisioning of users and groups serve different purposes.

sourceLabel: IAM Identity Center SCIM automatic provisioning

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Scan S3 files for malware when they are received
prompt: An application portal stores customer-uploaded files in S3. Before staff open a file, the company wants to automatically scan newly stored objects for malware and send the results to the responsible team’s workflow. Which feature is appropriate?

choices.text: Use Amazon Macie to classify sensitive data in the target bucket.
choices.explanation: It can identify sensitive data such as personal information, but it does not scan uploaded files for malware.

choices.text: Record S3 data events in CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: This can record operations such as uploads, but it does not inspect file contents for malware.

choices.text: Configure GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 for the target bucket.
choices.explanation: It can scan new objects in the target bucket and pass the results to downstream workflow processing.

choices.text: Enable standard checks for bucket configurations in AWS Security Hub CSPM.
choices.explanation: This can evaluate configuration compliance with standards, but it does not scan individual uploaded files for malware.

learning.reason: GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 can scan new uploads to the target bucket for malware and integrate the results with downstream processes.
learning.concept: Distinguish sensitive-data detection in stored documents, malware detection, and auditing of access operations.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Retrieve the latest secret in the recovery Region
prompt: An application manages database credentials with Secrets Manager. When operations fail over to another Region, the application needs to retrieve the secret in the failover Region. How can it do this without manually copying the value whenever the original secret is updated?

choices.text: Enable rotation only for the secret in the original Region.
choices.explanation: This can update the value periodically, but it does not create a replica for retrieval in the recovery Region.

choices.text: Store only the ARN of the secret in the original Region in the recovery Region application.
choices.explanation: The ARN still points to a resource in the original Region; it does not provide a retrieval target in the recovery Region.

choices.text: Create an independent secret with the same name in the recovery Region and enter only the initial value.
choices.explanation: The value is available when the secret is created, but subsequent updates to the original value are not propagated to this independent secret.

choices.text: Create a replica of the original secret in the recovery Region with Secrets Manager.
choices.explanation: Updates to the original secret can be propagated to the replica, and the application can retrieve that replica in the recovery Region.

source.label: AWS Secrets Managerのリージョン間レプリケーション

learning.reason: Secrets Manager cross-Region replication provides a retrieval target in another Region and can propagate updates from the primary secret to its replica.
learning.concept: Distinguish updating a value in the original Region from propagating that update to the recovery Region.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Use a certificate to provide short-term credentials to an on-premises workload
prompt: An on-premises aggregation service regularly calls AWS APIs. It runs without a person signing in, and the company can already use an X.509 certificate issued by a trusted corporate certificate authority. Which option is appropriate for obtaining short-term credentials for an IAM role without storing long-term AWS access keys on the service?

choices.text: Configure a trusted certificate authority in IAM Roles Anywhere and use a corresponding IAM role.
choices.explanation: The on-premises service can use its X.509 certificate to obtain temporary credentials for a role scoped to the required operations.

choices.text: Attach an EC2 instance profile directly to the on-premises server.
