choices.explanation: An EC2 instance profile lets an EC2 instance use a role; it is not a way to assign one directly to an arbitrary on-premises device.

choices.text: Sign in to the employee IAM Identity Center portal each time.
choices.explanation: This can be used for human access to AWS, but it does not meet the authentication requirement for an unattended service using a certificate.

choices.text: Obtain IAM access keys and register them with a Secrets Manager integration on the on-premises server.
choices.explanation: Even if a storage service is used, this design relies on long-term keys and does not obtain short-term credentials from the certificate.

learning.reason: IAM Roles Anywhere uses X.509 certificates issued by trusted certificate authorities to let workloads running outside AWS obtain temporary AWS credentials.
learning.concept: Distinguish employee authentication, IAM roles assigned to compute services in AWS, and authentication for workloads outside AWS or on premises.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Identify Granted but Unused Permissions
prompt: An auditor is reviewing permissions in an AWS account. The check for access available from outside the account has already been completed separately. The auditor now wants to identify, as candidates for review, IAM roles that have not been used during a specified period and service permissions granted to roles that have not been used. Which feature is appropriate?

choices.text: IAM Access Analyzer external access analysis
choices.explanation: It evaluates access that is available outside the trust boundary, but it is not intended to identify internally unused roles or permissions.

choices.text: IAM Access Analyzer unused access analysis
choices.explanation: It identifies roles and certain permissions that have not been used during a configured analysis period, so their necessity can be reviewed.

choices.text: IAM policy simulator
choices.explanation: It can evaluate whether specified actions are allowed, but it does not report whether existing permissions have actually been used.

choices.text: IAM Access Analyzer policy validation
choices.explanation: It evaluates policy syntax and practices, but it does not track how existing permissions are used.

source.label: IAM Access Analyzerの未使用アクセスの検出

learning.reason: IAM Access Analyzer unused access analysis can produce findings for unused roles and permissions.
learning.concept: The scope of permitted access, whether it is actually used, and whether it is shared externally are separate things to investigate.

sourceLabel: Detecting unused access with IAM Access Analyzer

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Let the Bucket Owner Own S3 Objects Written from Other Accounts
prompt: Departments save documents to a central S3 bucket from their respective AWS accounts. You want the bucket-owning account to own the objects and to control access with policies without using ACLs. Which S3 Object Ownership setting should you use?

choices.text: Object writer
choices.explanation: The account that writes the object owns it. This does not meet the central ownership requirement.

choices.text: Bucket owner preferred
choices.explanation: The bucket owner can own uploads with a particular ACL, but this setting does not avoid the use of ACLs.

choices.text: Bucket owner enforced
choices.explanation: It disables ACLs and makes the bucket owner own existing and new objects.

choices.text: Enable S3 Block Public Access alone.
choices.explanation: It prevents public access, but by itself does not determine object ownership or whether ACLs are enabled.

learning.reason: Bucket owner enforced enables centralized ownership by the bucket owner and policy-based access management.
learning.concept: Controlling public access and determining who owns an object after it is written are different concerns.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Find Out Why an IAM Policy Alone Cannot Grant KMS Key Access
prompt: An application role in an AWS account has an IAM policy that allows it to use a customer managed KMS key in the same account. The key policy does not directly allow the role and does not delegate permissions to IAM for the account. There are no KMS grants and no explicit deny. What happens when the application tries to use the key?

choices.text: Because the role is in the same AWS account, a single IAM allow is always enough to use the key.
choices.explanation: An IAM allow alone does not authorize key use when the KMS key policy does not allow permissions to be used through IAM.

choices.text: If the key is enabled, every role can encrypt with it.
choices.explanation: Even when a key is enabled, the required permissions are evaluated separately.

choices.text: The key's creator can attach an S3 bucket policy to the role so it can use the key.
choices.explanation: A bucket policy controls permissions on the S3 side; it does not independently grant permission to use a KMS key.

choices.text: The role cannot use the key because the key policy provides neither the required permission nor delegation.
choices.explanation: If the key does not allow delegation to IAM, an identity-based policy allow alone is ineffective.

learning.reason: The key policy is central to KMS key permissions. For an IAM allow to authorize key use, the key policy must permit delegation through IAM or otherwise authorize the use.
learning.concept: Check not only for an explicit deny, but also for the conditions under which a policy allow applies to the KMS key.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Restore a KMS Key Scheduled for Deletion Before It Is Deleted
prompt: You accidentally scheduled a customer managed KMS key that is in use for deletion. The key is pending deletion, and the deletion has not completed. You need to be able to decrypt records previously encrypted with this key again. What should you do?

choices.text: Give a new key the same alias as the current key.
choices.explanation: Even with the same alias, it is a different key with different key material; you need the original key to decrypt existing ciphertext.

choices.text: Cancel the deletion schedule and, after the necessary checks, enable the original key.
choices.explanation: You can cancel the schedule before deletion. Immediately after cancellation, the key is disabled, so you must enable it before use.

choices.text: Resume decryption immediately with the key pending deletion.
choices.explanation: A key pending deletion cannot be used for cryptographic operations.

choices.text: Wait until deletion is complete, then restore the key from AWS KMS.
choices.explanation: A KMS key cannot be restored after deletion, so action is required during the waiting period.

learning.reason: When a key is pending deletion, you can cancel the deletion schedule. After cancellation, an authorized operator can enable the original key and resume use.
learning.concept: Pending deletion, disabled, enabled, and deleted are distinct states with different conditions for using or recovering a key.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Verify CloudTrail log file integrity after delivery to S3
prompt: An auditor wants to verify later whether logs delivered by CloudTrail to S3 were changed after delivery. Which feature lets the auditor check the hash from the time of delivery using a signed digest?

choices.text: CloudTrail log file integrity validation
choices.explanation: It can deliver signed digests that are used to verify whether logs were changed or deleted after delivery.

choices.text: CloudTrail event history
choices.explanation: It lets you search recent events, but does not verify whether saved log files were changed after delivery.

choices.text: Enable S3 Versioning.
choices.explanation: It can retain object versions, but it does not cryptographically prove the original content delivered by CloudTrail or whether anything was omitted.

choices.text: Enable server-side encryption in S3.
choices.explanation: It encrypts data at rest, but does not create signed digests for files delivered by CloudTrail.

learning.reason: When integrity validation is enabled, CloudTrail delivers digests that can be used to validate signatures and log hashes.
learning.concept: In addition to encryption and versioning, AWS provides a way to check whether data changed or went missing after delivery.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Check whether a backup plan meets a vault's minimum retention period
prompt: In AWS Backup, a vault locked in compliance mode with its grace period expired enforces a minimum retention period of 30 days. A new backup job saved to this vault specifies 7 days of retention under the current plan, and the job fails. What should you change to make the job succeed while preserving the vault's requirements?

choices.text: Unlock Vault Lock, create the 7-day backup, and then lock the vault again.
choices.explanation: After the compliance-mode grace period expires, the vault cannot be unlocked.

choices.text: Change the backup frequency from weekly to daily and keep the 7-day retention period.
choices.explanation: This changes how often jobs run, but each recovery point still has a retention period below the minimum.

choices.text: Change the backup plan's retention period to at least 30 days, within the range allowed by the vault.
choices.explanation: The retention period for the new backup meets the vault's minimum. Keep it within the allowed range if a maximum is also configured.

choices.text: Add administrator permissions to the backup role and keep the 7-day retention period.
choices.explanation: Broader permissions do not satisfy the retention requirements applied to the vault.

learning.reason: A backup job fails when it tries to create a backup with a retention period shorter than the Vault Lock minimum. Set a retention period within the allowed range in the backup plan.
learning.concept: The vault's retention requirements and the retention period specified for a backup job are configured separately.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Run an approved remediation for an AWS Config compliance violation
prompt: An AWS Config rule detects that a resource's configuration does not meet an internal standard. In addition to notifying the team, they want to configure a reviewed remediation procedure to run in Systems Manager after detection. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Display only the AWS Config evaluation result.
choices.explanation: This lets you review the status but does not start remediation when a violation is detected.

choices.text: Associate a Systems Manager Automation runbook with an AWS Config remediation action.
choices.explanation: It can use the rule result to start approved operations as a runbook, automatically or manually.

choices.text: Only collect the target's data with Systems Manager Inventory.
choices.explanation: This collects asset information but does not change the configuration based on an AWS Config rule result.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail event history to identify who changed the configuration.
choices.explanation: This can identify the actor during an audit, but does not remediate the noncompliant value.

learning.reason: AWS Config can associate remediation actions that use AWS Systems Manager Automation documents with rules.
learning.concept: Producing a rule evaluation result and defining an action to run after a violation are separate tasks.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Distinguish temporary credential expiration from what to do afterward
prompt: A scheduled process uses a legitimate identity provider to obtain temporary IAM role credentials. When the process resumes after an interruption, the saved session credentials have expired. What is the appropriate way to continue accessing AWS?

choices.text: Use the same access key ID and secret with a token from a different session.
choices.explanation: Each component of temporary credentials is issued for the same session. You cannot combine them with a token from another session.

choices.text: Increase the role's maximum session duration and keep using the expired credentials.
choices.explanation: This may affect sessions obtained in the future, but it does not make already-issued, expired credentials valid again.

choices.text: Obtain and use new temporary credentials from the authorized identity provider.
choices.explanation: A new session provides a new set of credentials with an expiration time. Use the values as a set.

choices.text: Omit the session token and use the same keys as long-term credentials.
choices.explanation: Temporary credentials require their corresponding valid token, and expired keys cannot be used as long-term credentials.

learning.reason: AWS temporary credentials cannot be used after they expire. New credentials must be obtained to continue accessing AWS.
learning.concept: How short-term credentials are issued and how expired credentials are handled are separate considerations.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: View Security Hub CSPM findings from multiple Regions in one place
prompt: A company uses Security Hub CSPM in multiple Regions. Without switching Regions each time, the security team wants to view findings from linked Regions in one designated Region. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Enable the same security standard in each Region only.
choices.explanation: This evaluates resources against the same standard, but does not aggregate findings from other Regions into one Region.

choices.text: Set up a delegated administrator for multiple accounts only.
choices.explanation: This supports account governance, but configuring the aggregation Region and linked Regions is a separate step.

choices.text: Use an AWS CloudTrail multi-Region trail.
choices.explanation: This can consolidate AWS API activity logs, but does not configure where Security Hub CSPM findings are displayed.

choices.text: Configure a home Region and linked Regions using Security Hub CSPM cross-Region aggregation.
choices.explanation: You can view the in-scope findings from linked Regions in the home Region.

learning.reason: With Security Hub CSPM cross-Region aggregation, you designate a home Region and the Regions linked to it.
learning.concept: Distinguish multi-account management from the configuration that lets you view findings from multiple Regions in one place.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Set a permissions ceiling on IAM roles created by a delegated team
prompt: A platform team delegates creation of application IAM roles to a development team. Regardless of what permissions the new roles' identity-based policies specify, the roles must not exceed the scope set by the platform team, and existing unrelated roles must not be affected. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Restrict the delegated permissions so that the specified permissions boundary is attached when each role is created.
choices.explanation: A permissions boundary defines the scope that each role's identity-based policies can allow.

choices.text: Apply the same SCP to the organization's root.
choices.explanation: This can restrict permissions, but it affects a broader set of accounts in the organization.

choices.text: Only place the development users in the same IAM group.
choices.explanation: This can manage developers' permissions, but does not set a ceiling on each role they create.

choices.text: Restrict only the trust policies of roles that can be created.
choices.explanation: This limits which principals can use a role, but does not set a ceiling on the AWS actions the role can perform.

learning.reason: A permissions boundary sets the maximum scope that an IAM principal's identity-based policies can allow. Creation conditions can require that boundary to be applied.
learning.concept: The principals that can create a role, assume it, and the permissions ceiling on the role are separate controls.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Continuously assess unintended network paths to EC2
prompt: A security team is assessing the security posture of EC2. In addition to vulnerabilities in individual packages, the team wants vulnerability management findings that identify unintended network reachability to EC2 resulting from VPC configuration. Which Amazon Inspector finding type meets this need?

choices.text: Use only Inspector's operating system package vulnerability assessment.
choices.explanation: This assessment checks weaknesses in installed packages; it is a different finding type from one that identifies network reachability.

choices.text: Inspect images with Inspector's enhanced ECR scanning.
choices.explanation: This assesses packages and other components in stored images. It does not inspect network paths to running EC2 instances.

choices.text: Use VPC Flow Logs to check only traffic that actually flowed.
choices.explanation: This can show observed traffic, but differs from assessing reachability based on configuration, including when no traffic has been observed.

choices.text: Review Inspector's EC2 network reachability findings.
choices.explanation: This finding type assesses configuration-based exposure, such as network paths that allow access to EC2.

learning.reason: Amazon Inspector can generate findings about network reachability in addition to package vulnerabilities on EC2.
learning.concept: Distinguish known software weaknesses, traffic that actually occurred, and reachability based on configuration.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Control bursts of HTTP requests by source
prompt: A public web application is affected when many requests arrive from the same source within a set period. The goal is to let ordinary sources continue using the application while AWS WAF counts requests per source and applies protective measures to groups that exceed a configured threshold. Which feature is appropriate?

choices.text: Use only an AWS WAF IP set match rule.
choices.explanation: This can match specified IP addresses, but does not evaluate request counts over a period.

choices.text: Use an AWS WAF rate-based rule.
choices.explanation: It can group requests using specified aggregation keys and apply an action to groups based on their rate.

choices.text: Use only an AWS WAF regex pattern match rule.
choices.explanation: This can inspect request content, but does not evaluate the number of requests per source over a period.

choices.text: Configure only the AWS WAF Count action.
choices.explanation: This can record matching requests, but by itself it does not apply protective measures to groups that exceed a threshold.

learning.reason: A rate-based rule controls requests that exceed a specified rate limit based on aggregation criteria and the evaluation period.
learning.concept: Known IP addresses, request content, and request counts accumulated over a period are different evaluation criteria.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Issue TLS certificates for internal services using an organization-managed certificate authority
prompt: A company uses TLS for a private business service. Client devices can be configured to trust a certificate authority chosen by the company. The company wants to issue certificates for internal names through an organization-operated certificate hierarchy, rather than use certificates trusted broadly on the internet. Which AWS capability is appropriate?

choices.text: Request a public certificate through ACM and use a public certificate authority.
choices.explanation: Public certificates are suited to uses where broad trust is needed, but they do not provide issuance through a private certificate hierarchy managed by the organization.

choices.text: Import an externally issued certificate into ACM once.
choices.explanation: An existing certificate can be registered, but this does not create a private certificate authority for ongoing issuance.

choices.text: Configure a private certificate authority for the organization with AWS Private CA.
choices.explanation: The organization can issue certificates through its certificate hierarchy and configure client devices to trust its trust anchor for use with internal services.

choices.text: Distribute an AWS KMS symmetric key in place of a TLS certificate.
choices.explanation: A symmetric key can be used for data encryption, but it is not a certificate that uses a certificate authority’s signature to establish a TLS server’s identity.

source.label: 社内サービスのTLS証明書を組織が管理する認証局で発行する

learning.reason: AWS Private CA lets you manage private certificate authorities and certificate lifecycles. Clients must trust the relevant CA.
learning.concept: The trust anchor for signing private certificates applies to a different set of use cases than a publicly trusted certificate.

sourceLabel: Issue TLS certificates for internal services using an organization-managed certificate authority

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Identify Shield Advanced support and eligible cost protection
prompt: A company protects the relevant resources for a public application with Shield Advanced and also has AWS Enterprise Support. To plan its response to DDoS events, select TWO correct statements about support and cost protection.

choices.text: If the support conditions are met, the company can consult the Shield Response Team about an event.
choices.explanation: Under Shield Advanced protection and a qualifying AWS Support plan, the company can use the specialist assistance of the SRT.

choices.text: All cost increases for resources that have not been added as Shield-protected resources are covered.
choices.explanation: Shield Advanced cost protection is limited to cost increases that meet applicable conditions, including those for protected resources and eligible events.

choices.text: When a DDoS event occurs, all costs from past normal usage are automatically refunded in full.
choices.explanation: This is not a program that automatically refunds normal usage charges. It provides credits for eligible charges.

choices.text: The company can request the specified service credits for eligible cost increases caused by a DDoS attack on a protected resource.
choices.explanation: Cost increases that meet the applicable conditions may qualify for Shield Advanced cost protection.

choices.text: The application must be moved entirely to another AWS Region before the company can contact the SRT.
choices.explanation: SRT assistance requires a qualifying support plan and other applicable conditions, but moving Regions is not a general eligibility requirement.

source.label: DDoS対策の専門支援と対象料金の保護を確保する

learning.reason: Shield Advanced provides expert assistance subject to applicable conditions and service credits for eligible cost increases associated with DDoS events.
learning.concept: Distinguish technical protection, specialist assistance, and protection against eligible costs; check the conditions for each.

sourceLabel: Secure expert DDoS support and protection for eligible costs

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Protect an evidence version with no scheduled release date
prompt: The legal department wants to protect a specific object version in an S3 bucket that can use Object Lock from deletion or overwrite until an investigation is complete. The release date is unknown, and an authorized person will remove the protection when the investigation ends. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Set a provisional retention date in compliance mode.
choices.explanation: Strong protection remains in effect until that date, but this does not meet a requirement to leave the date unspecified and remove protection only after approval.

choices.text: Place a legal hold on the target object version.
choices.explanation: A legal hold has no fixed expiration date and protects the target version until an authorized principal removes it.

choices.text: Use bucket versioning alone.
choices.explanation: Versioning retains previous versions, but it does not prevent a principal with the necessary permissions from deleting a specific version.

choices.text: Configure expiration through an S3 Lifecycle rule.
choices.explanation: This makes an object eligible for deletion at a specified time; it does not protect it until the hold is released.

learning.reason: An Object Lock legal hold is applied to a version and remains in effect independently of retention periods until an authorized person removes it.
learning.concept: Distinguish protection based on a fixed date from protection based on a decision, such as the conclusion of an investigation.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Use the same work desktop after changing devices
prompt: A company wants employees who work from home or while traveling to continue using the same Windows desktop assigned to each user. They must be able to use their business applications and personal desktop settings after reconnecting from another device. Which AWS-managed virtual desktop option meets this need?

choices.text: Amazon WorkSpaces Pools
choices.explanation: It provides shared, nonpersistent desktops, which differs from the goal of assigning the same desktop to each person over the long term.

choices.text: Build a company-managed remote desktop environment on Amazon EC2.
choices.explanation: This can provide desktops, but the company must design and operate the assignment and remote desktop infrastructure.

choices.text: Amazon WorkSpaces Personal
choices.explanation: It assigns a persistent desktop to each user and allows access from supported devices.

choices.text: Open company websites with Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser.
choices.explanation: It can provide browser access to web applications, but it does not meet the requirement for each person’s full Windows desktop.

learning.reason: WorkSpaces Personal assigns a persistent virtual desktop to a user so they can continue using the same work environment when they reconnect.
learning.concept: A desktop assigned persistently to a user serves a different purpose from a temporary environment drawn from a shared pool.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Use a platform to route customer calls to agents
prompt: A retailer is opening a new phone support line. It wants to play a greeting when a call arrives, place the call in a queue, and route it to an available agent. Which option does this without requiring the retailer to operate its own telephone exchange?

choices.text: Configure contact flows and queues in Amazon Connect Customer.
choices.explanation: It can handle calls, play greetings, hold callers, and connect them to agents.

choices.text: Define a bot conversation using Amazon Lex alone.
choices.explanation: It can recognize customer intent from speech, but it does not assign phone numbers or route calls to agents.

choices.text: Receive support emails with Amazon SES.
choices.explanation: It can process email, but it cannot queue incoming calls and assign them to agents.

choices.text: Place records containing phone numbers in Amazon SQS.
choices.explanation: It can store messages, but it cannot receive voice calls or connect callers to agents.

learning.reason: Amazon Connect Customer provides a cloud contact center where call flows, queues, and routing to agents can be configured.
learning.concept: Distinguish conversational processing from a contact center that manages the path from an incoming call to an agent.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Provide previews for each frontend change
prompt: A web team wants to publish a frontend built with a supported framework and managed in Git. It needs managed hosting that can connect to the repository, continuously deploy changes, and provide previews for review. Which service should it choose?

choices.text: Use only the static website hosting feature of Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: It can serve static assets, but that feature alone does not connect to Git or deploy previews.

choices.text: Build the Git source with AWS CodeBuild alone.
choices.explanation: It can run builds, but hosting a site for browser access and providing previews require additional services.

choices.text: Manage the public domain with Amazon Route 53 alone.
choices.explanation: It provides DNS, but it cannot build and publish a site from source code.

choices.text: Connect the repository to AWS Amplify Hosting and configure deployments and previews.
choices.explanation: It can use Git changes to build and publish the frontend, and provide previews with supported configurations.

learning.reason: Amplify Hosting provides Git-based continuous builds and hosting, and can also provide web previews for changes when configured accordingly.
learning.concept: Distinguish an integrated frontend build-and-hosting service from standalone build or delivery features.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Run managed source compilation and tests
prompt: CI workflow orchestration is already in place. The team also needs a managed AWS build environment that uses a specified toolchain to compile source code, run tests, and produce artifacts. Which service should it use so it does not have to maintain build servers?

choices.text: Create stages in AWS CodePipeline without specifying a build execution provider.
choices.explanation: It manages release workflows, but an environment that runs the specified toolchain must still be configured.

choices.text: Define the build environment and commands in AWS CodeBuild.
choices.explanation: It can run compilation, tests, and artifact generation in a managed environment.

choices.text: Configure deployments with AWS CodeDeploy alone.
choices.explanation: It deploys existing artifacts but does not provide an environment to compile source code.

choices.text: Register container images rather than source code in Amazon ECR.
choices.explanation: It stores images but does not compile or test source code.

learning.reason: CodeBuild runs source compilation and tests in a build environment and produces deployable artifacts.
learning.concept: Distinguish a service that coordinates release stages from one that executes build processing.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Trace the work behind a slow request
prompt: An application API calls multiple services. Some users experience latency, and the team wants to trace which services a single request passed through and how long each segment took. Average CPU and aggregated metrics alone do not help narrow down the cause. Which feature is appropriate?

choices.text: Inspect configuration change times for each service with AWS Config.
choices.explanation: It can track configuration changes, but it does not record the processing path of an individual user request.

choices.text: Review service management API calls with AWS CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: It is useful for auditing API activity in AWS, but it does not show an application's request-processing path.

choices.text: Collect distributed traces from the application with AWS X-Ray.
choices.explanation: It can follow the services involved in a request and help investigate processing time and errors.

choices.text: Add only a CPU alarm in Amazon CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: It can notify the team when CPU exceeds a threshold, but it cannot show which dependency is slowing a specific request.

learning.reason: X-Ray traces requests in distributed applications and provides visibility into their paths and latency across services.
learning.concept: Aggregated metrics show overall trends, while distributed traces let you follow the path of an individual request.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Getting AWS coding and test suggestions in an IDE
prompt: An application developer wants to ask questions about using the AWS SDK in an IDE and get code completions and test drafts tailored to the code currently being edited. The team will perform the reviews and run the tests themselves. Which service is suitable for this developer assistance?

choices.text: Use Amazon Q Developer in a supported IDE.
choices.explanation: It can answer questions about code and AWS services and provide suggestions tailored to the code being edited.

choices.text: Run tests with AWS CodeBuild.
choices.explanation: It can build and test code that has already been written, but it does not interactively suggest code in the IDE.

choices.text: Visualize application traffic with AWS X-Ray.
choices.explanation: It analyzes traces from a running application and does not suggest how to use the AWS SDK while code is being edited.

choices.text: Deploy resource definitions with AWS CloudFormation.
choices.explanation: It can manage AWS resources from templates, but it does not generate suggestions for functions or tests in the IDE.

learning.reason: Amazon Q Developer assists with AWS questions, code completions, and code creation in supported IDEs.
learning.concept: A tool that suggests code to developers serves a different purpose from a service that runs builds or tests.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Restricting AWS Client VPN destinations by user group
prompt: A company already authenticates employees with AWS Client VPN and has configured routes to two business networks. It wants to grant access to the accounting network only to the accounting group. Which Client VPN setting associates a destination with a group?

choices.text: VPC name resolution settings
choices.explanation: These settings determine whether names can be resolved to IP addresses; they do not grant destination access by employee group.

choices.text: A Client VPN authorization rule
choices.explanation: It specifies a destination network and the user group allowed to access it.

choices.text: The Client VPN route table alone
choices.explanation: It provides a forwarding path to the destination, but destination access for individual groups must be authorized separately.

choices.text: A route in the VPC public subnet
choices.explanation: This setting is used for paths such as internet access and does not control authorization for groups authenticated through Client VPN.

source.label: AWS Client VPNの接続先を利用者のグループごとに制限する

learning.reason: A Client VPN authorization rule lets you specify which group can access a particular network.
learning.concept: User authentication, a route to a destination, and authorization for a group to access that destination are separate settings.

sourceLabel: Restricting AWS Client VPN destinations by user group

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Accepting custom TCP traffic with fixed IP addresses
prompt: A company exposes a custom TCP service that is not HTTPS in a single AWS Region. Its business partners add the destination's fixed IP addresses to their allowlists. Without changing the application, which load balancer distributes TCP connections across multiple healthy targets?

choices.text: An Application Load Balancer HTTPS listener
choices.explanation: It is used for HTTP and HTTPS traffic; it is not a listener that forwards a custom TCP protocol as is.

choices.text: Amazon CloudFront delivery
choices.explanation: It is suitable for delivery over HTTP or HTTPS, not as a load balancer for arbitrary TCP protocols.

choices.text: A Network Load Balancer TCP listener
choices.explanation: It forwards TCP traffic and can provide a fixed-IP entry point in each Availability Zone.

choices.text: An Amazon API Gateway HTTP API
choices.explanation: It exposes an HTTP API and does not forward TCP sessions using a custom protocol as is.

learning.reason: A Network Load Balancer provides TCP-level load balancing and can provide fixed IP addresses for each enabled Availability Zone.
learning.concept: Distinguish features that handle HTTP headers or paths from those that forward TCP connections.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Improving transfers to the same S3 bucket from remote locations
prompt: Production sites around the world upload large production files to the same S3 bucket in one AWS Region. Without adding another destination bucket, which AWS-provided feature improves the long-distance transfer path?

choices.text: Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication
choices.explanation: It can replicate data to another bucket after it reaches S3, but it does not improve the upload path from the site to the original bucket.

choices.text: Amazon S3 multipart upload alone
choices.explanation: It helps with parallel transfers and retrying individual parts, but by itself it does not change the long-distance network path.

choices.text: CloudFront caching for static content
choices.explanation: This cache is for delivering existing content; it is not a setting that caches uploads to improve the transfer path.

choices.text: S3 Transfer Acceleration
choices.explanation: Using the transfer acceleration endpoint for a supported bucket lets you route traffic through an edge location and the AWS network.

learning.reason: S3 Transfer Acceleration uses the AWS edge network for transfers between remote clients and S3.
learning.concept: A feature that changes the network path and one that splits an upload into parts can be used together, but they serve different purposes.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Resolve VPC private names from on-premises DNS
prompt: An on-premises application can reach a VPC over an existing Site-to-Site VPN. You want the on-premises DNS server to conditionally forward queries for names in a Route 53 private hosted zone associated with the VPC. Which component should you provision on the VPC side?

choices.text: A Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint
choices.explanation: It lets the on-premises DNS server forward queries to the Resolver in the VPC.

choices.text: Only a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint
choices.explanation: This is used when the VPC forwards queries to external DNS servers. The query direction is the opposite of what is required.

choices.text: A Route 53 public hosted zone with the same name
choices.explanation: A public DNS zone does not resolve the contents of the VPC's existing private hosted zone.

choices.text: Redo only the in-account association of the private hosted zone on the VPC side.
choices.explanation: This allows resolution in the VPC, but does not provide a forwarding destination for the on-premises DNS server.

learning.reason: Queries traveling from the network into the VPC are received by an inbound endpoint.
learning.concept: Check which way the query travels from the client that needs DNS resolution.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Store regenerable working data on EC2 local storage
prompt: An EC2 instance processes regenerable intermediate files for image conversion. You can choose an instance type that supports the needed option. Which storage is attached directly to the host, does not carry over to another instance, and may be lost when the instance is stopped or terminated?

choices.text: An Amazon EBS volume
choices.explanation: It is a block device, but it is not temporary storage attached directly to the host of the instance.

choices.text: An Amazon EFS file system
choices.explanation: It is a shared network file system that can be used by multiple clients.

choices.text: EC2 instance store
choices.explanation: It is temporary block storage directly attached to the host and is suitable for regenerable scratch data.

choices.text: An Amazon S3 bucket
choices.explanation: It is network-accessed object storage, not a temporary disk attached to the instance host.

learning.reason: Instance store is local storage on the host of a supported instance, and data is lost when the instance is stopped or terminated.
learning.concept: Separate data that must be retained from temporary data that can be regenerated if lost.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Manage software license usage against contract terms
prompt: A company brings contract-authorized software to multiple EC2 instances. It wants to track usage and manage limits based on the contract's counting method, and prevent license overuse for supported launches. Which AWS service manages the license terms?

choices.text: EC2 Dedicated Hosts alone
choices.explanation: They can help track physical sockets and host placement, but this setup alone does not manage license counting rules or limits.

choices.text: AWS Organizations consolidated billing
choices.explanation: It can consolidate charges, but does not track contract usage counts for bring-your-own software.

choices.text: The contract console in AWS Artifact
choices.explanation: It handles applicable agreements with AWS; it does not count third-party licenses used on EC2 instances.

choices.text: AWS License Manager
choices.explanation: You can create license configurations that reflect contract terms and manage usage and limits for supported resources.

learning.reason: License Manager can manage usage and limits based on license terms.
learning.concept: Distinguish managing contract usage from managing charges or physical host placement.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Move EFS files back to EFS Standard after first access
prompt: You use EFS lifecycle management to move shared files to an infrequent-access storage class. When a file starts being used again, you want it to return automatically to the EFS Standard storage class after its first access. The application's file path must not change. Which setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Copy the files from EFS to S3 and manage the storage class with S3 Lifecycle.
choices.explanation: An EFS setting will not detect reaccess on the S3 side, and this does not return the original file to EFS Standard.

choices.text: Use the EFS lifecycle management setting that transitions files to Standard on first access.
choices.explanation: After an eligible file in an infrequent-access class is accessed, it can transition to Standard in the same file system.

choices.text: Only shorten the number of days before transitioning files to EFS infrequent access.
choices.explanation: This changes when unread files are transitioned, but does not return files to Standard when they are accessed again.

choices.text: Only change the EFS throughput mode.
choices.explanation: This may change how file system performance is calculated, but it does not return files to another storage class.

learning.reason: EFS lets you configure a lifecycle policy to move eligible files, such as files in an infrequent-access class, to Standard after their first access.
learning.concept: Consider separately the setting that moves files to an infrequent-access class after a period without access and the setting that returns them to Standard when accessed again.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Preserve order within each order while processing separate orders in parallel
prompt: An order system using Amazon SQS must process the creation, modification, and cancellation of each order in the order they were submitted. Different orders do not need to be ordered relative to one another and should be processed in parallel. How should message groups be divided in the FIFO queue?

choices.text: Put every order in the same message group.
choices.explanation: Messages for all orders would be in one group, so separate orders could not be processed independently in parallel across groups.

choices.text: Use the operation type as the message group.
choices.explanation: The creation and cancellation of the same order would be placed in different groups, so the order of operations within that order would not be preserved.

choices.text: Use the order ID as the message group.
choices.explanation: Messages for the same order would be processed in submission order, while different orders could be processed as separate groups.

choices.text: Assign a different group ID to every operation.
choices.explanation: Each message would be in its own group, which would not preserve the order of operations within the same order.

source.label: 注文ごとに順番を維持し、別々の注文は並行処理する

learning.reason: SQS FIFO preserves order within the same message group and allows independent processing across different groups.
learning.concept: A total order across all events is different from preserving order within each business unit.

sourceLabel: Preserve order within each order while processing separate orders in parallel

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Choose the container runtime settings specified in an ECS task definition
prompt: An application is being deployed to multiple development environments with Amazon ECS. The goal is to separate the container runtime configuration from operational settings determined by the service. Choose two items that belong in an ECS task definition.

choices.text: The number of tasks an ECS service maintains under normal conditions
choices.explanation: The number maintained by a service is an ECS service setting, not part of the template for the container runtime configuration.

choices.text: The image used by the container
choices.explanation: The container definition in the task definition specifies the image to run.

choices.text: The retention rule for expiring images in ECR
choices.explanation: This is managed through the repository lifecycle and is not part of how an ECS task runs.

choices.text: The maximum desired task count for ECS service autoscaling
choices.explanation: This is a service scaling setting, not an individual container requirement specified in a task definition.

choices.text: The CPU and memory requirements for the container or task
choices.explanation: A task definition can specify compute resource requirements.

source.label: ECSコンテナのイメージや必要メモリを定義する

learning.reason: An ECS task definition records runtime specifications such as the image to launch and CPU and memory requirements.
learning.concept: Resource requirements, management of stored images, and ECS service operations are configured in different places.

sourceLabel: Define the image and required memory for ECS containers

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Share only a specific S3 object through a time-limited URL
prompt: A company wants to share a single sample file in a private S3 bucket with a business partner who does not have an AWS account, for a short time. The bucket's public access settings must not be changed, and the person sharing the file has permission to retrieve the object. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Make object reads public to everyone in the S3 bucket policy.
choices.explanation: Unauthenticated retrieval would be possible, but this would not meet the requirements to keep the bucket's public access settings unchanged and limit access to a time-limited URL.

choices.text: Generate an S3 presigned URL for retrieving the object, with an expiration time.
choices.explanation: While the signature is valid, the recipient can use the URL to perform the specified operation on the object. The expiration of the signing credentials also affects validity.

choices.text: Send only the ordinary S3 object URL.
choices.explanation: For a private object, the ordinary URL alone does not give the business partner permission to retrieve it.

choices.text: Allow the business partner's AWS account in the bucket policy.
choices.explanation: This can be used to share with someone who has an AWS account, but this partner does not have one.

learning.reason: An S3 presigned URL grants its holder permission to perform a specified operation within its validity period, based on the signing principal's permissions.
learning.concept: When sharing temporarily without changing a public policy, account for the fact that anyone who receives the URL can access the object.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Handle unpredictable DynamoDB demand based on actual usage
prompt: A newly launched service has irregular DynamoDB read and write traffic, and the team wants to avoid having to predict and configure capacity units for now. Which capacity mode uses capacity in response to request volume?

choices.text: On-demand capacity mode
choices.explanation: There is no need to configure read and write capacity units in advance, and charges are based on requests.

choices.text: Fixed provisioned capacity
choices.explanation: This requires specifying read and write capacity in advance.

choices.text: Provisioned capacity with auto scaling
choices.explanation: Although capacity can be adjusted automatically, this approach requires specifying values such as minimum and maximum capacity.

choices.text: Add DAX while retaining provisioned capacity.
choices.explanation: DAX can accelerate reads, but it does not change the table's read and write capacity mode.

learning.reason: DynamoDB on-demand mode responds to requests without requiring the application to provision capacity in advance.
learning.concept: Even with usage-based billing, check the service's scaling characteristics and limits.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Transforming multiple raw data sources and writing them to an analytics destination
prompt: The analytics team regularly reads raw data from multiple sources in S3, transforms it into datasets with consistent column names and types, and writes the results to a different S3 location. The team needs to run existing ETL processes continuously without managing processing servers or clusters. Which AWS feature is appropriate?

choices.text: Register only the raw data columns in the AWS Glue Data Catalog.
choices.explanation: This records data definitions, but a separate process is still needed to perform the transformations and write the results to the destination.

choices.text: Run only a sample aggregation SELECT query in Amazon Athena.
choices.explanation: Athena can query data for analysis, but this does not run scheduled ETL jobs or produce a new dataset as required.

choices.text: Change the Amazon S3 storage class with a lifecycle rule.
choices.explanation: This can change the storage class, but it does not transform column names or types inside files.

choices.text: Run a serverless AWS Glue ETL job on a schedule.
choices.explanation: The job can run the defined transformations and produce a dataset for analysis.

learning.reason: AWS Glue provides managed ETL that can retrieve and transform data, then write it to an analytics destination.
learning.concept: Managing data metadata and transforming the data itself are different tasks.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Configuring in-progress message handling and repeated-failure behavior in SQS
prompt: A worker receives and processes an Amazon SQS message, then deletes it if processing succeeds. After a message is received, it should remain hidden from other workers only during the processing grace period. Messages that reach a specified number of failures should be examined in a separate queue. Which two settings should be configured?

choices.text: Only shorten the message retention period.
choices.explanation: The retention period controls how long a message is stored in the queue; it does not configure post-receipt invisibility or movement based on failure count.

choices.text: Configure a delivery delay for messages when they are sent.
choices.explanation: This sets how long a message waits before it can first be received; it does not provide a processing grace period after receipt.

choices.text: Configure the visibility timeout after receipt.
choices.explanation: After receipt, the message is generally hidden from other workers for a set period. If it is not deleted before that period expires, it becomes available for receipt again.

choices.text: Only change the standard queue to a FIFO queue.
choices.explanation: This changes features related to ordering and deduplication, but a separate policy is still needed to move messages to another queue.

choices.text: Configure a dead-letter queue and the maximum receive count that triggers movement.
choices.explanation: Messages that are not processed and deleted can be moved to an examination queue when they reach the receive-count limit.

learning.reason: The SQS visibility timeout sets the temporary period of invisibility after receipt, while a dead-letter queue policy determines how to handle messages that repeatedly cannot be processed.
learning.concept: The processing grace period after receipt and the isolation of messages that repeatedly fail are separate settings.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Returning a DNS response that points to a standby site when the primary site has an issue
prompt: A company normally uses its website in the Tokyo Region with a custom domain. While the Tokyo site is considered unhealthy, the company wants DNS responses for the same name to switch to its standby site in Virginia. The company does not need to intentionally distribute traffic between the two sites during normal operation. Which Route 53 routing policy is appropriate?

choices.text: Use weighted routing and assign the same weight to both sites.
choices.explanation: This distributes responses between both sites during normal operation and does not meet the requirement to prioritize Tokyo and switch only when it is unhealthy.

choices.text: Use geolocation routing to select a site based on the user's location.
choices.explanation: This changes the destination based on the user's location; it does not switch to a standby site based on the primary site's health.

choices.text: Register both site values using simple routing only.
choices.explanation: Multiple response values can be registered, but this does not configure a failover role that prioritizes a healthy primary.

choices.text: Use health evaluation and failover routing to specify a primary and secondary site.
choices.explanation: This uses the primary while it is healthy and can return the standby site when the primary is unhealthy.

learning.reason: Failover routing sets a primary and secondary site and switches the response based on health status.
learning.concept: DNS caching affects failover timing. Distinguish failover from traffic distribution and routing based on geographic location.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Maintaining copies of new S3 objects in another Region
prompt: A company wants audit files added to an S3 bucket in one Region in the future to be automatically replicated asynchronously to an S3 bucket in another Region. Existing files are out of scope, and the company can configure prerequisites such as versioning for both buckets. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Run S3 Batch Replication once.
choices.explanation: This can replicate existing objects and other objects in a batch, but a single run does not continuously replicate objects added in the future.

choices.text: Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication.
choices.explanation: After configuration, objects added to the source bucket that match the rule can be continuously replicated to a bucket in another Region.

choices.text: Use an S3 Lifecycle transition to move objects to an infrequent access storage class.
choices.explanation: This changes the storage class in the same bucket; it does not create a copy in another Region.

choices.text: Configure S3 Transfer Acceleration on the source bucket.
choices.explanation: This improves the transfer path between clients and a bucket; it does not continuously replicate objects between buckets.

learning.reason: S3 live replication asynchronously replicates new objects according to a rule. Use CRR when the destination is in another Region.
learning.concept: Continuous replication of new objects and batch replication of existing objects happen through different processes.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Collect OS and application inventories from managed EC2 instances
prompt: An operations team wants to periodically collect and centrally review the running OS versions and installed applications across multiple EC2 instances managed by Systems Manager. Which Systems Manager capability collects information from each instance?

choices.text: Systems Manager Inventory
choices.explanation: It collects configuration data such as software and OS details from managed nodes and can create an asset inventory.

choices.text: Systems Manager Patch Manager
choices.explanation: It is used to apply patches and check patch compliance. The stated goal is to collect overall software information from the nodes.

choices.text: Systems Manager Session Manager
choices.explanation: It provides interactive access to individual instances, but it does not periodically collect asset information across multiple nodes.

choices.text: Systems Manager Parameter Store
choices.explanation: It manages configuration values for applications to retrieve; it does not inspect installed software.

learning.reason: Systems Manager Inventory collects metadata about managed nodes, including their configuration and installed applications.
learning.concept: Distinguish applying changes from collecting and understanding the current state.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Allocate socket-based licenses to EC2 instances
prompt: A company owns commercial licenses that it is permitted to bring to AWS. It must allocate licenses by the number of physical sockets and be able to audit which instances were placed on specific physical hosts. Which EC2 option is appropriate?

choices.text: Use EC2 Dedicated Instances.
choices.explanation: The hardware is not shared with other accounts, but the specific physical host and socket information for each placement are not managed.

choices.text: Use EC2 Dedicated Hosts.
choices.explanation: Host information and instance placement can be managed, supporting the tracking of licenses based on the corresponding physical units.

choices.text: Launch EC2 instances with default tenancy and add cost allocation tags.
choices.explanation: Tags can categorize costs, but they do not manage physical socket-level allocation information or instance placement.

choices.text: Purchase regional Reserved Instances.
choices.explanation: These apply discounts to eligible usage costs; they do not manage hardware allocation and placement.

learning.reason: Dedicated Hosts allocate dedicated physical servers and provide visibility into information such as physical sockets and host placement.
learning.concept: After confirming that BYOL is permitted, check what physical unit the license counts and whether the host in use is visible.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Exchange a reservation for a different EC2 family during the term
prompt: A company purchases EC2 Reserved Instances. During the term, it may need to switch to a different instance family or platform in the same Region. Which type of Reserved Instance can it exchange, provided it meets conditions such as those governing the value of the exchange?

choices.text: Regional Standard Reserved Instances
choices.explanation: They can discount eligible usage when attributes such as the instance family match, but they are not exchangeable for a different family or platform.

choices.text: Zonal Standard Reserved Instances
choices.explanation: They can provide capacity and discounts for matching usage in a specified Availability Zone, but do not offer exchanges for Reserved Instances in a different family.

choices.text: EC2 Instance Savings Plans
choices.explanation: Discounts apply when certain attributes change, but this is not a purchase option for exchanging Reserved Instances.

choices.text: Convertible Reserved Instances
choices.explanation: An eligible current reservation can be exchanged for a new reservation in a qualifying family or on a qualifying platform.

learning.reason: Convertible Reserved Instances can be exchanged for eligible Convertible Reserved Instances, including changes to the instance family or platform.
learning.concept: Distinguish size flexibility under specific conditions from exchanging a purchased reservation for one with different attributes.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Manage S3 data with unpredictable access patterns
prompt: A team stores documents that are each at least 1 MB in S3 for the long term. It cannot predict which documents will be read frequently again. Which configuration changes tiers based on observed access, requires no advance restoration from an archive tier, and incurs no additional data retrieval charges from the tier?

choices.text: Use S3 Standard-IA as a fixed tier for the entire retention period.
choices.explanation: Objects can be retrieved immediately, but the storage does not automatically tier based on changing access, and retrieval charges apply.

choices.text: Move all objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
choices.explanation: It suits low-frequency archival use, but objects generally must be restored before they can be retrieved.

choices.text: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering without enabling the optional asynchronous archive tiers.
choices.explanation: It uses instant-access tiers based on access frequency, and S3 Intelligent-Tiering has no data retrieval charges.

choices.text: Move objects to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval a fixed number of days after publication.
choices.explanation: Objects can be retrieved immediately, but retrieval charges apply, and this does not automatically move them back based on observed access.

learning.reason: Intelligent-Tiering moves eligible objects among its standard instant-access tiers and does not charge data retrieval fees. Monitoring and automation fees should be considered separately.
learning.concept: Distinguish moving objects to a fixed tier after a set time from automatically changing tiers based on access patterns.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Require approval before stopping test EC2 instances after a budget threshold is reached
prompt: The testing team wants to make it possible to stop EC2 instances designated for testing when AWS costs exceed a monthly budget threshold. To avoid stopping the wrong instances, the action must run only after an assigned team member receives a notification and approves it. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Create an action in AWS Budgets to stop the target EC2 instances and require manual approval.
choices.explanation: When the threshold is exceeded, the assigned team member is notified, and the target instances can be stopped only if the action is approved.

choices.text: Set up only an email notification for the threshold in AWS Budgets.
choices.explanation: The assigned team member can learn that the threshold was exceeded, but no action is configured to proceed from approval to stopping the instances.

choices.text: Automatically stop the instances 72 hours after they are launched in Amazon EC2.
choices.explanation: A time-based condition can be configured, but it does not evaluate the cost threshold or use the assigned team member's approval.

choices.text: Review the forecast in AWS Cost Explorer each month.
choices.explanation: This provides a spending forecast, but it does not trigger an approval and stop action when the threshold is exceeded.

source.label: AWS Budgetsアクションのレビューと承認

learning.reason: AWS Budgets actions can be configured to require approval from an assigned team member and, after approval, run an action on the applicable resources.
learning.concept: Budget notifications report the situation, while budget actions connect configured conditions and approvals to operations on resources.

sourceLabel: Review and approval of AWS Budgets actions

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Have a designated contact for ongoing architecture and operations advice
prompt: For a business service on AWS, the team needs a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM) whom it can consult on an ongoing basis about operations planning and architecture, in addition to technical questions during incidents. Which of the current plans shown is the lowest tier that provides a designated TAM?

choices.text: AWS Business Support+
choices.explanation: It provides access to technical support, but does not meet the requirement for the lowest plan that includes a designated TAM.

choices.text: AWS Enterprise Support
choices.explanation: It provides a designated TAM and ongoing operational advice and technical guidance.

choices.text: AWS Unified Operations
choices.explanation: It also provides access to a designated TAM, but offers a higher tier of operational support.

choices.text: Basic Support
choices.explanation: It includes basic account and billing support, but does not provide a designated TAM.

learning.reason: Enterprise Support provides a designated TAM for ongoing technical consultation and operational guidance.
learning.concept: Technical support available as needed differs from ongoing consultation with a designated account manager.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Use creator information that users do not have to enter manually for cost analysis
prompt: The finance team wants to use creator information in billing analysis for new resources that support automatic creator tagging, even if the person who creates a resource forgets to enter a tag. What is the key of the creator tag that AWS applies?

choices.text: A user-defined Owner tag
choices.explanation: This can represent the responsible person, but the option requires users to supply the tag value.

choices.text: A user-defined CostCenter tag
choices.explanation: This can identify the cost allocation destination, but it is not the key of an AWS-applied creator tag.

choices.text: The linked account ID in a Cost and Usage Report
choices.explanation: This can identify the account billed, but it is not an AWS-generated tag that identifies who created the resource.

choices.text: aws:createdBy
choices.explanation: For supported new resources, AWS can apply this tag to identify creator information. Check the tag's status when using it for billing.

source.label: AWS生成のコスト配分タグ

learning.reason: For resources that support automatic creator tagging, the AWS-generated cost allocation tag aws:createdBy can be used. Enabling the tag and ensuring that it applies to the resources and billing require additional conditions.
learning.concept: Distinguish AWS-generated tags from cost allocation tags that users create and apply.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Limit new purchases of third-party products to an approved list
prompt: The procurement team decides which third-party products each department may use in AWS Marketplace. Each department must be able to keep its account while purchasing only products approved for that department. Which feature is appropriate?

choices.text: Create a cost estimate for each department with AWS Pricing Calculator.
choices.explanation: This can estimate costs, but it does not restrict the Marketplace products available to each department.

choices.text: Create your own CloudFormation products in AWS Service Catalog.
choices.explanation: This can be used to provision approved infrastructure, but it does not configure department-level controls on new purchases of third-party Marketplace products.

choices.text: Manage each department's approved products in AWS Private Marketplace.
choices.explanation: You can specify the departments in scope and their approved product lists to manage procurement.

choices.text: Enable consolidated billing with AWS Organizations.
choices.explanation: This can consolidate payments, but it does not provide a list of approved products to show purchasers.

learning.reason: AWS Private Marketplace lets organizations manage lists of approved Marketplace products aligned with organizational units.
learning.concept: Distinguish the Marketplace, where third-party products are found and purchased, from Private Marketplace, which controls which products an organization can purchase.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Report suspected abuse of an AWS-hosted resource to the right channel
prompt: An organization's security team suspects that a public resource hosted on AWS by a third party is being used as a fraudulent site impersonating the organization. This is not a billing issue or service outage affecting the organization's AWS account. Which channel should they use to report the suspected abuse to AWS?

choices.text: The AWS abuse report form for AWS Trust & Safety
choices.explanation: This channel accepts reports of suspected abuse involving AWS resources.

choices.text: The AWS product vulnerability reporting channel
choices.explanation: This channel is for reporting defects in AWS services, not abuse involving a third party's site hosted on AWS.

choices.text: Open an account and billing case in AWS Support Center.
choices.explanation: This can be used for support with the organization's own billing or account, but it is not the dedicated channel for reporting abuse by a third party.

choices.text: Check AWS service status in the AWS Health Dashboard.
choices.explanation: This shows AWS service issues and maintenance, but it does not provide a way to report abuse involving a third party.

source.label: AWSリソースの不正利用を報告する

learning.reason: If you suspect abuse involving a resource hosted by AWS, use the AWS Trust & Safety abuse reporting channel.
learning.concept: Distinguish technical support for your own environment, disclosure of AWS product vulnerabilities, and reports of abuse involving a third party's resource.

sourceLabel: Report abuse involving an AWS resource

category: クラウドの概念
title: Keep retries from adding load during temporary congestion
prompt: An application that reads order status repeatedly retries immediately when a dependent service is temporarily congested, making the congestion worse. Short outages should be recoverable through retries, while the overall response deadline for the screen must still be met. Which two approaches should be used?

choices.text: Retry continuously without waiting for a response on every error from the dependent service.
choices.explanation: This also retries errors that will not recover, worsening the load on the dependency and response time.

choices.text: Space out retries, and retry only transient failures that are likely to recover.
choices.explanation: This prevents calls from piling up immediately after a failure and gives a temporary problem time to clear.

choices.text: Enable unlimited retries independently at every layer, including the client library and application.
choices.explanation: Retries can multiply across layers, making it difficult to control the total number of requests sent to the dependency and the time spent waiting.

choices.text: Always keep waiting for the dependency's response and never cancel, even when the caller has a deadline.
choices.explanation: This can exceed the overall response deadline.

choices.text: Limit the number of retries or their total elapsed time so they finish within the overall response deadline.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes temporary failures from situations that will not recover and prevents the operation from waiting indefinitely.

learning.reason: Space out retries for transient errors and set a limit on the retry count or elapsed time. Do not wait beyond the permitted response deadline.
learning.concept: Retries can help ride out temporary failures, but more frequent and concurrent calls add load to dependencies.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Let users read the latest value immediately after a change
prompt: A customer reads an item from a DynamoDB table in the same Region immediately after changing a setting. The write is confirmed successful, and there are no other updates before the read. No cache is used, and the read after the response must return the latest value. Which read should be selected?

choices.text: Use an eventually consistent read and assume that a successful write is reflected immediately.
choices.explanation: An eventually consistent read might not yet reflect the latest successful update.

choices.text: Wait a fixed number of seconds before every eventually consistent read.
choices.explanation: A fixed wait does not guarantee that the strict read requirement will be met.

choices.text: Perform a strongly consistent read from the table in question.
choices.explanation: A strongly consistent read from the table can reflect a write that completed successfully beforehand.

choices.text: Read the same data eventually consistently from a global secondary index.
choices.explanation: Reads from a global secondary index are eventually consistent and do not guarantee that the preceding write will be visible.

learning.reason: Request a strongly consistent read from the DynamoDB table to retrieve a value that reflects a previously successful write.
learning.concept: Distinguish use cases where a change can become visible later from those that require the result to be guaranteed immediately after a successful write.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Add serverless-specific guidance to a standard architecture review
prompt: A company conducts common architecture reviews using the Well-Architected Framework. For a new serverless application, it wants to continue applying general principles while also evaluating additional best practices suited to event-driven applications. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Apply the lens for serverless applications to the common framework.
choices.explanation: This preserves the common review areas while adding questions and recommendations tailored to the technology.

choices.text: Use only the Reliability pillar and omit the other pillars and serverless-specific questions.
choices.explanation: This focuses on resilience but does not retain the full scope of the common review or the serverless-specific questions.

choices.text: Evaluate the application's technical design using only the perspectives in the AWS CAF.
choices.explanation: The AWS CAF can help organize an organization's cloud adoption capabilities, but it is not a substitute for a workload framework and lens.

choices.text: Use only the cost checks in AWS Trusted Advisor to evaluate specialized design considerations.
choices.explanation: These checks can identify specific improvement opportunities, but they do not provide a technology-specific review of the entire workload.

learning.reason: AWS lenses provide review guidance for specific industries or technology areas. The standard framework can be combined with the lens for serverless applications.
learning.concept: Common review guidance and workload-specific questions can be applied in one review without dropping either.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Set data classifications first, then align protection levels
prompt: A company handles public materials, internal operational records, and sensitive customer data in the same workload. Before choosing storage services, it wants to define access restrictions and protection policies based on data classification. Which two actions should it take?

choices.text: Classify all materials based on their file sizes.
choices.explanation: Size can help determine storage costs, but it does not necessarily indicate a material’s sensitivity or the protection it requires.

choices.text: Give all data stored in AWS services the same classification and protection standard.
choices.explanation: Using only the storage destination as the basis does not account for the different handling requirements of public materials and personal information.

choices.text: Define classifications based on data owners and the data’s business importance or sensitivity.
choices.explanation: This helps determine the appropriate classification by considering the impact if data is disclosed, changed, or lost inappropriately.

choices.text: Define access and protection requirements for each classification and map them to the corresponding controls.
choices.explanation: This ensures that classifications inform actual decisions about permissions, encryption, and protection levels.

choices.text: Determine classifications only after adding elevated permissions for sensitive data.
choices.explanation: Required access should first be determined from the classification and business requirements. Adding permissions is not a prerequisite for classification.

learning.reason: Classify data by factors such as sensitivity and business importance, define the handling requirements for each classification, and apply them through actual controls.
learning.concept: Even when data is stored in the same service or looks similar, its purpose and importance can change the protection it requires.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Compare regional sustainability among candidates that meet business requirements
prompt: Two AWS Regions have the required services and both meet the users’ response-time objectives and data-residency requirements. Which approach should be used to reflect sustainability goals in the Region selection while preserving functionality?

choices.text: Always move to the Region with the best environmental electricity metric, even if doing so violates storage regulations.
choices.explanation: Environmental goals can be considered, but a choice that violates a mandatory data-residency requirement cannot be made.

choices.text: Choose the candidate with the lowest storage price and assume it has the same environmental ranking.
choices.explanation: A price difference does not directly represent differences in electricity carbon intensity or environmental impact.

choices.text: Choose the candidate with more Availability Zones and assume that alone means a lower environmental impact.
choices.explanation: The number of Availability Zones can be relevant to design, but it is not a measure of electricity use or resource efficiency.

choices.text: Compare environmental information, such as electricity carbon intensity, among candidates that meet the business requirements.
choices.explanation: This reflects sustainability considerations in the Region selection while preserving mandatory constraints.

source.label: 持続可能性に基づくリージョン選択

learning.reason: After identifying candidates that meet business requirements, compare sustainability-related information such as electricity carbon intensity.
learning.concept: Do not judge environmental impact solely by a Region’s price or distance; compare environmental metrics among candidates that meet the requirements.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Identify a deployment model that divides processing between a facility and AWS
prompt: A factory’s inspection equipment will continue processing data in an on-premises data center at the factory. It sends certain inspection results to AWS, where an analytics service exchanges data with the factory environment. Which deployment model uses both environments for business processing?

choices.text: Cloud-only deployment
choices.explanation: Some business processing continues at the factory, so this is not a configuration in which all processing is in AWS.

choices.text: Hybrid deployment
choices.explanation: The workload connects processing running on premises with AWS services.

choices.text: On-premises-only deployment
choices.explanation: The analytics service runs on AWS and is used for the business, so this model does not place everything on premises.

choices.text: Multi-Region cloud deployment
choices.explanation: This describes running infrastructure in multiple cloud Regions; it does not describe combining the factory environment with AWS.

source.label: AWSのクラウド展開モデル

learning.reason: A configuration that connects and uses an existing on-premises environment and the cloud is a hybrid deployment.
learning.concept: Determine the cloud deployment model by identifying where business processing runs and whether the environments are connected and used together.

category: クラウドの概念
title: See slow requests hidden by the average
