prompt: Most requests to a search API have short response times, but some are very slow. The success rate has not changed. The team wants to examine the boundary within which 95% of requests complete and compare whether the slow user experience has improved. Which statistic should it use?

choices.text: Average latency
choices.explanation: This shows the average of all observations, but not the response-time boundary within which 95% fall.

choices.text: Median latency
choices.explanation: This is the boundary at which approximately half of the observations fall, not the requested 95% boundary.

choices.text: Latency p95
choices.explanation: This statistic shows how long it took for the specified proportion of requests to complete.

choices.text: Maximum latency
choices.explanation: This shows the slowest single observation, which is generally different from the time within which 95% of requests complete.

learning.reason: The 95th percentile of latency is the boundary at or below which approximately 95% of observations fall.
learning.concept: The average, median, and higher percentiles describe different parts of the response-time distribution.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Switch to a validated separate environment while retaining the old one for rollback
prompt: Deploy a new version separately from the application environment currently in use, and validate it. After validation, move all production traffic to the new environment. If a problem occurs, route users back to the same old environment. Data compatibility can be ensured separately. Which deployment strategy fits this approach?

choices.text: Blue/green deployment, with both the old and new environments kept available
choices.explanation: The new environment can be validated in advance, and if a problem occurs with the new version, traffic can be routed back to the retained old environment.

choices.text: Rolling deployment, updating the nodes in the existing environment one at a time
choices.explanation: This supports a gradual update, but it does not match the approach of retaining the entire independent old environment and switching traffic back to it.

choices.text: Stop all instances in the existing environment and overwrite them at once
choices.explanation: This replaces the version, but does not retain the old running environment or allow traffic to be routed back to it.

choices.text: Canary deployment, directing some production users to the new environment first
choices.explanation: This deployment uses a portion of live traffic, whereas the stated approach is to switch all users at once after validation.

source.label: AWSのブルーグリーンデプロイ

learning.reason: Blue/green deployment keeps the old and new environments available in parallel, switches traffic after validation, and allows traffic to be routed back to the old environment if needed.
learning.concept: Consider environment replacement, traffic switching, and how long to retain the old environment as separate decisions.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Prepare the foundation and execution capability before scaling migration
prompt: An organization has completed its migration business case and readiness assessment. Next, before starting a large-scale migration, it wants to establish a scalable landing zone, automate security and operations, and gain hands-on experience with a small group of applications. Which phase of the AWS migration process is the most appropriate?

choices.text: Assess
choices.explanation: This phase evaluates current readiness, the portfolio, and the business case; implementing the foundation and gaining hands-on experience are not its primary goals.

choices.text: Mobilize
choices.explanation: Correct. This phase establishes the landing zone, operational readiness, and skills, and builds a foundation for large-scale migration through an initial group of applications.

choices.text: Migrate and modernize
choices.explanation: This phase uses the processes and foundation defined and validated in Mobilize to migrate and modernize applications at scale.

choices.text: CAF Envision
choices.explanation: This is a transformation-stage activity for defining goals and business outcomes, not the execution-readiness phase of the AWS migration process.

source.label: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Mobilize your organization

learning.reason: Mobilize builds on the plans and gaps identified in Assess to establish a landing zone, operational capabilities, skills, and experience from a small-scale migration.
learning.concept: CAF Envision/Align/Launch/Scale and the migration phases Assess/Mobilize/Migrate differ in purpose and level of detail.

sourceLabel: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Mobilize your organization

category: クラウドの概念
title: Reduce dependencies so services can be updated independently
prompt: In a retail site, every time the inventory service's internal data structure changes, the order service must also be updated on the same day. Both teams want to keep using the features while changing their internal implementations independently. Which design approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Change the design so both services read and write directly to the same internal table.
choices.explanation: Both services would have to accommodate changes to the shared table, so this would not reduce their change dependency.

choices.text: Require all services to be released together in the same week.
choices.explanation: This could align the timing of changes, but the services would still be unable to be updated independently.

choices.text: Have the services integrate through published interfaces so other services do not depend directly on their internal implementations or data.
choices.explanation: As long as the interface contract is maintained, internal changes can proceed without applying them to the other service at the same time.

choices.text: Always use the same size of compute capacity for both services.
choices.explanation: Matching resource sizes does not remove the dependency that propagates internal implementation changes.

source.label: サービスを別々に更新できるよう依存を減らす

learning.reason: A loosely coupled design uses clear interfaces for integration, separating changes to a service's internal implementation or data from other services.
learning.concept: Independent updates require reducing direct dependencies on other services' implementations, not merely running services separately.

sourceLabel: Reduce dependencies so services can be updated independently

category: クラウドの概念
title: Assess the schema before migrating to a different database engine
prompt: An organization is migrating from a commercial database to a different database engine. Some table definitions, data types, and stored procedures may not be compatible as is. What is the most appropriate item to plan before moving the data?

choices.text: Assess the source schema, identify what can be converted and what requires manual work, and then prepare a schema for the target.
choices.explanation: Correct. Between heterogeneous engines, plan to assess and review the schema conversion and handle any necessary manual work before migrating the data.

choices.text: Copy the data first, then define only the tables that produce errors in the target.
choices.explanation: Starting data migration without checking schema compatibility increases the risk of migration failures and rework.

choices.text: Assume all SQL and data types are identical across database engines and skip the assessment.
choices.explanation: Different database engines may require conversion or manual work for schema elements and code.

choices.text: Leave the schema unchanged and only increase the frequency of data backups.
choices.explanation: Backups are important, but they do not resolve schema compatibility issues between heterogeneous engines.

learning.reason: For a heterogeneous database migration, assess schema conversion separately from data migration, identify elements that cannot be converted automatically, and prepare the target schema.
learning.concept: This is a migration-planning decision about checking schema compatibility before moving data, not a choice of migration tool.

category: クラウドの概念
title: Manage migration assets by owner and configuration
prompt: Several departments are migrating applications. The program lead wants an inventory that tracks which servers, databases, and networks each application depends on, as well as who is responsible for business decisions. Which inventory management approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Record server names once, without tracking their relationship to applications or maintaining change history
choices.explanation: This does not track application-to-infrastructure mappings, dependencies, or changes, reducing the reliability of migration planning.

choices.text: Keep separate spreadsheets for each department and do not collect application owners’ contact information
choices.explanation: This makes it difficult to understand cross-department dependencies or coordinate with the owners needed for migration decisions.

choices.text: Use AWS billing information alone as the inventory and collect no pre-migration asset information
choices.explanation: Billing information alone does not show application configurations, dependencies, owners, or migration scope.

choices.text: Map applications to their components, centrally maintain an inventory that includes owners and dependencies, and assign someone to keep it up to date
choices.explanation: Correct. An accurate portfolio assessment requires centralizing application-to-infrastructure mappings, dependencies, and owner information, and keeping them up to date.

source.label: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Complete assessment data requirements

learning.reason: A migration asset inventory must include application-to-infrastructure mappings, dependencies, and application owners, not just a list of equipment.
learning.concept: Unlike an MRA, which assesses organizational readiness, this is about tracking the configuration and responsibility for the migration portfolio.

sourceLabel: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Complete assessment data requirements

category: クラウドの概念
title: Make cloud costs visible to departments
prompt: The FinOps team wants each business unit to see its own cloud usage costs so it can review its budget and design. However, it is not yet introducing a process that actually charges costs between departments for accounting purposes. Which initiative is most appropriate?

choices.text: Implement chargeback and automatically finalize interdepartmental accounting charges
choices.explanation: Chargeback actually bills or allocates costs, which goes beyond the visibility-only requirement here.

choices.text: Use showback to report costs attributable to each department, product, or team based on tags and similar information
choices.explanation: Correct. Showback makes cloud costs visible and reports them by the responsible entity that incurred them.

choices.text: Consolidate all costs into a single central IT expense line and do not display usage by department
choices.explanation: This does not meet the goal of helping each department understand and act on its usage costs.

choices.text: Increase service quotas and only raise the limits on available resources
choices.explanation: Quotas govern available usage limits; they are separate from cost attribution and visibility.

source.label: Guidance for Cloud Financial Management on AWS

learning.reason: Showback reports cloud costs to responsible entities such as teams or business units. It differs from chargeback, which involves actual billing.
learning.concept: Cost visibility, accounting charges, and cost allocation configuration are related, but they serve different purposes and have different implementation responsibilities.

sourceLabel: Guidance for Cloud Financial Management on AWS

category: クラウドの概念
title: Deploy your own application to a managed runtime with PaaS
prompt: A development team continues to write code for its own application to meet its requirements. The team leaves day-to-day management of the operating system and application runtime platform to the service provider, and is responsible for deploying the application and developing its features. Which service model is this?

choices.text: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service)
choices.explanation: This model provides infrastructure such as virtual machines, but users generally manage the operating system and application runtime environment.

choices.text: SaaS (Software as a Service)
choices.explanation: Users consume finished software provided by the service provider. This is not a runtime environment for deploying their own code.

choices.text: PaaS (Platform as a Service)
choices.explanation: This model lets users focus on developing and deploying applications while leaving management of the underlying infrastructure and runtime environment to the service provider.

choices.text: On-premises operations only
choices.explanation: The organization manages the equipment and runtime environment, so this does not meet the requirement to leave runtime platform operations to the provider.

source.label: PaaSで自社のアプリをマネージド実行環境へ配備する

learning.reason: PaaS is a cloud service model in which users deploy applications they develop while reducing their infrastructure management responsibilities.
learning.concept: Distinguish the service scope by whether users consume a finished product, deploy their own application, or manage the operating system.

sourceLabel: Deploy your own application to a managed runtime with PaaS

category: クラウドの概念
title: Set recovery objectives according to business impact
prompt: Even a brief outage of order intake would have a major impact on revenue and customer trust. By contrast, restoring an internal monthly report by the next business day is acceptable. What is the most appropriate approach before deciding on recovery designs?

choices.text: Set the same most stringent recovery objectives for every system
choices.explanation: Applying overly stringent objectives to workloads with different business impacts creates unnecessary complexity and cost.

choices.text: Set the same least stringent recovery objectives for every system
choices.explanation: This would fail to meet the needs of high-impact workloads such as order intake.

choices.text: Have only the technical team choose common objectives without consulting business teams
choices.explanation: Business and technical stakeholders should agree on recovery objectives based on business impact, contracts, regulations, and dependencies.

choices.text: Create tiers based on business impact and assign each workload appropriate recovery objectives
choices.explanation: Correct. Classify workloads according to the impact of outages or data loss, then set recovery objectives appropriate to each tier.

source.label: AWS Well-Architected Reliability: Define recovery objectives

learning.reason: Recovery objectives should be based on the business impact of outages and data loss rather than assigning the same values to every system.
learning.concept: Tiers of criticality help direct recovery capabilities where they are needed and avoid overdesigning or under-protecting workloads.

sourceLabel: AWS Well-Architected Reliability: Define recovery objectives

category: クラウドの概念
title: Check availability through the public access path when no users are online
prompt: The application site has very few users at night. Error alarms based only on real usage do not reveal nighttime problems, and someone may not notice an issue until opening the application form the next morning. How can you regularly verify, even when no users are online, that the path to opening the page is working?

choices.text: Regularly run a non-destructive check from outside the application, following the same path as a user.
choices.explanation: This lets you observe behavior from name resolution through page display even when there are no real users.

choices.text: Check only the server’s average CPU utilization overnight.
choices.explanation: This shows resource utilization, but does not verify that an external user can open the page.

choices.text: Disable the application’s error logs at night and stop monitoring notifications until morning.
choices.explanation: This does not verify availability during periods when there are few user requests.

choices.text: Use measurements from successful daytime requests as the result for tonight’s operation.
choices.explanation: A page that worked in the past does not show whether a problem occurred overnight.

source.label: 利用者がいない時間帯も公開経路から利用可能性を確かめる

learning.reason: Synthetic monitoring periodically performs non-destructive checks that simulate a user, so it can assess whether an application is usable even when there is no real traffic.
learning.concept: In addition to monitoring based on actual usage, you can validate the user access path when no one is using the application.

sourceLabel: Check availability through the public access path when no users are online

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Create a team-specific entry point to a shared S3 bucket, limited to a VPC
prompt: A shared S3 bucket contains data for multiple teams. For one team, you need an entry point with a dedicated access name and policy, and access through that entry point must be limited to a specified VPC. You want to preserve the existing entry point for another team. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Replace the bucket policy for all users with one for the target team.
choices.explanation: This affects the entire bucket and does not add a dedicated name and policy while preserving the other teams’ existing access paths.

choices.text: Create an S3 access point for the target team that is limited to the specified VPC.
choices.explanation: An access point can provide a team-specific name and policy, and access can be restricted to the associated VPC.

choices.text: Add only a route from the VPC to S3.
choices.explanation: Making S3 reachable from a VPC does not, by itself, add a team-specific access name or policy for the bucket.

choices.text: Only enable S3 Block Public Access.
choices.explanation: This prevents public access to S3, but does not configure the access point’s name or VPC restriction.

source.label: VPCに限定されたAmazon S3アクセスポイント

learning.reason: Each S3 access point can have its own name and access point policy, and its network origin can be limited to a specified VPC.
learning.concept: Distinguish the VPC connection path from a separately managed entry point to a shared bucket.

sourceLabel: Amazon S3 access points limited to a VPC

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Use a separate AWS WAF scope for CloudFront
prompt: A company uses AWS WAF and already has a regional Web ACL configured for an ALB in the Tokyo Region. The company now wants to apply AWS WAF protection directly to requests received by a CloudFront distribution. Which scope should the Web ACL have?

choices.text: Associate the existing Web ACL for the Tokyo Region with CloudFront as is.
choices.explanation: That Web ACL is for regional resources and does not have the global scope for CloudFront.

choices.text: Create only a regional Web ACL for each origin, based on the origin’s location used by CloudFront.
choices.explanation: Protection in an origin’s Region can be configured separately, but that does not create a Web ACL applied directly to the distribution.

choices.text: Add the Tokyo regional Web ACL to the Route 53 hosted zone referenced by CloudFront.
choices.explanation: DNS provides name resolution for the distribution, but it is not a resource to which AWS WAF associates a Web ACL.

choices.text: Create a Web ACL with the global scope for CloudFront and associate it with the distribution.
choices.explanation: This applies the Web ACL rules directly to web requests handled by CloudFront.

source.label: AWS WAFの保護対象リソースのスコープ

learning.reason: An AWS WAF Web ACL applied directly to CloudFront uses the global scope for CloudFront.
learning.concept: A CloudFront distribution and a regional load balancer have different Web ACL scopes.

sourceLabel: Scope of resources protected by AWS WAF

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Update a dependency included in a Lambda package
prompt: An application uses a Lambda managed runtime and includes a third-party library in the function’s ZIP package. The library’s publisher has released a secure version that fixes the issue. Apart from AWS’s runtime management, what should the application operator do?

choices.text: Include the fixed library in the package and redeploy the function after validation.
choices.explanation: The application team is responsible for updating dependencies included as part of the application.

choices.text: Wait, because an AWS runtime update will also replace the contents of the ZIP package.
choices.explanation: Updating a managed runtime does not cause AWS to automatically rewrite a customer’s deployed package.

choices.text: Increase the Lambda function’s memory allocation and leave the package contents unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing the memory allocation does not fix a vulnerability in an included dependency.

choices.text: Give the function additional IAM permissions and continue using the current library.
choices.explanation: Changing AWS operation permissions does not update the library in use.

source.label: Lambdaランタイム管理の責任共有

learning.reason: Even when using a managed runtime, the application operator is responsible for updating dependency libraries included in the application package.
learning.concept: Distinguish the execution environment and managed runtime maintained by AWS from application dependencies supplied by the customer.

sourceLabel: Shared responsibility for Lambda runtime management

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Restrict access to materials classified as shareable in the same bucket
prompt: Internal materials are stored in a single S3 bucket under the same prefix, and the materials have classification tags. A business role must be able to retrieve only materials classified by an existing tag as shareable externally. What should be used as the condition when adding the permission?

choices.text: Add a shared cost center tag to the bucket.
choices.explanation: This can support billing analysis, but it does not distinguish business classifications attached to individual objects.

choices.text: Allow only the prefix shared by all the target objects.
choices.explanation: This narrows the storage location, but does not distinguish classification tags among objects under the same prefix.

choices.text: Evaluate the value of the classification tag already attached to the target object in the policy condition that grants retrieval.
choices.explanation: Only objects with the specified tag value can be included in this permission.

choices.text: Export an object inventory to S3 Inventory.
choices.explanation: This supports asset inventory, but does not restrict access when a request is processed.

source.label: Amazon S3のタグとアクセス制御ポリシー

learning.reason: For the retrieval operation, a policy conditioned on existing object tags can restrict which objects are readable.
learning.concept: Using tags for AWS cost management and using tags as per-resource authorization conditions serve different purposes.

sourceLabel: Amazon S3 Tags and Access Control Policies

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Centrally review the contents of maintenance sessions
prompt: An administrator maintains EC2 instances using the standard interactive shell in Systems Manager Session Manager. In addition to the time a session starts, the administrator wants the session input and output sent to a designated destination. Which feature is appropriate?

choices.text: Record only CloudTrail management events for StartSession.
choices.explanation: The session-start API operation can be reviewed, but shell input and output are not included in this event record.

choices.text: Enable a destination for session logs in Session Manager settings.
choices.explanation: Logs from supported standard sessions can be sent to the specified destination, subject to the permissions and retention policies.

choices.text: Collect a list of installed applications with Systems Manager Inventory.
choices.explanation: This provides server asset information, but does not record activity during an interactive session.

choices.text: Collect instance network traffic records with VPC Flow Logs.
choices.explanation: This can record information such as traffic sources and destinations, but not interactive shell input and output.

source.label: AWS Systems Managerのセッションログ

learning.reason: Session Manager can send input and output from supported sessions to CloudWatch Logs or S3 according to the session settings.
learning.concept: A management API record showing that a session started is different from a record of the input and output during the interactive session.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Audit AWS API activity across an organization in a central trail
prompt: An audit team wants management events from current and future members of AWS Organizations delivered to a central S3 bucket through a shared organizational configuration. The team does not want administrators in member accounts to be able to delete the shared trail individually. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Create a single-account, multi-Region trail only in the management account.
choices.explanation: It records applicable Regions for that account, but does not include other member accounts in the trail's scope.

choices.text: Configure a CloudTrail organization trail.
choices.explanation: It can apply the trail to each account in the organization, and members cannot modify or delete the organization trail.

choices.text: Refer to each member's Event history page individually.
choices.explanation: Recent management events can be viewed account by account, but this does not provide a shared organizational configuration that automatically collects records centrally.

choices.text: Create only an AWS Config aggregator.
choices.explanation: It can aggregate configuration and compliance information, but does not deliver AWS API management events as an organization trail.

learning.reason: An organization trail applies to the management account and members in the organization, and can include members that join later.
learning.concept: Distinguish the scope of a multi-Region trail in one account from the scope of a trail covering an entire organization.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: View AWS Config configuration and compliance across multiple accounts
prompt: AWS Config records resources and evaluates rules across multiple AWS accounts and Regions. In an audit account, you want to view resource configuration details and rule compliance in one place. The rules and records do not need to be moved to the audit account. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Use Security Hub CSPM to aggregate findings across Regions.
choices.explanation: It can aggregate security findings, but it is not a way to view AWS Config configuration items and rule compliance.

choices.text: Select continuous recording in AWS Config in the audit account only.
choices.explanation: This sets the recording frequency, but does not by itself make records from other accounts visible.

choices.text: Deliver an organization CloudTrail trail to a central location.
choices.explanation: This supports auditing activity history, but does not aggregate configuration items or compliance evaluations recorded by Config.

choices.text: Configure the target accounts and Regions in an AWS Config aggregator.
choices.explanation: Configuration information and compliance status aggregated from the targets can be viewed in the audit account.

learning.reason: An AWS Config aggregator is a resource for viewing configuration and compliance information aggregated from selected sources.
learning.concept: Choose based on the type of information being aggregated: security findings, API events, or resource configuration.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Identify the version of a secret that was current immediately before rotation
prompt: Secrets Manager rotation has completed successfully. An auditor wants to review the version list without exposing secret values and identify the version that was current immediately before the current one. After a successful rotation, when the standard labels are in place, which label should they check?

choices.text: AWSPREVIOUS
choices.explanation: This label identifies the version that was current immediately before the current version.

choices.text: AWSCURRENT
choices.explanation: After successful rotation, this label identifies the current version, not the one before it.

choices.text: AWSPENDING
choices.explanation: This label is used to manage a new version during rotation. It does not identify the version that was current immediately before the current one.

choices.text: List only the VersionId values as strings and choose the second value in lexicographic order.
choices.explanation: The lexicographic order of version IDs does not indicate which version was current earlier.

learning.reason: Secrets Manager uses staging labels such as AWSCURRENT and AWSPREVIOUS, which identifies the version that was current immediately before the current one.
learning.concept: A version ID identifies a version; a staging label indicates the version's current role.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Check whether a new AWS service is in scope for an audit program
prompt: An organization is designing a new service. Early in the design review, it wants to find out whether AWS lists a candidate AWS service as in scope for a specific compliance program. Before obtaining audit evidence for its own application, which resource should it consult first?

choices.text: Consult only the overview of the AWS Shared Responsibility Model.
choices.explanation: It explains the general division of responsibilities, but does not list whether individual AWS services are in scope for a specific program.

choices.text: Estimate the service's usage charges with the AWS Pricing Calculator.
choices.explanation: This can estimate the candidate service's cost, but cannot determine whether it is in scope for an audit program.

choices.text: Check the AWS Services in Scope list for the relevant program.
choices.explanation: This list shows the services AWS identifies as in scope, along with supplemental information. The details of the applicable scope can be checked separately as needed.

choices.text: Check that GuardDuty has no findings in an existing account.
choices.explanation: The absence of findings does not prove that a service is listed as in scope for a specific audit.

source.label: 新しく使うAWSサービスが監査プログラムの範囲か確認する

learning.reason: AWS provides resources for checking in-scope services for each audit or certification program.
learning.concept: Check AWS's list of in-scope services separately from assessing compliance in your own environment and gathering evidence for a specific audit.

sourceLabel: Check whether a new AWS service is in scope for an audit program

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Set a resource-side permissions ceiling that also applies to external principals
prompt: A company manages applicable S3 resources with AWS Organizations. AWS principals outside the organization might also access them. The company wants to set an organizational policy ceiling on the resource side for the target OU so that resource policies in member accounts do not grant excessive access to external principals. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Use only a service control policy (SCP).
choices.explanation: An SCP sets a permissions ceiling on IAM principals in the targeted accounts; it does not meet the requirement for a resource-side ceiling that also applies to principals outside the organization.

choices.text: Add the external principals to an IAM user group.
choices.explanation: IAM user groups help grant permissions collectively to IAM users in the same account; they do not restrict access to the target resources at the organization level.

choices.text: Record the policy's state with an AWS Config rule.
choices.explanation: This can check configuration, but recording it does not enforce a ceiling on the access that can be allowed.

choices.text: Apply a resource control policy (RCP) to the target OU or another appropriate organizational scope.
choices.explanation: An RCP limits the maximum permissions that can be granted to applicable resources in the organization, and it is effective for external principals accessing those resources.

learning.reason: An RCP sets a permissions ceiling for requests to applicable resources. An RCP does not grant access by itself.
learning.concept: The ceiling on what a principal can access differs from the ceiling on which principals a resource can allow to access it.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Require MFA verification in the session for sensitive AWS operations
prompt: In a standalone AWS account, a company adds permission for a specific IAM user to perform sensitive operations. The user can obtain a corresponding temporary session, and this permission is not granted separately. Which policy condition should it use to limit the permission to sessions in which MFA can be verified?

choices.text: Use only the IAM user's name as the condition.
choices.explanation: This identifies the user, but does not determine whether MFA was used for the session.

choices.text: Check for MFA using the request context key that indicates whether MFA is present (aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent).
choices.explanation: This evaluates the context of the applicable temporary session so the permission can be limited to requests for which MFA is verified.

choices.text: Use only the fact that an AWS CloudTrail trail is enabled as the condition.
choices.explanation: This supports auditing operations, but does not verify MFA at the point when permission is evaluated.

choices.text: Require long-term use of an AWS access key for the same IAM user.
choices.explanation: Having long-term credentials is not the same as using a temporary session authenticated with MFA.

learning.reason: For requests using applicable temporary credentials, a policy can use MFA information as a condition to limit its permissions.
learning.concept: Registering an MFA device and verifying MFA for a particular request are different conditions.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Detecting a spike in management API activity against normal patterns
prompt: An operator records management events with CloudTrail. When calls to management APIs under audit spike above normal levels, the operator wants to use CloudTrail's analysis as a starting point for investigation instead of reviewing ordinary event history one event at a time. Which feature should be used?

choices.text: Sort events only in the CloudTrail Event history console.
choices.explanation: This lets you view individual events, but it does not automatically analyze anomalies against normal patterns.

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation.
choices.explanation: This can validate whether delivered data has been changed, but it does not analyze the frequency of management API calls.

choices.text: Enable API call rate analysis with CloudTrail Insights.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail Insights uses normal call rates as a baseline and lets you review activity identified as anomalous as Insights events.

choices.text: Use AWS Config to record AWS resource configurations after changes.
choices.explanation: You can review configuration changes, but this does not compare individual management API call rates with a baseline.

learning.reason: CloudTrail Insights can help investigate anomalies in the call rates or error rates of supported events.
learning.concept: Collecting activity logs, validating file integrity, and analyzing usage patterns serve different purposes.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Recording resource configurations that change repeatedly over short periods
prompt: A team investigates the configurations of AWS Config-supported resources. A setting may be changed and then reverted several times in a single day, and the intermediate states must also be recorded as configuration items. What recording frequency should the team configure?

choices.text: Continuous recording in AWS Config
choices.explanation: This records configuration items for supported resources when changes occur.

choices.text: Daily recording in AWS Config
choices.explanation: This captures the latest supported configuration for a period every 24 hours; it does not record every intermediate state.

choices.text: Shorten only the AWS Config snapshot delivery time.
choices.explanation: Configuration data delivery can be adjusted, but the recording frequency itself must be changed to continuous recording.

choices.text: Configure only an AWS Config aggregator.
choices.explanation: An aggregator centralizes a view of resources that are already being recorded, but it does not change the source recording frequency.

learning.reason: To track intermediate states, use continuous recording to capture configuration changes for supported resources.
learning.concept: Distinguish when data is recorded from when and where recorded data is delivered.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Creating a permissions proposal based on recorded AWS activity
prompt: An application's IAM role has broad permissions. The team has recorded representative operations over a period with CloudTrail and wants to create a policy proposal based on the AWS actions actually recorded, as a starting point for a least-privilege review. Which feature should the team choose?

choices.text: External access analysis in IAM Access Analyzer
choices.explanation: This evaluates external sharing of resources, but it does not generate an IAM policy proposal from a role's activity history.

choices.text: Validate the syntax of an existing IAM policy
choices.explanation: This is used when a policy already exists; it does not prepare a policy from activity history.

choices.text: Use the IAM policy simulator to test candidate actions.
choices.explanation: This can check whether specified actions are allowed, but it does not create a permissions proposal based on CloudTrail records.

choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer policy generation for the target role.
choices.explanation: This uses CloudTrail activity from a specified period to propose permissions aligned with the observed actions.

source.label: 実際のAWS操作の履歴から絞り込んだ権限案を作る

learning.reason: IAM Access Analyzer can evaluate CloudTrail access activity and generate a permissions policy proposal. Review it before applying, including for operations that are used infrequently.
learning.concept: Generating a proposal from performed actions is different from checking an existing policy's syntax or authorization effects.

sourceLabel: Creating a permissions proposal based on recorded AWS activity

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Analyzing S3 HTTP response processing time from access logs
prompt: A team is investigating download latency in an S3 bucket that is not intended for public access. In addition to records of calls to retrieval APIs, the team wants to examine information from S3 access logs, such as the time between when S3 receives an HTTP request and when it sends a response. Which feature should the team use?

choices.text: Use only CloudTrail S3 data events.
choices.explanation: These can be used to audit object API operations, but this scenario calls for the processing-time fields in S3 access logs.

choices.text: Configure S3 server access logging.
choices.explanation: In addition to bucket request details, the log records include information such as the total time, which can be used for analysis.

choices.text: Add object size as a column in S3 Inventory.
choices.explanation: This provides an inventory of stored objects but does not record processing time for each request.

choices.text: Use S3 Storage Lens only to review storage capacity aggregates.
choices.explanation: This provides storage usage aggregates but not logs of processing time for each HTTP response.

learning.reason: S3 server access logs contain detailed request and processing information. Delivery is best effort.
learning.concept: Distinguish API events used for auditing from service operations analysis based on request details.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Determine the scope of EBS encryption by default
prompt: A company enabled EBS encryption by default in the Tokyo Region of one AWS account. It has not enabled it in other Regions in the same account. Choose two statements that are true for this configuration.

choices.text: New EBS volumes created in that Region are encrypted even if encryption is not specified.
choices.explanation: Encryption by default applies to new EBS volumes in the account and Region where it is enabled.

choices.text: Enabling the setting immediately encrypts existing unencrypted EBS volumes in that Region.
choices.explanation: Enabling the setting does not retroactively change the configuration of volumes that already exist.

choices.text: To apply the setting in other Regions, enable it separately in each of those Regions.
choices.explanation: Encryption by default is a Region-level setting.

choices.text: The same setting is automatically applied to EBS volumes in other AWS accounts that belong to the same OU.
choices.explanation: The setting is configured per account; membership in the same OU does not automatically apply the same value.

choices.text: When this setting is enabled, data sent over the network by applications on EC2 is also always encrypted.
choices.explanation: This setting encrypts data at rest in volumes; it does not determine whether application network traffic is encrypted.

learning.reason: Enable EBS encryption by default separately for each account and Region. It applies to new eligible resources and does not automatically change existing volumes.
learning.concept: Distinguish the scope of a default setting from the separate steps needed to protect existing data or network traffic.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Monitor the security of workloads running on EKS
prompt: The operations team scans the images it builds for vulnerabilities. It also wants to receive findings about potential threats based on activity involving processes, files, and other aspects of running containers in supported Amazon EKS environments. Which capability fits this requirement?

choices.text: Amazon GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring
choices.explanation: It can analyze runtime events from supported workloads and provide findings about suspicious activity.

choices.text: Basic scanning of ECR images
choices.explanation: It assesses software vulnerabilities in stored images. It does not observe activity inside running containers.

choices.text: Record only AWS CloudTrail management events.
choices.explanation: This records AWS management API operations, but does not collect runtime events inside containers.

choices.text: Store only the configuration history of EKS resources in AWS Config.
choices.explanation: This lets you review configuration changes, but does not analyze the behavior of running processes.

learning.reason: GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring uses runtime activity from supported workloads, including EKS, for threat detection.
learning.concept: Distinguish software vulnerability scanning, configuration auditing of AWS resources, and monitoring behavior at runtime.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Allow database connections only from application EC2 instances that scale dynamically
prompt: An application EC2 instance and a PostgreSQL database are in the same VPC. Any EC2 instance added or replaced for the application also uses the application security group. How can you allow connections on the required database port only from EC2 instances that belong to this group, without entering each IP address manually?

choices.text: Specify the entire application subnet as the source in the database's inbound rule.
choices.explanation: This reduces IP management, but also includes other resources in the same subnet.

choices.text: List the individual IP addresses of currently running EC2 instances in the database's inbound rule.
choices.explanation: This narrows the allowed sources, but you must add or remove IP addresses as instances scale or are replaced.

choices.text: Specify the application security group as the source for the required inbound database port.
choices.explanation: You can allow traffic from resources associated with that group in the same VPC, and the rule follows changes in the number of instances.

choices.text: Specify the application security group only in the database's outbound rule.
choices.explanation: This does not configure the database inbound rule needed to allow connections from the application to the database.

learning.reason: A rule that references a security group as its source can allow traffic from resources associated with that group.
learning.concept: Distinguish allowing traffic by IP address range from allowing it by referencing a group of resources that can change over time.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Manage patch approval rules separately from installation times
prompt: The operations team uses Systems Manager Patch Manager to approve Windows security updates that AWS treats as critical after a set period from publication. The maintenance window for installation is set separately. Where should the team configure the patch classifications and the number of days before approval?

choices.text: Set the day of the week when a maintenance window runs.
choices.explanation: This determines when to start the operation, but not which patches to approve.

choices.text: Configure the approval rules in a custom patch baseline.
choices.explanation: For classifications supported by the target OS, the team can specify conditions such as classification and severity, along with the delay between availability and approval.

choices.text: Change the collection frequency for Systems Manager Inventory.
choices.explanation: This changes how often inventory data is collected, but not the patch approval conditions.

choices.text: Save maintenance logs for Session Manager.
choices.explanation: This can help document work, but does not configure the criteria for approving patches.

source.label: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager baselines

learning.reason: A patch baseline with approval rules specifies which updates are eligible for approval and when.
learning.concept: The controls for deciding which patches to apply differ from the controls for scheduling when installation starts.

sourceLabel: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager baselines

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Reuse a shared library across multiple Lambda functions
prompt: Several Lambda functions in the same Region use ZIP packages and need the same dependency library. Which approach lets you manage the library as a single versioned package that the functions can reference?

choices.text: Copy the same library separately into every function's ZIP package.
choices.explanation: Each function can use the library, but it is stored separately in each ZIP rather than referenced as one versioned package.

choices.text: Store the shared library contents as Lambda environment variable values.
choices.explanation: Environment variables pass configuration values; they do not unpack dependency packages into the runtime.

choices.text: Publish the library as a Lambda layer and associate the relevant version with each function.
choices.explanation: The shared package can be versioned and referenced by the functions that use it.

choices.text: Add only the URL where the library is stored to the IAM execution role.
choices.explanation: An execution role grants permissions; it does not add a library to the function's runtime environment.

learning.reason: A Lambda layer packages libraries and other dependencies separately, and a specific layer version can be associated with multiple functions.
learning.concept: Deploying each function's code is distinct from letting multiple functions reference dependencies in a shared package.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Notify only when both alarms are in the alarm state
prompt: A web service uses separate CloudWatch metric alarms to track its error rate and latency. Keep their individual states, and notify the on-call team only when both are in the alarm state. Which CloudWatch feature is suitable for these notifications?

choices.text: Create a composite alarm that combines the two alarm states with an AND condition.
choices.explanation: The composite alarm can trigger its configured notification only when both conditions are met.

choices.text: Connect both existing alarms individually to the same SNS notification target.
choices.explanation: Either alarm will send a notification as soon as it enters the alarm state, without waiting for the other.

choices.text: Display both metrics on the same graph in a dashboard.
choices.explanation: A person can inspect both metrics, but this does not automatically set a notification condition across multiple alarms.

choices.text: Enable anomaly detection on the error-rate alarm alone.
choices.explanation: This can identify unusual error-rate values, but it does not logically combine the states of the two existing alarms.

learning.reason: A composite alarm applies logical conditions to existing alarm states and can notify when the specified conditions are met.
learning.concept: An alarm built from metric data is different from one that combines the states of existing alarms.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Deliver only a business application to employees' browsers
prompt: A company wants employees to use an existing Windows application for design work from several types of devices. The application must be usable in a supported browser without installing its executable files on user devices or assigning each user a dedicated desktop. Which service is suitable?

choices.text: Assign each user a dedicated desktop with Amazon WorkSpaces Personal.
choices.explanation: Users can work from a dedicated desktop with the business application, but this scenario calls for delivering the application without assigning a desktop.

choices.text: Deliver the business application with Amazon WorkSpaces Applications.
choices.explanation: The application runs in the cloud and can be used in a supported browser.

choices.text: Open existing business websites with Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser.
choices.explanation: This service can provide access to web applications, but it does not run and deliver an existing Windows executable from the cloud.

choices.text: Place the Windows application's files on a website with AWS Amplify Hosting.
choices.explanation: It can host files for publication, but it does not run the application on a server and make its interface interactive.

learning.reason: Amazon WorkSpaces Applications (formerly Amazon AppStream 2.0) runs applications in the cloud and can stream their interfaces to supported clients.
learning.concept: Accessing a website, delivering a whole desktop, and delivering an individual application running in the cloud serve different needs.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Apply a correction before the cached copy expires at the existing URL
prompt: A company corrects an informational PDF delivered through CloudFront and has updated the content at the origin under the same file name. The URL already shared externally must remain unchanged. Treat browser caching separately. Which method removes the old copy from CloudFront before its existing TTL expires?

choices.text: Overwrite the file at the origin under the same key again.
choices.explanation: This updates the content at the origin, but does not by itself immediately remove the old copy retained by CloudFront.

choices.text: Rename the file and distribute a new URL to users.
choices.explanation: A different URL avoids the old cache, but does not meet the requirement to keep the URL already shared.

choices.text: Wait for the current cache to expire under its existing TTL.
choices.explanation: The content can be fetched again after expiration, but waiting does not remove the old copy before then.

choices.text: Create a CloudFront invalidation for the path.
choices.explanation: Once the invalidation propagates, the old CloudFront cache is discarded and subsequent requests use the content from the origin.

learning.reason: When an invalidation for a path propagates, CloudFront removes the old edge-cached content so that a later request can retrieve the content from the origin.
learning.concept: Using a URL for a new version and explicitly invalidating the CloudFront cache for the same URL are different approaches.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Run an approved inspection across multiple servers and review the results
prompt: An operations team wants to run an approved, read-only inspection once across a fleet of managed EC2 instances. The team must be able to target the instances without connecting to each server interactively and review the results together. Which Systems Manager feature is appropriate?

choices.text: Open individual interactive sessions with Systems Manager Session Manager.
choices.explanation: This provides access to individual servers, but it does not meet the requirement to run an operation across the fleet at once.

choices.text: Use only the scheduled collection in Systems Manager Inventory.
choices.explanation: This can collect standard inventory information, but this configuration alone does not run an arbitrary specified inspection across the fleet once.

choices.text: Select the targets and run an inspection document with Systems Manager Run Command.
choices.explanation: Run Command sends an operation to the specified managed nodes, and you can review the results for each node.

choices.text: Register the inspection's name in Systems Manager Parameter Store.
choices.explanation: Parameter Store can store configuration values, but registering a name does not automatically run the corresponding operation.

learning.reason: Run Command runs an approved command document non-interactively on targeted managed nodes and lets you review the execution results.
learning.concept: Systems Manager features serve different purposes: opening an individual session is different from sending an operation to multiple nodes and collecting the results.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Distinguish an RDS single standby from read scaling
prompt: A company runs a single RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. It does not need to distribute read traffic, but it wants RDS to automatically switch roles to a standby in a different Availability Zone if the primary fails. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Add only an RDS read replica and have the application connect only to the original instance.
choices.explanation: A read replica can be used for reads or promotion, but this configuration alone does not provide the same automatic failover as a single-standby Multi-AZ deployment.

choices.text: Use an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment with a single standby.
choices.explanation: A standby is maintained in a different Availability Zone, and RDS automatically switches roles if a failure occurs.

choices.text: Use a single-AZ DB and increase the backup retention period.
choices.explanation: This changes how long backups can be restored from, but does not provide an automatic switch to a standby DB in another Availability Zone.

choices.text: Increase the DB instance size and keep it in a single-AZ deployment.
choices.explanation: This can provide more resources, but it does not provide a standby in another Availability Zone.

source.label: Amazon RDSの単一スタンバイを含むMulti-AZ配置

learning.reason: An RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment with a single standby maintains a synchronous standby in a different Availability Zone and can fail over automatically if a failure occurs.
learning.concept: RDS uses a single standby for availability; read scaling uses a different approach.

sourceLabel: Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployment with a single standby

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Create a route-table path to S3 without using NAT
prompt: An EC2 instance in a private subnet uses S3 in the same Region. Which type of VPC endpoint adds a route for traffic to S3 to the subnet's route table without using an internet gateway or NAT gateway for the connection?

choices.text: An S3 interface VPC endpoint
choices.explanation: It provides private connectivity to S3, but it uses ENIs and does not add the endpoint route to S3.

choices.text: S3 Transfer Acceleration
choices.explanation: This feature optimizes the path between a user’s device and S3; it does not create a route to S3 in a VPC route table.

choices.text: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint
choices.explanation: When you associate it with the relevant route table, traffic to S3 can use a route that targets the endpoint.

choices.text: A default route through an AWS NAT Gateway
choices.explanation: This can be used for outbound connectivity, but the route in this scenario must not pass through NAT.

learning.reason: A gateway endpoint adds a route in the selected route table to the S3 prefix list.
learning.concept: Private connectivity to S3 can use either an endpoint with ENIs or a gateway endpoint that uses a route to the service.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Set an expiration period for old CloudWatch Logs events by log group
prompt: An application continuously sends logs to a CloudWatch Logs log group. The operations policy allows searching only the most recent 90 days and makes log events past their expiration eligible for automatic deletion. Which setting accomplishes this without adding a destination?

choices.text: Include the year, month, and day in the log stream names.
choices.explanation: This can help organize logs, but the names do not determine when log events are deleted.

choices.text: Set the retention period of the target log group to 90 days.
choices.explanation: Setting a retention period makes log events past that period eligible for deletion by CloudWatch Logs.

choices.text: Change the evaluation period of a metric alarm that specifies the log group.
choices.explanation: This changes the range used to evaluate the alarm condition, but it does not set an expiration period for the original log events.

choices.text: Set only an S3 bucket lifecycle rule.
choices.explanation: The rule applies to S3 objects but does not change the retention period for log events in CloudWatch Logs.

learning.reason: CloudWatch Logs retention policies are set at the log group level.
learning.concept: Distinguish an alarm's evaluation period from the retention period for the underlying log data.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Run a task at the local time despite daylight saving changes
prompt: Invoke a Lambda function to send team notifications at 9:00 a.m. New York local time, Monday through Friday. The application does not convert the time to UTC, and the schedule must remain at 9:00 a.m. local time after daylight saving time changes. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Configure a legacy EventBridge scheduled rule at a fixed UTC time.
choices.explanation: A fixed UTC time corresponds to different local times during daylight saving time and standard time.

choices.text: Match only the business event type on an EventBridge event bus.
choices.explanation: This can route events based on their content, but it does not invoke a function periodically according to local time.

choices.text: Create a schedule at 24-hour intervals in UTC and align only its initial start time with local time.
choices.explanation: This uses a fixed elapsed-time interval, so it does not necessarily run at the same local clock time after daylight saving time changes.

choices.text: Specify the regional time zone and local Monday-through-Friday time in EventBridge Scheduler.
choices.explanation: Cron invocation times with a supported time zone account for daylight saving time.

learning.reason: Cron-based EventBridge Scheduler schedules are evaluated in the specified time zone.
learning.concept: A schedule based on a fixed elapsed-time interval differs from one that follows a local calendar time.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Understand which state EC2 hibernation preserves while an instance is stopped
prompt: A development team needs to pause a long-running test application on a supported EC2 instance until the next day. The instance is already configured with an encrypted root EBS volume of sufficient capacity and to support hibernation. Choose two statements that correctly describe EC2 hibernation.

choices.text: The contents of memory while the instance is running are saved only to the EC2 local instance store.
choices.explanation: During hibernation, memory is saved to the root EBS volume. Instance store data is temporary.

choices.text: When the instance stops, its RAM state can be saved to a supported EBS root volume.
choices.explanation: Hibernation saves the RAM contents to the encrypted root volume.

choices.text: You can terminate the EC2 instance first and then restore the memory state of that same instance.
choices.explanation: A terminated instance cannot be resumed. Hibernation stops and resumes the instance.

choices.text: Creating only a snapshot of the data EBS volume saves the same RAM state as hibernation.
choices.explanation: A snapshot of a data disk does not automatically capture memory contents.

choices.text: When the instance resumes, its preserved RAM state is restored.
choices.explanation: With a supported configuration, the saved RAM is read back so the test can resume from its pre-hibernation state.

learning.reason: Hibernation saves the memory state of a supported EC2 instance to the root EBS volume and restores it when the instance resumes.
learning.concept: Distinguish the running state preserved by hibernation from disk data preserved by an ordinary stop.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Point a custom domain’s zone apex to an ALB’s changing endpoint
prompt: A company has a public hosted zone for example.com in Amazon Route 53. It wants example.com itself, not a subdomain, to point to an Application Load Balancer. Which DNS record is appropriate if the company does not want to manage the load balancer’s numeric IP addresses as fixed values?

choices.text: Create a standard CNAME at the zone apex pointing to the ALB DNS name.
choices.explanation: You cannot configure a standard CNAME at a DNS zone apex.

choices.text: Manually enter the ALB’s currently visible IP address in a standard A record.
choices.explanation: If the address changes, it must be updated manually, which does not meet the requirement to avoid managing the ALB endpoint as a fixed value.

choices.text: Create an A-type alias record and target the supported ALB.
choices.explanation: A Route 53 alias can point the zone apex to the ALB and maintain the public name.

choices.text: Create a CNAME to the ALB only for www.example.com.
choices.explanation: This points a subdomain to the ALB but does not configure a response for the required example.com name.

learning.reason: Route 53 aliases can point to supported AWS resources, including at the zone apex.
learning.concept: Distinguish the zone-apex restriction from the method for pointing a name to a managed service endpoint.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Compare files received by S3 with their pre-upload checksums
prompt: A production team uploads large files to a private S3 bucket. It wants S3 to verify upon receipt that the data matches a checksum calculated by the application before sending it. Which method should the team use?

choices.text: Configure only S3 Transfer Acceleration.
choices.explanation: This improves long-distance transfer paths but does not specify validation against an expected value.

choices.text: Upload the file with the expected checksum using a supported method.
choices.explanation: S3 can calculate the checksum of the received data and compare it with the specified value.

choices.text: Use only a presigned URL, without specifying a checksum.
choices.explanation: This can grant upload permissions, but that configuration alone does not specify a comparison with the value calculated by the application.

choices.text: Only enable S3 Versioning.
choices.explanation: This preserves previous versions but does not compare received content against the specified checksum.

learning.reason: When a checksum is included with an upload, Amazon S3 can verify data integrity across the transfer.
learning.concept: Transfer paths, authorization to perform an operation, and data-integrity validation are separate properties.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: View telemetry from another account in the same Region
prompt: Multiple AWS accounts run services in the same Region and collect metrics, logs, and traces. Operators want to view telemetry from permitted accounts through a dedicated monitoring account without switching accounts each time. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Aggregate organization trails in AWS CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: This is suitable for auditing AWS API activity, but it does not provide a combined view of application metrics and traces.

choices.text: Specify the same email address in metric alarms in each account.
choices.explanation: This can deliver notifications, but it does not let the monitoring account view the underlying data across accounts.

choices.text: Create a new dashboard individually in each account and do nothing else.
choices.explanation: This can organize views within each account, but it does not configure telemetry sharing with the monitoring account.

choices.text: Link the source accounts to the monitoring account with CloudWatch cross-account observability.
choices.explanation: In the same Region, the monitoring account can centrally view supported telemetry from permitted source accounts.

source.label: 運用者が同じリージョンの別アカウントのテレメトリを確認する

learning.reason: CloudWatch cross-account observability works by linking the monitoring account and source accounts.
learning.concept: Sharing application observability data and aggregating audit logs of AWS management activity address different needs.

sourceLabel: View telemetry from another account in the same Region

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Repeatedly launch EC2 instances from a configured operating system image
prompt: You have installed the required operating system settings and business application on EC2. You want to launch EC2 instances repeatedly with the same initial state from an image that includes the configured boot disk. Restoring the runtime memory state is not required. What should you prepare?

choices.text: Only a snapshot of the EBS volume dedicated to application data
choices.explanation: This can reproduce the data volume, but it does not meet the requirement for a boot image containing the operating system and application.

choices.text: An Amazon Machine Image (AMI)
choices.explanation: You can create an image that includes the software configuration needed for launch, then launch EC2 instances by specifying that AMI.

choices.text: The EC2 hibernation state
choices.explanation: This resumes the same instance; it is not an image for launching multiple new EC2 instances in the same state.

choices.text: A launch configuration that uses the same instance type and a new, empty volume
choices.explanation: This can keep compute capacity consistent, but it does not reproduce the operating system settings or installed applications.

learning.reason: An AMI provides software and volume information used when launching an instance.
learning.concept: Launching new instances from an image, restoring a single disk, and resuming one stopped instance are different operations.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Aggregate stored application logs by time period
prompt: After an application outage last night, you want to count occurrences of a specific error by time period using logs already stored in CloudWatch Logs. You did not create a metric for that error in advance. Which option can provide the required result with an additional query?

choices.text: Filter the stored logs and aggregate the counts with CloudWatch Logs Insights.
choices.explanation: You can select a log group and time range, then search and aggregate the relevant logs.

choices.text: Create only a new log metric filter.
choices.explanation: It can measure logs received after it is created, but it does not retroactively create metrics from last night's stored data.

choices.text: Only extend the log group's retention period.
choices.explanation: This changes how long logs are retained, but it does not filter recorded events or calculate their count.

choices.text: Create only a CloudWatch metric alarm.
choices.explanation: An alarm evaluates existing metrics; it does not aggregate historical counts based on log content.

learning.reason: CloudWatch Logs Insights is used to search and analyze collected logs.
learning.concept: Searching historical logs after collection differs from creating metrics as logs are collected.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Detect the structure of new S3 data and register it in the Data Catalog
prompt: New CSV and Parquet data arrives in an S3 area for analytics. You want a feature that examines the supported files, infers the table and column structure without transforming the data, and registers it in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Which feature avoids entering the definitions manually each time?

choices.text: Rewrite the data in an AWS Glue ETL job.
choices.explanation: This can be used when data transformation is required, but this choice does not infer and register the structure without changing the existing data.

choices.text: Run SELECT against an existing table in Amazon Athena.
choices.explanation: This queries a table that is already registered; it is not a job for automatically discovering definitions for new data.

choices.text: Run an AWS Glue crawler on the S3 data area.
choices.explanation: It can examine the data and register or update the inferred structure as table information in the Data Catalog.

choices.text: Configure an S3 object lifecycle.
choices.explanation: This manages object storage classes and expiration, but does not discover column definitions.

learning.reason: A Glue crawler can examine a data source, infer its schema, and register it in the Glue Data Catalog.
learning.concept: The catalog stores definitions; a crawler automates their discovery.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Restore DynamoDB to a New Table at a Point Just Before an Incorrect Update
prompt: The team had enabled point-in-time recovery for a DynamoDB table in advance. An incorrect update occurred yesterday afternoon. They want to retrieve the data as it was just before that update and compare it without overwriting the production table. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Change the table's capacity mode to on-demand.
choices.explanation: This affects current read and write capacity management but does not restore historical data.

choices.text: Create an on-demand backup of the current production table and restore it as is.
choices.explanation: This can restore the current state, but it does not include the state from just before the specified incorrect update.

choices.text: Add a new Region that replicates all current data.
choices.explanation: This replicates the current table to another Region; it does not let you select and restore a past state.

choices.text: Select the target time from the PITR recovery period and restore it to a new table.
choices.explanation: This creates a separate table for the selected point in time and does not overwrite the production table's current data.

learning.reason: DynamoDB point-in-time recovery lets you select a past time within the recovery period and restore the data to a new table.
learning.concept: A current backup and an operation that restores data from a specified past point in time are different.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Determine Whether Traffic Can Be Routed Through a VPC Peering Connection
prompt: VPC A is connected to VPC B, and VPC B is connected to VPC C. Both connections use VPC peering. VPC A and VPC C have no direct connection, and no other routing feature is configured. Can this peering configuration alone route traffic from A through B to C?

choices.text: No. VPC peering does not provide transitive routing.
choices.explanation: Communication between a third pair of VPCs by chaining two separate VPC peering connections is not supported.

choices.text: Yes. If the peering between B and C is active, A can automatically use the route to C as well.
choices.explanation: Even when a peering connection is active, it only permits communication between the two VPCs in that connection.

choices.text: Yes, as long as the address ranges of A and B do not overlap, traffic can reach C through B.
choices.explanation: Non-overlapping address ranges are one of the connection requirements, but VPC peering still does not provide transitive routing.

choices.text: Yes. Add only a route from C to A to B's peering connection, and A can then communicate with C.
choices.explanation: Adding a route does not enable transit traffic that VPC peering does not support.

learning.reason: VPC peering enables communication between the two VPCs in a peering connection; it does not provide transitive routing through a peering connection to another VPC.
learning.concept: Distinguish the scope of a direct connection from the scope needed to relay traffic among multiple networks.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Configure the Required IOPS Without Changing EBS Capacity
prompt: An EBS volume attached to an EC2 instance already has enough capacity for the data. Measurements show that it cannot meet the required random I/O performance. Which general purpose SSD option lets you specify the required IOPS without increasing the volume’s capacity?

choices.text: Keep the gp2 volume at the same capacity and configure its baseline IOPS separately.
choices.explanation: With gp2, baseline performance is tied to volume capacity; it cannot be configured independently as it can with gp3.

choices.text: Use gp3 and configure the required IOPS independently of capacity, within the supported limits.
choices.explanation: With gp3, performance can be provisioned separately from volume size.

choices.text: Take EBS snapshots more frequently.
choices.explanation: This creates more recovery points but does not change the IOPS of the running volume.

choices.text: Choose a throughput optimized HDD with the same capacity and expect it to match the SSD’s random IOPS.
choices.explanation: HDDs are intended for workloads with large sequential I/O. This does not meet the requirement to use a general purpose SSD and specify random I/O performance in IOPS.

learning.reason: Amazon EBS gp3 lets you adjust IOPS and throughput independently of storage capacity, within the supported limits.
learning.concept: Capacity, operations per unit of time, and data transfer per unit of time are separate design requirements.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Create an Error Count Metric from Incoming Logs
prompt: CloudWatch Logs is receiving application logs. The team wants future incoming log events that match a specified error condition to be recorded as a time series CloudWatch metric, with an alarm notifying them if the count increases. Which combination is appropriate?

choices.text: Change only the retention period of the target log group.
choices.explanation: This changes how long logs are retained but does not record matching log events as a metric.

choices.text: Aggregate already stored logs once using Logs Insights.
choices.explanation: This can help investigate historical logs, but this operation does not continuously create a metric from incoming logs.

choices.text: Create a metric using a CloudWatch Logs metric filter, then configure an alarm for that metric.
choices.explanation: A metric filter can measure matching events in incoming logs, and an alarm can be applied to the time series count.

choices.text: Set the same threshold on an application CPU utilization metric.
choices.explanation: This monitors CPU usage but does not record the number of log events matching the error condition.

learning.reason: A metric filter can match events as they arrive in logs and generate a CloudWatch metric.
learning.concept: Distinguish analyzing historical logs from configuring continuous counting of incoming events.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Restore a specific point in time after retiring the original RDS DB instance
prompt: Keep the state of a replacement RDS DB instance immediately after a business period-end close for several months into the future. Retire the original DB instance afterward. You want to create a new DB from the saved state even after the automated backup retention period has elapsed. Which preparation is appropriate?

choices.text: Only extend the automated backup retention period and assume you can restore from it even after that period has elapsed.
choices.explanation: Restoring from automated backups is subject to a retention-period limit.

choices.text: Keep only an RDS Proxy that points to the original DB.
choices.explanation: It provides application connection management and does not save the DB state.

choices.text: Save only the original DB's configuration parameters.
choices.explanation: You could recreate the configuration, but you could not restore the business data as it stood at period-end close.

choices.text: Create a manual DB snapshot immediately after period-end close and retain it after retiring the original DB.
choices.explanation: A manual snapshot can be retained separately from the original DB and later restored to a new DB instance.

learning.reason: A manual snapshot can restore a DB instance to a specified point in time. You can retain and use the snapshot after deleting the original DB.
learning.concept: Distinguish the retention period for automated backups from how long an explicitly retained restore point can be used.

category: クラウド技術とサービス
title: Store a regenerable secondary S3 copy in a single AZ
prompt: The source data is already stored in another highly durable location. A secondary copy stored in S3 has infrequent access and can be regenerated if lost in an AZ failure. It must be retrievable without waiting for a restore, and you do not need redundancy across multiple AZs. You want to prioritize low storage charges for infrequently accessed data. Which storage class fits?

choices.text: S3 Standard-IA
choices.explanation: It supports immediate access for infrequently accessed data, but provides redundancy across multiple AZs and has higher storage charges than a single-AZ class.

choices.text: S3 One Zone-IA
choices.explanation: It stores infrequently accessed data in a single AZ and can be used for copies that can be regenerated.

choices.text: S3 Glacier Deep Archive
