choices.explanation: It is intended for long-term archiving, but a restore operation must complete before the data can be retrieved immediately.

choices.text: S3 Standard
choices.explanation: It supports immediate access, but it is not the class that prioritizes the low storage charges assumed for an infrequently accessed secondary copy.

learning.reason: S3 One Zone-IA is a storage class for infrequently accessed data stored in a single AZ.
learning.concept: Choose based on support for variable access, restore delays, and whether data can be regenerated after an AZ loss.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Distinguish discounted usage coverage from commitment utilization
prompt: The finance team has purchased Savings Plans. It wants to separately determine whether it fully used its purchased hourly commitment and what proportion of eligible AWS usage the plans covered. Select TWO correct actions.

choices.text: Use the coverage report to measure how much of the purchased commitment was used.
choices.explanation: Coverage concerns how much eligible usage received a discount. Refer to utilization to see how much of the purchased amount was used.

choices.text: Use the utilization report to see how much of the purchased commitment was used.
choices.explanation: It shows the used and unused portions of the purchased commitment.

choices.text: Use the coverage report to check whether physical instance capacity is available in a specified AZ.
choices.explanation: It reports discount coverage from Savings Plans; it does not show physical capacity available in an AZ.

choices.text: Use the achievement percentage for an AWS Budgets budget amount to calculate commitment utilization.
choices.explanation: The achievement percentage helps monitor spending, but it differs from utilization of a purchased Savings Plan.

choices.text: Use the coverage report to check what proportion of eligible usage was covered by Savings Plans.
choices.explanation: It shows eligible usage covered by the discount and the portion that remains uncovered.

source.label: Savings Plansのカバレッジレポート

learning.reason: Utilization shows how much of the purchased commitment was used, while coverage shows how much eligible usage was covered by Savings Plans discounts.
learning.concept: Even with high utilization, a substantial amount of other eligible usage may remain without a discount.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Notify before actual spending exceeds the budget
prompt: Monthly AWS usage varies by season. The finance department sets a monthly spending limit and wants a notification if the forecast through month-end exceeds that limit, even before actual spending reaches it. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Configure AWS Budgets to notify only when actual spending exceeds the limit.
choices.explanation: This notifies you after actual cumulative spending reaches the limit; it is not an early notification based on a forecast.

choices.text: Use AWS Cost Anomaly Detection to notify only about deviations from usage patterns.
choices.explanation: It can alert you to unusual spending, but it does not meet the requirement to compare a fixed monthly limit with a month-end forecast.

choices.text: Configure AWS Budgets to notify when the forecasted amount exceeds the limit.
choices.explanation: It can notify you according to the configured condition once the month-end total is forecast to exceed the threshold.

choices.text: Only display the forecast chart in AWS Cost Explorer.
choices.explanation: You can review the outlook, but this does not configure notifications to compare a limit with the forecast.

learning.reason: AWS Budgets can be configured to notify when actual or forecasted values are compared with a budget threshold.
learning.concept: Monthly cumulative actual spending, a month-end forecast that includes future usage, and deviations from usual usage patterns are different measures.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Reviewing a Marketplace contract offered to a specific buyer
prompt: A company has agreed with an AWS Marketplace seller on a price and contract term that differ from the public listing. The seller wants to present those terms to the company's account so a representative can review and accept the contract on Marketplace. Which method should they use?

choices.text: Subscribe through the public product page under the standard listing terms.
choices.explanation: The standard price and terms apply; this does not present the negotiated terms for the company's account.

choices.text: Only add the product as approved in AWS Private Marketplace.
choices.explanation: This manages which products are available, but it does not present special pricing or contract terms to the company.

choices.text: Save an estimate below the public price in AWS Pricing Calculator.
choices.explanation: Creating an estimate does not establish contract terms that can be purchased from the seller.

choices.text: Open a private offer that the seller has directed to the account.
choices.explanation: The account can review and accept the individually offered price and terms.

source.label: AWS Marketplaceのプライベートオファー

learning.reason: With a private offer, a seller can present an offer with different pricing or contract terms to a specific target account.
learning.concept: AWS Private Marketplace, which controls approved products, differs from a private offer, which presents terms negotiated directly with a buyer.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Choosing support case severity based on production impact
prompt: A company using AWS Enterprise Support has a complete outage of its production order system. Users cannot place orders, and there is no workaround. Orders are important, but the company has another core system that it treats as having an even higher severity; this is not an outage of that system. Which severity best fits the case?

choices.text: Production system down
choices.explanation: This fits a case where a critical production function is unavailable.

choices.text: Production system impaired
choices.explanation: This can fit a case where some functionality is affected but the system is still operating; it understates the impact of this complete outage.

choices.text: System impaired
choices.explanation: This is for a relatively less urgent issue and does not fit the complete outage of this production function.

choices.text: General guidance
choices.explanation: This is for questions such as how to use a product, not a situation where users cannot use a production function.

source.label: AWS Supportのケースと重要度

learning.reason: Production system down is the severity for an incident in which a critical production function is unavailable.
learning.concept: Choose severity based on user impact, available workarounds, and the business importance of the affected system, not just the technical error name.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Checking API parameters and error specifications in official documentation
prompt: An operations team is considering using an API to send metrics to CloudWatch. Before implementation, the team wants to check the types and required or optional status of the fields to send, as well as error responses, in AWS documentation. Which source is the most direct?

choices.text: Check the billing units for CloudWatch on the AWS pricing page.
choices.explanation: This provides pricing information, not the API request and response specifications.

choices.text: Read the page for the operation in the Amazon CloudWatch API Reference.
choices.explanation: It provides specifications such as required fields and parameter types for the operation.

choices.text: Read the Operational Excellence pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework.
choices.explanation: It is useful for operational principles and design guidance, but it does not define every parameter of an individual API.

choices.text: Check the list of covered services in the AWS certification exam guide.
choices.explanation: This identifies exam topics, but does not document API specifications.

source.label: Amazon CloudWatchのPutMetricData APIリファレンス

learning.reason: The operation-specific page in the AWS API Reference lists interface specifications such as request parameters, types, required conditions, and errors.
learning.concept: Use different sources for service overviews, architecture guidance, and API contracts.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Using a regional reservation discount across smaller sizes in the same family
prompt: A company has a size-flexible regional EC2 Reserved Instance for Linux/UNIX with default tenancy. It uses several smaller sizes in the same Region and instance family. If it does not exchange the reservation individually, which statement correctly describes how the discount applies?

choices.text: Only one instance with exactly the original size receives the discount.
choices.explanation: The regional reservation in this case is size-flexible and can apply to other sizes in the same family.

choices.text: All smaller instances receive the discount, regardless of how many are running.
choices.explanation: Discounted usage is limited by the normalization units of the reservation purchased.

choices.text: The discount can apply to smaller sizes in the same eligible family, up to the reservation's normalization units.
choices.explanation: Usage on other sizes in the same eligible family can receive the discount using normalization factors.

choices.text: It automatically applies to other instance families as long as they are in the same Region.
choices.explanation: Being in the same Region is not sufficient. Size flexibility applies within the same family.

source.label: リージョンリザーブドインスタンスの適用

learning.reason: The discount from an eligible regional Reserved Instance can apply across different sizes in the same family based on normalization factors.
learning.concept: Regional size flexibility depends on eligible attributes and normalized usage, not just the price or instance count.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Separate responsibility for S3 storage and data access charges
prompt: A dataset for external distribution is stored in a general purpose S3 bucket. Access is granted to external users with AWS accounts, and Requester Pays is enabled. For a standard download, which combination is responsible for the storage charge and the applicable request and data transfer charges?

choices.text: The bucket owner pays the storage charge, and the requester pays the applicable request and data transfer charges.
choices.explanation: This arrangement splits the costs between storage and the requests used to access the data.

choices.text: The requester pays the storage charge, and the owner pays the request and data transfer charges.
choices.explanation: Requester Pays shifts applicable request and transfer charges to the requester; the owner still pays for storage.

choices.text: If the requester has permission to retrieve the data, the requester pays all storage and transfer charges.
choices.explanation: Access permission does not transfer the cost of storing the data from the owner.

choices.text: The owner pays both the storage and request charges, and charges the requester only for data transfer.
choices.explanation: With Requester Pays, the requester is also responsible for applicable request charges.

learning.reason: With Requester Pays, the bucket owner pays storage charges, while the authenticated requester pays applicable request and data transfer charges.
learning.concept: Access permissions are separate from which AWS account pays for requests.

category: 請求と料金とサポート
title: Apply tags that were present before activation to cost analysis
prompt: The finance team enabled a departmental tag as a cost allocation tag for the first time at the beginning of this month. The same tag had actually been attached to the affected resources during the previous two months. The team wants the billing data for those periods to reflect the tag values that were present at the time. Which feature should they consider?

choices.text: The past bills are finalized, so they should only expand the date range in Cost Explorer.
choices.explanation: That can display past amounts, but it does not by itself apply cost allocation tags to historical data.

choices.text: Apply a tag with the same key to all resources now so that the past periods match the current value.
choices.explanation: This does not use a tag applied now as evidence of what was true in the past.

choices.text: Set a departmental budget for next month in AWS Budgets.
choices.explanation: This can monitor a future budget, but it does not add past cost allocation tag values to billing analysis.

choices.text: Request a cost allocation tag backfill for the specified period.
choices.explanation: Based on tags that were present at the time and the applicable requirements, historical cost allocation data can be updated for the specified period.

source.label: AWSコスト配分タグのバックフィル

learning.reason: A cost allocation tag backfill can update historical cost data when tags present on resources during the specified period meet the applicable requirements.
learning.concept: Applying historical tag values to cost data differs from inferring past values from current tags.
